issues.title: [Feat] diffusion/disaggregation: Add declarative stage deployments
issues.body:
## Motivation

Roles should describe where pipeline stages run, rather than require a new hardcoded role and payload for each split. This adds an experimental, opt-in stage deployment path on top of the existing generation API and Mooncake transport.

Targets `main`; the prerequisite #45309 has landed. Main has been merged, not rebased.

## Modifications

- Declare stage groups, worker endpoints, replicas, node placement, and per-role server arguments in a deployment file. Select stages by registered name or zero-based index.
- Transfer the complete request context automatically between consecutive stage groups, including nested tensors, scheduler state, and consumed RNG state. Tensor data uses the tensor transport; tracing, metrics, and model modules remain process-local.
- Retain explicit-field contracts for parallel encoder branches and fan-out/join graphs. Automatic context transfer does not infer parallel branches.
- Load only the selected role's components and construct its stages through factories. Separate standard decoder postprocessing into a stage while retaining monolithic result handling.
- Add local node launch, bounded admission/result leases, cancellation cleanup, scalar-tensor transport support, and explicit remote error propagation.
- Support directly targeted encoder pools with `EncodingClient.encode(..., role=...)`, independent checkpoint/configuration per role, and independently sized replica pools. Same-model roles preserve explicit settings while recalculating automatic defaults for their GPU count.
- Add scoped, bounded, input-ordered client prefetch. Receive copies use a dedicated CUDA stream and do not block the event loop while completing; cancellation waits for the copy before recycling the receive slot.
- Update the generic disaggregation guide, CLI reference, and model integration guidance. Add focused unit coverage and a reusable manual cross-model E2E matrix.

## Accuracy Tests

### Encoder-pool follow-up (2026-10-27)

- Linux H200, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130: **377 tests and 191 subtests passed**, including the public-checkpoint manual E2E test and the deployment/server-args/disaggregation unit suites. Required pre-commit hooks passed.
- Public-model E2E: two Z-Image Turbo text encoder replicas plus one FLUX.2 Klein 4B VAE replica. Tests exercise role-specific model loading through the node launcher, direct pool calls, combined outputs, different prompt lengths and image sizes, ordered prefetch, early exit, invalid-role recovery, and zero remaining coordinator leases/jobs. Conditioning caching is disabled in this test; repeated tensors compare with `rtol=atol=0`.
- Separately validated Mooncake RDMA tensor returns between two GPU pods on **one physical H200 host**. BF16 prompt embeddings and image latents arrived on the client GPU and matched separate/combined role calls exactly. This follow-up does not claim a new cross-physical-node test or a training-throughput improvement.
- Public docs include a mixed-checkpoint 2:1 pool deployment and scoped client examples. Encoder outputs retain each model stage's existing semantics; arbitrary hidden-layer extraction, training-specific VAE representations, cross-process autograd, and dynamic batching are not implied.

### Earlier generation validation

Validation used Linux H200 workers and independent monolithic references with matched precision, attention backend, stage parallelism, and VAE layout. Output comparisons used `rtol=atol=0`.

| Coverage | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Independent encoder / denoiser / decoder: Wan2.1-1.3B, Z-Image Turbo, Qwen Image | Passed |
| FLUX.2 Klein 4B: reference-image VAE encoding and T2I | Passed |
| Sana 600M and Anima: different stage orders, custom conditioning, multi-output requests | Passed |
| Z-Image TP2, Z-Image Ulysses2 with an odd patch grid, Wan TP2 x Ulysses2 | 3 passed in 448.82s |
| Two physical H200 nodes, Mooncake RDMA: Z-Image and Wan TP2 x Ulysses2 | All compared outputs had max absolute difference 0 |

The matrix varies resolution, steps, and seed; checks repeated and concurrent requests; and verifies recovery after invalid requests. FLUX.1-schnell was attempted but blocked by checkpoint access, so it is not counted as validated.

- At `fd59d2b6125`: 25 deployment unit tests passed, including the direct file entrypoint. The multi-rank matrix above also passed at this revision.
- Earlier at `8ed79b61785`: 448 tests plus 139 subtests passed, and the existing explicit FLUX.3 encoder graph passed both E2E cases. This broader suite was not rerun at the final revision.
- Cross-node runs used `40eca988b5f`; subsequent changes through `fd59d2b6125` only changed tests/docs.
- The publication merge `6935cb44f40` incorporates the prerequisite's docs/test corrections and leaves the validated runtime code unchanged. Required pre-commit hooks and `git diff --check` passed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No latency, throughput, or peak-memory improvement is claimed. Full-context transfer prioritizes correctness and can transfer/retain more data than an explicit-field graph. Representative coordinator warmup and workload-specific benchmarking are still required before production rollout.

## Current Limits

- Automatic mode requires complete placement in original sequential order, with consecutive stages per role. Pipelines still need accurate stage/component manifests and compatible factories/loaders.
- Workers must be trusted and run matching source versions: control metadata uses Python serialization. Do not expose internal RPC to untrusted clients.
- Arbitrary runtime objects, hidden stage-local state, overlapping storage views, and arbitrary cross-role sharded layouts are not universally supported.
- Each worker executes one request at a time; replicas provide concurrency. Node launch starts local processes, not remote provisioning or cluster scheduling. Failed work is not durably replayed.

## Checklist

- [x] Run required pre-commit checks.
- [x] Add unit and real multi-process/model tests.
- [x] Update documentation.
- [x] Document validation scope and operational limitations.
- [ ] Complete review and CI before marking ready.

issues.title: [Feat] ovis-image: add native Ovis-Image support
issues.body:
## Motivation

Add native text-to-image inference for [Ovis-Image 7B](https://huggingface.co/ATH-MaaS/Ovis-Image-7B) (Diffusers format). It is available through `sglang generate` and the OpenAI-compatible image API. `ATH-MaaS/Ovis-Image-7B`, the legacy `AIDC-AI/Ovis-Image-7B`, and local Diffusers component directories all resolve to the native pipeline. Defaults follow the official recipe: 1024 × 1024, 50 steps, CFG 5, 256 text tokens, BF16.

## Modifications

**Model and pipeline**
- Native Ovis DiT: 6 dual-stream and 27 single-stream blocks, context RMSNorm, SwiGLU, and the official weight mapping. Value/gate and attention/MLP output weights keep their own TP partitions.
- Reuses native Qwen3, AutoencoderKL, the shared denoising and residency stages, packed FLUX latents, and the conditioning cache.
- Follows the official prompt template, prefix masking, fixed-length text attention, dynamic scheduler shift, and `[A,A,B,B]` multi-output ordering.
- Supports serial and parallel CFG, DiT TP, Ulysses and Ring SP, and component/layerwise offload, with no new production CLI flags.
- Image editing, single-file weights, quantization, LoRA, caching accelerators, `torch.compile`, and breakable CUDA graphs are rejected with explicit errors.

**Numerics.** The goal is that single-GPU runs match pinned Diffusers bit for bit, and parallel runs stay within the reference's own noise.
- The QK RMSNorm rounds to BF16 before the FP32 RoPE, as the official `nn.RMSNorm` does. This is Ovis opt-in; FLUX defaults are unchanged.
- **Row-parallel projections**: TP row projections in the Ovis DiT (`OvisImageRowParallelLinear`) all-reduce FP32 partial products and round once with the bias, which is what the dense GEMM does. Reducing BF16 partials alone already puts short-text first predictions outside the BF16 tolerance; that was measured on one GPU with a K-split emulation.
- **Flash split-KV**: PyTorch flash attention switches to split-KV once `B·H·⌈Sq/128⌉ < 0.8·SMs`. TP and Ulysses shrink the local head count, so at short sequence lengths the shards take a different summation order than the full-head reference. On B200, at seq 1025, 24 heads and 12/6-head shards differ in 1.29M elements; at seq 4224 they match exactly. `OvisImageSDPAImpl` pads query rows past the threshold, but only when the full-head model would not split. This restores bitwise per-head equality, which a unit test checks.
- **Tail padding**: Ulysses tail-padded attention trims the padding after the all-to-all instead of masking it.
- Ovis-only, opt-in HF-compatible Qwen TP numerics. Text-encoder row projections gather the input and weight and run the full-K GEMM.

**Shared code**
- **VAE**: `AutoencoderKLMixin` now runs each tile of a tiled decode through spatial-parallel decode. Inputs shorter than the decode world size fall back to local decode. Before this, tiled + spatial decode called the sharded decoder on whole tiles. The Flux2 KL VAE shares this mixin and gets the same fix.
- **USP**: fixes receive-buffer ownership for sequential unpacked FP32 Q/K/V collectives.

**Tests and docs**
- Unit tests in `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/` cover component numerics against the official small models, the TP and attention numerics above, config, the validator, USP buffers, and tiled spatial VAE on real Gloo groups.
- A B200 HTTP e2e test.
- A manual oracle and multi-GPU runner in `test/manual/diffusion/`. It requests `quality="exact"` by default, because the serving default `lossless` mounts VAE fast paths that only move rounding.
- Cookbook page, catalog entry.

Attribution and sources: [official transformer](https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers/blob/c6df88a511a98740646ee55577b590c9852650ce/src/diffusers/models/transformers/transformer_ovis_image.py), [official pipeline](https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers/blob/c6df88a511a98740646ee55577b590c9852650ce/src/diffusers/pipelines/ovis_image/pipeline_ovis_image.py), [checkpoint](https://huggingface.co/ATH-MaaS/Ovis-Image-7B/tree/41be1c5821a92c970d63d7eb595a2fd3fe32b22e).

## Accuracy Tests

**Setup**
- Pins: checkpoint `41be1c58`, independent official Diffusers `c6df88a5`.
- Inputs: identical CPU initial latents. Reference SDPA excludes cuDNN, matching the native platform policy.
- Tolerances are unchanged: BF16 `atol=0.05, rtol=0.02`; FP32 `1e-4`.
- Commit: every result below is from this branch's HEAD, on B200, with a clean tree.

**Single GPU (exact tier)**
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| 512² L1/L64 and 1024²/50 quality scenes | Conditioning, every prediction, the full trajectory, and the decoded images are bit-exact vs official (PSNR ∞) |
| CFG2 L64 | Bit-exact |
| Same-latent dense VAE decode | Bit-exact vs official |

**Parallel, first predictions at the original tolerance**
| Topology | max abs / out-of-tolerance |
|---|---|
| L1 512² TP2 | 0.049 / 0 |
| L1 512² Ulysses2 | 0.016 / 0 |
| L1 512² TP2 × Ulysses2 | 0.049 / 0 |
| 1024² TP2 × Ulysses2 | 0.031 / 0 |

**Later steps against the noise baseline.** A late-step same-input check at the original tolerance cannot tell a parallel bug from evaluation-order noise. On a single GPU, changing only the FP32 summation order already puts step 49 at 496 out-of-tolerance elements.

We therefore gate the same-input four-GPU TP2 × Ulysses2 replay (1024², steps 0/11/12/49) against single-GPU controls:
- The controls are efficient-kernel SDPA, split-K with FP32 reduction, and split-K with BF16 reduction.
- Rule: per step, take the worse CFG branch. Max abs and the out-of-tolerance count must not exceed the worst control; RMSE must stay within 1.05× of it, because RMSE saturates at the BF16 floor.

| Step | TP2 × SP2 (max / count / rmse) | Worst control |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0.031 / 0 / 0.0044 | 0.031 / 0 / 0.0051 |
| 11 | 0.039 / 0 / 0.0057 | 0.148 / 23 / 0.0071 |
| 12 | 0.137 / 2 / 0.0065 | 0.270 / 93 / 0.0079 |
| 49 | 0.219 / 1693 / 0.0200 | 0.375 / 2242 / 0.0223 |

**Spatial VAE (same latent).** Raw decoder output has 17 out-of-tolerance values at max 0.090. The worst control (cuDNN autotune) is at 45 / 0.098, so this is within noise. Decoded images pass at the original tolerance.

**Runtime matrix.** All cases pass:
- single GPU, no-CFG, batch 2, prompt batch;
- component and layerwise offload;
- tiny TP2, tiny Ulysses2, tiny TP2 × SP2;
- TP2, Ulysses2, Ring2, CFG2, TP2 × SP2;
- tiled and spatial VAE;
- the HTTP lifecycle.

The cookbook HTTP recipe (1024²/50, one GPU) passes in 7.9 s including HTTP. Unit tests: 64 passed, 2 skipped.

## Visual comparison

1024 × 1024, 50 steps, CFG 5, seed 42, CPU generator, exact quality tier. All runs use the same initial latents. Reference is official Diffusers `c6df88a5`; columns are SGLang on 1 GPU, TP2 and Ulysses2 (2 × B200). The bottom row shows the mean absolute RGB error against the official image, amplified 8×.

- **1 GPU**: bit-exact, so the diff map is black.
- **TP2 and Ulysses2**: both pass the first-prediction gate at the original tolerance. Their later steps drift within the BF16 noise floor, which shows up as small content shifts rather than artifacts.

Prompt: 一个温暖的咖啡馆门口，木制招牌写着“欢迎光临”，电影写实摄影。

![Ovis-Image scene 0](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fusheng-ji/sglang/61769368c593c22a26a108cc14326b9220a13b2c/ovis-image-scene-0.jpg)

Prompt: A red bicycle leaning against a stone wall beside a quiet lake at sunset, realistic photography.

![Ovis-Image scene 1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fusheng-ji/sglang/61769368c593c22a26a108cc14326b9220a13b2c/ovis-image-scene-1.jpg)

| Topology | Scene 0 PSNR / SSIM | Scene 1 PSNR / SSIM |
|---|---|---|
| 1 GPU | ∞ / 1.0000 | ∞ / 1.0000 |
| TP2 | 28.05 / 0.9408 | 37.72 / 0.9731 |
| Ulysses2 | 27.02 / 0.9232 | 36.95 / 0.9685 |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The FP32 TP reduction doubles row-projection all-reduce traffic.

| Configuration | BF16 reduction | FP32 reduction (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| TP2, 1024², 50 steps, 2 × B200 (s/step, median of 4) | 0.083 | 0.099 |

Query padding only triggers at short sequences and does not run at 1024². These are DiT-step timings, not a serving benchmark.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- The flash split-KV head-count dependence affects any DiT that shards heads at short sequence lengths, for example FLUX, Qwen-Image, and Anima. The shared fix is in #43242 (`SDPAImpl` / `USPAttention`, exact tier). Whichever PR lands second will switch `OvisImageSDPAImpl` to the shared implementation.
- `.github/workflows/_pr-test-check-changes.yml` still references the old `test/registered/unit/diffusion` path. This predates this branch.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add unit tests.
- [x] Update documentation (cookbook page, catalog).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed results.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

### Update (2026-10-14)

- **Fixed an import broken by the previous `main` merge.** `ovis_image.py` still imported `qwen_image._pack_latents`, which #43064 removed, so the Ovis-Image config failed to import. It now uses `base.pack_latents_2x2`, which computes the same packing.
- **Merged current `main`.** Breakable CUDA graph conflict: `main` now keeps an explicit graph request on unvalidated models with a warning. Ovis-Image still rejects it through `validate_breakable_cuda_graph`, which now runs before that warning, and the config test follows `main`'s policy for other models.
- **Strict FP32 VAE oracles.** The FLUX.2 VAE parallel check now turns TF32 off in a scope on each rank for the strict FP32 oracle (restored on exit, nesting and exceptions) and keeps the 1e-4 tolerance; BF16 is checked separately under the production policy.

Validation on the merged head: Ovis-Image unit tests 37 passed, 2 skipped, 153 subtests passed. FLUX.2 VAE two-GPU check with full weights (tiled, tail tiles, tiny fallback, recovery): 8 cases per rank, all within tolerance, weights loaded strictly. `test_server_args.py` has the same 3 failures on this branch and on a clean `main` checkout (`c82e8bd5fe`), both 3 failed / 232 passed: two cold-import subprocess timeouts on our loaded host and an HF cache permission error. The two tokenizer-oracle tests that skip without a checkpoint were also run, with the local Ovis-Image-7B checkpoint: `test_ovis_image_config.py` 15 passed, none skipped.

The VAE check prints 60 `CUDACachingAllocator ... failed with OOM` warnings under the default allocator: each is one 138.8 GB request failing while the process already caches about 143 GB (most likely a cuDNN workspace probe; the call site was not captured). With `PYTORCH_NO_CUDA_MEMORY_CACHING=1` there are no warnings and the same 8 cases per rank pass, so the warnings do not hide a failure. fp32 results differ slightly between the two runs (up to 1.3e-5 against the 1e-4 tolerance), so they are not bit-identical.

### Update (2026-10-15)

Merged `main` again (73 commits). One conflict, in `docs/src/snippets/diffusion/model-catalog.jsx`: `main` added the MOSS-Image catalog entry next to Ovis-Image; both entries are kept. On the merged head: Ovis-Image unit tests 37 passed, 2 skipped without a checkpoint; with the local Ovis-Image-7B checkpoint `test_ovis_image_config.py` 15 passed, none skipped. `pre-commit run --all-files` passes twice (Rust hooks skipped: no `cargo` here, no Rust files touched). The FLUX.2 VAE two-GPU check was re-run on this head: 8 cases per rank, none out of tolerance, weights loaded strictly; the allocator warnings described above are unchanged (60 with the default allocator, none without caching).

### Update (2026-10-20)

Merged `main` twice more (to `7656071309`, no conflicts). On the merged head:

- `pre-commit run --all-files` passes twice.
- Ovis-Image unit tests (`test_ovis_image.py`, `test_ovis_image_config.py`, `test_ovis_image_validation.py`, `test_qwen3_encoder.py`, `test_usp_input_cache.py`) with `MODEL_PATH` set to the real Ovis-Image-7B checkpoint and offline mode: 43 passed, 155 subtests passed, 0 skipped. This runs the two checkpoint tokenizer tests that are skipped without a checkpoint: the real `text_encoder/config.json` gives `hidden_size == 2048` with `preserve_hf_numerics`, and empty and truncated prompts tokenize identically to the official diffusers chat tokenization (shape `(2, 284)`).
- `test_vae_tiled_spatial_parallel.py` on 4 x B200: 3 passed, 2 subtests passed. This includes `test_four_ranks_handle_small_tiles_and_restore_spatial_decode`, which fails with `invalid device ordinal` on a machine with fewer than 4 GPUs, so it needs a 4-GPU runner.

The test environment was rebuilt from a saved package manifest (diffusers 0.37.0, FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1, sglang-kernel 0.4.8, torch 2.13.0+cu130).

issues.title: [Refactor] kernels/diffusion/tests: Prune dead code and fix tests that never ran
issues.body:
## Motivation

Six months of fast kernel and diffusion work left a lot behind in `python/sglang/kernels`, `python/sglang/multimodal_gen` and the kernel/diffusion test trees: kernels nothing calls, registry metadata nothing reads, per-model copies of the same fused-op glue, env knobs that do nothing, and tests that pass without testing anything. This PR removes that, and fixes the real bugs the audit turned up along the way (several were silently shipping).

**408 files, +3,629 / -26,346.** About 1.3K of the additions are test oracles and helpers moved out of production modules into `python/sglang/test/kernels/`.

## Bugs fixed (please review these first)

| Area | Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| SANA (diffusion) | Since #37816 the VAE loader calls `vae.state_dict()` before `load_state_dict`; `AutoencoderDC` builds its inner diffusers model lazily, so that call built it with random init and the later load returned early. **All 375 VAE tensors were random; every SANA T2I image on main is noise.** | `load_state_dict` loads into an already-built inner model. Regression test in `test_vae_loader.py` (fails on main). |
| GLM-Image (diffusion) | #33555 added an unconditional `query[:, t:] = q_img` write-back after an in-place RoPE; torch 2.14 rejects the self-copy, so **every GLM-Image request fails** in the first DiT block. | Copy back only when the rotation returned new memory. Regression test `test_glm_image_attention.py`; `test_ar_models` re-enabled (fails on main, passes here in 175 s on 2xH200). |
| MiniMax-H3 VAE | The default-on `h3_vae_qk_rmsnorm_rope` path ran in `quality=exact` but was not bit-exact (~25% of rotated channels differ). A second, faster, quality-gated fused path for the same op already existed. | Removed the non-bit-exact path. **Behavior change:** the exact tier now runs the native chain (bit-identical to native); lossless is unchanged. |
| Diffusion CI | `STANDALONE_FILES` moved to `server/gpu_cases.py` in #24630 but the CUDA partition planner kept reading the runner, so **no CUDA standalone file has run since June** (12 2-GPU files + the 1-GPU ones). | Planner reads the case config. All 15 newly scheduled files were run on H200 through the CI code path; one rotted test fixed. |
| Env vars | Code read the legacy `SGL_*` names while docs/`environ.py` define `SGLANG_*`, and the rewrite is one-directional, so the documented names did nothing: `SGLANG_USE_DEEPGEMM_BMM` (5 models), `SGLANG_DG_USE_NVRTC`, `SGLANG_CPU_QUANTIZATION`, `SGLANG_DSA_TOPK_ROW_SPLIT`. | Read via `envs`; legacy names still work. |
| `BaseFusedOp` | `KernelBackend.FLYDSL` mapped to a missing `forward_flydsl`, so `SGLANG_FORCE_FUSED_OP_BACKEND=flydsl` raised `AttributeError`. | Stub added + test. |
| Tests that never ran | `test_fp8_kernel` returned early on every CUDA GPU with sm>=90; `test_swapab_attention` was registered on H100 but gated to sm_10x (production SM100 kernel had no CUDA coverage); sm_100 / sm_120 / 2-GPU / 4-GPU diffusion unit tests sat on a 1-GPU H100 lane; `test_qwen_image21` cache tests exercised a test-local re-implementation of the fix. | Each now runs on hardware that satisfies its gate (or was deleted with its dead kernel); the qwen_image21 tests drive the real block and fail when the fix is reverted. |
| SenseNova-U1 | `FlowMatchingHead` called `SimpleMLPAdaLN` with a signature the class doesn't have (crash for `fm_head_layers > 2`). | Restored the timestep-conditioned head; test fails on main. |

## Modifications

### Kernels (`python/sglang/kernels`, -13.8K)
- **Dead / test-only kernels removed** (each re-verified with whole-repo grep incl. string lookups): seg_la kernel, dsv4 `fused_ape_pool_norm_rope`, tilelang `fp8_index`, KDA prefill timing scaffolding, nvlink push/pull all-reduce wrappers, inkling two-shot all-reduce, `cutedsl_gdn_mtp_ring` T=1 entry, non-`f_b` FlyDSL KDA decode, dsa `GetK/GetS`, adler32 whole-tensor entry points, ReplaySSM circular commit, cvt helpers, mxfp8 v-cache update, fp8 ue8m0/hopper/transpose helpers, `w8a8_block_fp8_matmul`, `awq_gemm_triton`, rocm `tkw1`, `moe_fused_gate_jit`, inkling gate v1, `post_reorder_triton_kernel`, `fused_inplace_qknorm_across_heads`, elementwise `silu_and_mul_triton`/autotune path, `rms_normalize_triton`, stale `top_p_renorm_triton` copy, and others.
- **Legacy DSV4 compressor path removed** (`compress_old.py`, `fused_compress_triton.py`, srt `dsv4/compress_hip.py`, the old `CompressorBackendMixin`): every CUDA/HIP backend uses `compressor_v2`; `fused_norm_rope_inplace` (live) moved to `dsv4/elementwise.py`. AOT dsv4 q/k norm+RoPE ops (duplicates of the JIT ones) removed.
- **Registry (option A):** the KernelSpec inventory stays; write-only metadata goes (`FormatSignature`, `KernelSpec.format_signature/description/group/name`, `BaseFusedOp.format_signature/descriptions/dispatch_forward`, unused selector/platform helpers). `spec.CUDA_ONLY` replaces ~44 inline frozensets. Unused `BaseFusedOp`s (4 RMSNorm, Gelu/GeluTanh/ReLU2/QuickGELU) removed; facade wrappers nobody imports removed (this also fixes facade functions shadowed by same-named submodules). `Fp8ScaledMMOp` no longer declares an SM90 heuristic as a capability.
- **#42184 criteria applied** to the four remaining gate sites (route-quant, engram, vision_rope, minimax_m3): gates check eligibility, launchers enforce contracts.
- **Duplicates:** sparse-MLA decode reuses the shared kernels (bit-exact, 720 cases x 2 archs incl. fully masked rows); mxfp8 gfx95 reuses `mxfp8_quant`. Forks that are *not* bit-exact stay, each with a one-line comment (grok RMSNorm, gfx1250 qk-RMSNorm, int8 group quant on ROCm, marlin SiTU, minimax Gemma RMSNorm).
- **Test oracles shipped in op modules moved to `sglang.test.kernels`** (LPLB, dsa transform index, DCP LSE combine, dsv4 K-cache quant refs, extend attention, dspark window, multigpu launcher, mhc, per-token-group quant dispatch).

### Diffusion (`python/sglang/multimodal_gen`, -9.4K)
- **Dead code:** SenseNova-U1 unreachable chat/interleave/it2i paths (~2.6K; T2I output byte-identical), auto-residency estimators and the warmup stage-iteration calibration chain nothing read, SANA-WM parity debug harness (`SANAWM_*` env hooks incl. `torch.load` input injection), `MINIMAX_H3_USE_FUSED_NORM` path, unresolved MiniMax-H3 euler scheduler, registry subprocess-inspect path (pointed at a nonexistent module), delta-gzip realtime encoding (server + web UI), bundled-overlay lookup, `EncodingStage`, bitsandbytes 4-bit swap, `generate_with_lora` (could never run), `convert_hf_to_fp8.py`, unused platform hooks, unread `ServerArgs` fields, etc.
- **Env:** 12 `envs.py` entries nothing read removed (+ the docs rows presenting 5 of them as working knobs); raw reads of `SGLANG_ENABLE_FUSED_QKNORM_ROPE` / `MINIMAX_H3_VAE_*` declared in `envs.py` with identical parsing; unprefixed GDN dev knobs dropped.
- **Refactors (bit-exact):** `BitExactFusionGate.run()` replaces 24 hand-written verify-once/fallback blocks and the `mismatch_msg` boilerplate; one LayerNorm+modulate helper for FLUX.3/GLM/LongCat; `sites/` exports one `QualityGatedFusion` per family instead of four wrappers each (~50 facade entries, 28 imports gone). Sites that are hand-tuned for launch overhead, re-raise, verify inside the try, or differ in reference were left as they are (listed in the commit messages).

### Tests and CI
- Deleted always-skipped tests (env var set nowhere, `skipif(True)`, hard-coded dev paths), tautologies (default/literal echoes, `inspect.getsource` shape tests, log-format echoes, torch-behavior tests), duplicate cases and duplicate helpers; trimmed grids with no extra coverage (`fused_fp8_qkv_kv_cache` 1,344 -> 288 cases, AOT `moe_align` 4,368 -> 144, AOT per-token-group quant 3,632 -> 320). CI-tooling meta-tests are intentionally kept.
- New lane wiring: swapab on B200; Blackwell, SM120 and 4-GPU diffusion unit steps; 2-GPU diffusion unit files as 2-gpu standalone files; `quant-videogen` installed for its tests; comm benches no longer register no-op AMD runs; HPC-Ops tests (always skipped: the package isn't in the CI venv) disabled explicitly.
- **CI cost:** the standalone-file fix adds runners (1-GPU H100: 5 -> 6 partitions; 2-GPU: 3 -> 5 by current estimates). The estimates are 2-15x above the measured H200 times; I'll copy this PR's CI-measured values into `STANDALONE_FILE_EST_TIMES` before merge.

## Accuracy Tests

End-to-end, same GPU, fixed seed, base vs this branch (fused paths confirmed active by a gate tracer on both sides; no gate disabled):

| Model | Paths exercised | Result |
|---|---|---|
| ERNIE-Image, LongCat-Image, FLUX.2-klein-4B, Joy, MOSS-Image, Anima, Qwen-Image, Wan2.1-1.3B, Helios-Distilled | `BitExactFusionGate.run`, LN+modulate helper, QK-norm+RoPE, handler-table sites, gated residual | byte-identical |
| GLM-Image (1024², 30 steps) | LN+modulate helper, QK-LN | identical to main+fix; fused == native |
| SANA 600M (512², 20 steps) | VAE fix | identical to main+fix; reproducible across processes (main is noise) |
| SenseNova-U1.5-8B-MoT T2I | dead-path removal | PNG md5 identical |
| Z-Image-Turbo server warmup | residency/warmup cleanup | PNG identical, same peak memory |
| MiniMax-H3 VAE decoder | lossless in-place path / exact tier | lossless identical; exact == native |

Kernel dedups were checked bit-for-bit on H200 and GB300 (scripts in the commit messages' descriptions).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No perf-path changes intended. `BitExactFusionGate.run` was not applied to the launch-overhead-tuned sites (the closures add ~160-180 ns per call on the host).

## Validation

- **H200 (sm_90):** every file under `test/registered/kernels/ops`, `test/registered/unit` and `multimodal_gen/test/unit` (1,624 files). Failures were re-run on main: identical failing test ids (rust extensions not built in the source tree, NPU-only, multi-GPU tests on one GPU, pre-existing diffusion kernel failures); 2 port collisions from parallel runs pass alone. 
- **GB300 (sm_103):** every file under `test/registered/kernels/ops` (334 files): failing ids identical to main.
- **RTX PRO 6000 (sm_120):** FA4 sm120 + FA4 + dense FA4 + sm120 paged MQA logits + sm120 fp8 linear + mxfp4 sm120 + diffusion fp8 FA sm120 + kernel namespace: all pass, same as main.
- **Multi-GPU:** every CUDA diffusion standalone file run on 2xH200 through the CI runner path (incl. `test_ar_models` and `test_diffusion_bcg_tp2_zimage_turbo` at the final head); Kandinsky 6 4-GPU cases on 4xH200.
- `pytest --collect-only` over the test trees: no new collection errors; import walk over `sglang.kernels`, `sglang.multimodal_gen`, `sglang.srt.{layers,models,...}`: no new import failures.
- **Not validated:** ROCm, NPU, XPU, MUSA (HIP-only deletions are traced through backend selection and import-checked on CUDA), a full AOT wheel link (affected TUs compiled for sm90/sm100), 4-GPU cases on Blackwell.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

issues.title: [diffusion] Pipeline every USPAttention Ulysses path's exchange over the copy engine
issues.body:
## Motivation

#43164, #43361 and #43373 pipeline MiniMax-H3's Ulysses all-to-all against its dense attention, one head group at a time, over the copy engine:

- while group g attends, group g + 1's q/k/v moves;
- finished groups send their output back while later groups still attend;
- the result is bit for bit that of the sequential exchange.

It took 2–4% off H3 on H200 and B300.

No other model got it: every `USPAttention` Ulysses path still exchanges all heads first and attends afterwards. That covers Wan2.1/2.2, LTX-2, the FLUX family, Qwen-Image, Z-Image, HunyuanVideo, LongCat, GLM-Image, Helios, Krea2, Joy-Image, Kandinsky 6, Cosmos3 and more. This PR turns the pipeline into a building block that every Ulysses path of the layer uses, and that a custom attention module can call directly.

## Modifications

**The transport: `ulysses_pipelined_attention` / `IpcA2AMultiState.pipelined_attention`**

- **Layouts.** It covers every layout `USPAttention` exchanges:
  - q/k/v as `[batch, s_local, heads, head_dim]` at any batch size;
  - GQA, where k/v have fewer heads than q;
  - text rows every rank holds (`replicated=`, per part): a prefix, a suffix (`replicated_first=False`), or a K/V-only prefix.

  Replicated rows stay out of the exchange. Each rank places its own head groups of them into its receive slot on the copy engine. Their output reaches every rank with the shard rows, so the merged output comes back in the caller's row order: replicated rows (all heads) and this rank's shard.
- **Receive slots.** Per head group and part, the slot is one contiguous `[batch, rows, group_heads, head_dim]` tensor in exactly the order attention reads. `attend(q, k, v)` runs on views of it.
- **Buffers: one pool for every shape.** One pool per dtype holds the receive slots and output blocks of every call, grown to the largest call seen. The first version kept a set per call shape (up to 16), each twice over, alternating per call. One set is enough:
  - a rank sends a group's output only after attending over that group's slot, and a peer writes the next call's rows only after merging all of that output;
  - a peer's next output block needs this rank's rows of the next call, which this rank sends only after merging the previous call.

  The pool takes about 4 × rows per rank × heads × head_dim. That is half of what the sequential exchange's staging keeps at Ulysses 2 (two slots of q/k/v and output, per shape).
- **First-sight check (`sequential=`, `signature=`).** The first call per plan and signature also runs the caller's sequential path. It keeps the pipeline only if every rank sees the same bytes (one all-reduce); otherwise that shape keeps the sequential exchange for good. A backend that would not compute a head group exactly as it computes those heads in the full call can therefore never change a result.
  - The check runs the sequential path first, with the pool released, and over NCCL on per-call buffers (`uncached_a2a_staging()`). So the call never holds both exchanges' buffers, and no staging sized for it stays allocated. An all-to-all is a permutation, so its bytes do not depend on the transport.
- **Automatic group count.** It is now the largest of 7, 5, 4, 3 and 2 that divides the q and k/v heads per rank while each group's call still fills four waves of 128-row tiles. 5 and 3 are new candidates for Wan's 40 and 12 heads. The waves floor comes from B300, where cuDNN SDPA calls too small to fill the SMs cost more than the overlap saves:
  - Wan2.1 1.3B at Ulysses 4 in three one-head groups ran 44% slower than sequentially;
  - an LTX-2-shaped layer in four two-head groups ran 17% slower.

  Short sequences, such as a 1024² image, keep the sequential exchange. H3 keeps 7 groups on H200. On B300, T2VA at Ulysses 4 moves from 7 to 2 groups (3.99 waves at 7); the two were within run-to-run noise there in #43373.
- **Host cost.** Copies are issued from precomputed addresses instead of tensor views. A view per copy cost more host time than the copy at Ulysses 4. The decision per call shape is cached, so a shape that cannot pipeline steps aside at once.
- **H3 unchanged.** The H3 `fill` path (batch 1, no replicated rows) issues the same copies as before. Its buffers drop from about 10 to 6 × rows per rank × heads × head_dim (Ref2VA at Ulysses 2: 3.6 → 2.1 GB). The cookbook page says so.

**The layer: `USPAttention._pipelined_ulysses`**

Every Ulysses path describes its layout, hands over its attention core as `attend` and its own exchange-attend-exchange as `sequential`. The sequential code is kept as written and still runs whenever the pipeline does not. The paths covered:

| Path | Users | Attention core per head group |
|---|---|---|
| dense | Wan2.1/2.2, LTX-2 (unmasked) | `attn_impl.forward` |
| key mask / tail padding | Kandinsky 6, Anima, MOVA; FLUX family and Qwen-Image when the text is sharded | varlen FA over `cu_seqlens_tail`, the dense gap, or the gathered mask (FA varlen or SDPA) |
| replicated prefix (± key mask) | FLUX.1/2 with replicated text, Qwen-Image, LongCat, GLM-Image, Helios, Krea2 | `attn_impl.forward`, or the masked local attention |
| replicated suffix | Z-Image, Joy-Image, HunyuanVideo | `attn_impl.forward` (K/V in tail order, as before) |
| replicated K/V prefix | Cosmos3, Qwen-Image 2.1 | `attn_impl.forward` |

- The masked path's gathered mask and its varlen metadata are computed once before the exchange. Attention then has no collective or host sync per group.
- Ring attention, uneven sequence shards (`seq_lens`), the K/V-gather mode and the legacy `UlyssesAttention` keep the sequential exchange.
- `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_ULYSSES_PIPELINE_GROUPS=0` turns the pipeline off. The parallelism page and the environment-variable table describe it.

## Accuracy Tests

- `test_ipc_a2a_multi_gpu.py` passes at 2 and 4 ranks (4×B300). New cases:
  - batch 2;
  - replicated prefix, suffix and K/V-only prefix;
  - GQA;
  - automatic groups at a shape that fills the GPU, and declining at one that does not;
  - a verified signature that keeps pipelining;
  - a mismatching first call that returns the sequential result and stops pipelining that shape.

  - one pool serving every plan of the test, sized for the largest;
  - six back-to-back calls of two alternating plans with rank 0 attending about 10 ms slower, compared only after all were queued.

  Each case is checked byte for byte against attention over the global layout, with every head at once.
- New `test_usp_pipelined_attention_multi_gpu.py` passes at 2 and 4 ranks. It runs 13 `USPAttention` cases sequentially and with the pipeline and requires identical bytes:
  - dense at batch 1 and 2;
  - replicated prefix, with and without a key mask;
  - replicated suffix;
  - replicated K/V prefix;
  - gathered key mask;
  - GQA.

  It also checks that every case actually pipelined and verified, and that the first call of a new shape leaves no sequential staging behind. On B300 FlashAttention resolves to Torch SDPA, so these ran under cuDNN SDPA. The tail-padding varlen-FA branch needs Hopper and is covered there by the first-sight check.
- End to end, the output bytes do not change:
  - Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B 480p 81f: four alternating runs give the same MP4 (`0b3acb06debb`);
  - Z-Image-Turbo 2048²: four alternating runs give the same PNG (`34e0d5d0fb90`);
  - MiniMax-H3 T2VA at Ulysses 2 (its own fill pipeline through the rewritten transport): the MP4 is the same as on main (`639d5a2f219d`), before and after the shared pool;
  - Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B 1280×720 49f with the CI's server flags: six servers across main and both versions of this PR give the same MP4 (`10e8e381ddbc`).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

**One attention layer** (exchange + attention + output exchange), cuDNN SDPA, 4×B300, CUDA-event median. Every pipelined output equals the sequential one:

| Shape (global tokens × heads, replicated rows) | Ulysses 2: sequential → pipelined | Ulysses 4: sequential → pipelined |
|---|---:|---:|
| Wan2.1 14B 480p (32760 × 40) | 7.91 → 7.01 ms (−11.4%) | 4.10 → 3.61 ms (−11.8%) |
| Wan2.1 14B 720p (75600 × 40) | 40.98 → 39.13 ms (−4.5%) | 20.35 → 18.95 ms (−6.9%) |
| Wan2.1 14B 480p, batch 2 | 17.06 → 14.67 ms (−14.0%) | 9.07 → 7.76 ms (−14.5%) |
| Wan2.1 1.3B 480p (32760 × 12) | 2.65 → 2.31 ms (−12.6%) | 1.434 → 1.435 ms (keeps the sequential exchange) |
| LTX-2-like (24576 × 32) | 3.85 → 3.21 ms (−16.7%) | 2.17 → 1.88 ms (−13.3%) |
| Z-Image 2048² (16384 × 30, 128-row caption suffix) | 2.17 → 1.69 ms (−22.1%) | — (30 heads) |
| FLUX 2048² (16384 × 24, 512-row text prefix) | 1.90 → 1.44 ms (−24.0%) | 1.150 → 1.138 ms (keeps the sequential exchange) |
| HunyuanVideo-like (61440 × 24, 256-row text suffix) | 16.62 → 15.37 ms (−7.5%) | 8.39 → 7.80 ms (−7.1%) |

Shapes too short to split at Ulysses 4 keep the sequential exchange, at no cost: they skip straight to it once the first call turns them down.

**End to end on B300**, client latency per request, alternating sequential (`SGLANG_DIFFUSION_ULYSSES_PIPELINE_GROUPS=0`) and pipelined runs:

| Model, layout | sequential | pipelined |
|---|---:|---:|
| Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B 480p 81f, `--num-gpus 4 --ulysses-degree 2 --enable-cfg-parallel` (the cookbook's multi-GPU layout for 14B, here on 1.3B) | 6.89 / 6.89 / 6.89 / 6.90 s | 6.49 / 6.50 / 6.49 / 6.49 s (−5.8%) |
| Z-Image-Turbo 2048², `--num-gpus 2 --ulysses-degree 2` (the cookbook serves it on one GPU; Ulysses 2 here exercises the replicated caption suffix) | 1.53 / 1.53 / 1.55 / 1.55 s | 1.41 / 1.44 / 1.43 / 1.43 s (−7.1%) |

MiniMax-H3, which main already pipelines, does not regress through the rewritten transport. T2VA 5 s at Ulysses 2, 50 steps: 65.37 / 64.86 s on main, 64.41 / 64.40 s with this PR, same MP4. With the shared pool, in another session: 65.32 / 64.83 s against main's 65.38 / 64.90 s, same MP4.

On the 2×H100 CI runners (the FlashAttention path), Wan2.1 I2V 14B at Ulysses 2 denoises 3.0% (720P), 2.7% (720P with LoRA) and 3.1% (480P) faster than the H100 baselines.

**Memory.** The first version failed CI's peak guard on Wan2.1 I2V 14B 720P at Ulysses 2 on H100: 46440 MiB runtime allocated against a 44992 MiB baseline (+3.2%). The measured request's shape differs from every warmup shape, so the first-sight check ran inside it. It left the sequential exchange's staging allocated next to the pipeline's buffers, and a warmup shape's buffer set stayed allocated too. The shared pool and the uncached first-sight check above remove both.

One attention layer, per rank, at the Wan2.1 14B 720P 81f shape at Ulysses 2 (37800 rows × 40 heads × 128), 4×B300:

| | first call: peak | between calls: held | later calls: peak |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| sequential exchange | 4434 MiB | 2954 MiB | 4434 MiB |
| this PR, first version | 7831 MiB | 5907 MiB | 6425 MiB |
| this PR | 2475 MiB | 1477 MiB | 1994 MiB |

The first version's held memory assumes nothing released the staging between requests. The worker does release it after a warmup probe, and the first version then held 2953 MiB.

End to end, Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B with the CI's server flags (`--num-gpus 2 --ulysses-degree=2 --warmup-sampling-params '{"quality": "exact"}'`), two requests per server, two servers per arm in ABCCBA order. The request is 1280×720 at 49 frames: at 25 frames this model's groups fall just short of four waves on B300's 148 SMs, so that shape keeps the sequential exchange.

| | runtime allocated peak per request | second request |
|---|---:|---:|
| main | 15.21–15.22 GB | 22.04 / 22.08 s |
| this PR, first version | 15.75 GB | 20.92 / 20.71 s |
| this PR | 15.08–15.09 GB | 20.86 / 20.87 s |

The layer timings did not move with the shared pool. Against the first version, ABBA at Ulysses 2 and 4, every shape of the table above stays within ±1%; shapes that keep the sequential exchange in both trees vary by ±0.7%. The outputs are identical.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).

issues.title: [Diffusion] Fuse Anima AdaLN modulation and cache the FFI callable
issues.body:
## Motivation

With Anima's default 28-block configuration, each transformer forward evaluates 85 AdaLN modulation chains:

`LayerNorm(x) * (1 + scale) + shift`

Reuse the existing bit-exact modulation kernel to reduce intermediate tensor traffic and kernel launches. Also cache the shared kernel's exported FFI callable to avoid repeated function lookup.

## Modifications

- Route Anima's eager CUDA FP16/BF16 modulation through `modulate_scale_shift`.
- Convert strided scale/shift views into contiguous `[B, D]` rows when necessary, without copying the `[B, S, D]` activation.
- Cache the exported FFI callable.
- Preserve the original expression for CPU, FP32, and `torch.compile` tracing.

LayerNorm reduction, CUDA arithmetic, launch geometry, and the shared wrapper's eligibility checks, fallback, and error propagation remain unchanged.

## Correctness

Validated on H200 against baseline `affa261e3d`, with candidate `05bee50b2f`:

- **Anima AdaLN:** 36/36 bit-exact comparisons covering FP16/BF16/FP32, batch sizes 1/2, sequence lengths 17/1024/4096, hidden size 2048, and gated/ungated modules. Eligible cases assert fused dispatch; FP32 cases assert fallback. BF16 batch-2 CUDA graph replay also passes.
- **Shared callers:** 48 component cases per version cover FLUX, Ideogram, LingBot, and LTX-2 video/audio. Output byte hashes and dispatch counts match across versions. Five changed-input CUDA graph replays per version pass.
- **Existing tests:** 42 passed per version across the modulation kernel, FLUX/LTX model-site, LTX layout, and Anima test suites.
- **Full-model generation:** all 16 images across the two benchmark experiments have identical decoded pixels and PNG bytes.
- Pre-commit passes for both modified files.

The AdaLN and shared-caller checks use external validation scripts with synthetic inputs. No new repository unit tests are added. Other models were validated at the component level.

[Correctness report, test logs, and source provenance](https://github.com/cuzmi/sglang/tree/codex/pr-results/diffusion-prs/anima-modulate-fusion/rebase_validation)

## Performance

**Workload:** H200, BF16, TP1, FA attention, one 1024×1024 image, 30 steps, CFG 4, seed 42. `torch.compile` and CUDA graph are disabled.

**Model:** `circlestone-labs/Anima-Base-v1.0-Diffusers`, revision `073c3a9db359c31ad0e8aa268d15775473c2176c`.

Both versions run on the same GPU in ABBA + BAAB order. Each arm starts a fresh CLI process, performs a one-step same-resolution request warmup, and then measures one 30-step request: **four process samples per version**.

The metric is worker request wall time with CUDA synchronized at request boundaries. Both versions receive the same timing-only instrumentation, which is excluded from this PR. Model loading, warmup, output transport, and PNG saving are excluded. No profiler or per-stage synchronization is enabled.

| Version | Mean request (ms) | Range (ms) | Sample SD (ms) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Baseline `affa261e3d` | 3185.73 | 3164.03–3229.58 | 29.95 |
| Candidate `05bee50b2f` | 3065.52 | 3051.42–3099.78 | 22.94 |

Mean latency decreases by **120.21 ms (3.77%)**. The ABBA and BAAB blocks separately show **3.98%** and **3.56%** reductions.

All eight requests complete 30 steps with identical outputs. Source hashes and timing instrumentation are verified for the experiment.

These results cover one fixed prompt, seed, resolution, and GPU instance. The two code changes are measured together; their individual contributions are not isolated.

[Benchmark reports, configuration, and measurements](https://github.com/cuzmi/sglang/tree/codex/pr-results/diffusion-prs/anima-modulate-fusion/rebased_perf)

[Published evidence index](https://github.com/cuzmi/sglang/blob/codex/pr-results/diffusion-prs/anima-modulate-fusion/PUBLISHED.md) · [Raw synchronized run: logs, timings, and eight PNGs](https://github.com/cuzmi/sglang/tree/codex/pr-results/diffusion-prs/anima-modulate-fusion/results/anima-rebased-sync-perf-20261004T164048Z-a9b075f6)

<details>
<summary>Additional measurements and historical evidence</summary>

A separate eight-arm experiment using the unmodified native worker timer measured **3151.82 → 3016.00 ms (4.31% lower)**. That timer does not explicitly wait for CUDA completion before stopping. It ran on another H200 instance, so these samples are not pooled with the primary result, and the difference between experiments does not measure the CUDA tail.

Earlier experiments against `6fa3fe69e2` included an integration-only run that regressed by **4.93%** and a later combined run that improved by **4.15%**. The latter included duplicate-check removal already present in the current baseline. These historical results are retained in the archive and are not used as the current PR's performance result.

Historical profiling showed modulation launches decreasing from 510 to 170 in a denoising step containing 170 AdaLN calls. This was not reprofiled after rebasing.

[Historical experiment archive](https://github.com/cuzmi/sglang/tree/codex/pr-results/diffusion-prs/anima-modulate-fusion/evidence)

</details>

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [ ] Add unit tests. No new repository tests are added; existing suites and external validation results are listed above.
- [x] Review documentation requirements. No user-facing API or configuration changes.
- [x] Provide correctness and performance results.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

issues.title: [diffusion] Add native Anima Base v1.0 support
issues.body:
## Summary

Add native text-to-image support for `circlestone-labs/Anima-Base-v1.0-Diffusers`.

- Implement Anima's Cosmos Predict2 transformer and learned T5-token conditioner with native attention, linear layers, TP/SP, and layerwise offload.
- Reuse the Qwen3 encoder, Qwen-Image VAE, component loaders, scheduler, denoising loop, and serving API. Read the official modular checkpoint layout without conversion or a Diffusers runtime upgrade.
- Integrate Cache-DiT and breakable CUDA graphs. Preserve the conditioner's unmasked padding semantics instead of adding graph-bucket padding.
- Add numerical/registration regressions, an opt-in repeated-request HTTP test, a nightly generation case, and a cookbook/deployment picker.

Scope is Base v1.0. Aesthetic/Turbo and single-file ComfyUI checkpoints are not covered. The cookbook links the checkpoint's non-commercial license.

## Validation

Remote validation on up to two H200 GPUs, Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, Diffusers 0.37.0, Transformers 5.12.1:

- 76 related unit tests and seven subtests passed, including full tiny-transformer FP32/BF16 comparisons against Diffusers Cosmos.
- The additional full `test_server_args.py` run plus Anima contracts had 213 passing tests and one LTX placement assertion failure (`test_auto_ltx_original_replaces_component_cpu_offload`). The same failure reproduces on the unchanged base `82cdd72588e4` source tree on H200; this PR does not change that policy.
- HTTP tests passed for 512px/4-step/two-output and 1024px/30-step/single-output requests, with two identical requests per case and pixel-exact repeatability.
- Full-checkpoint functional checks passed for TP2, Ulysses2, Ring2+FA, CFG2, encoder folding, DiT/conditioner layerwise offload, parallel tiled VAE decode, FA/SDPA, SageAttention (pinned SM90 build), Cache-DiT (30 steps), and actual breakable graph capture/replay. Sage and Cache-DiT are approximate paths, not quality-equivalent replacements.
- At 512px/30 steps, CFG 4, seed 42, CPU generator, BF16 components, FP32 latents, and matched SDPA, native versus official Diffusers output measured SSIM **0.9512**, PSNR **31.61 dB**. First positive/negative DiT noise-prediction cosine similarity was **0.999991/0.999992**. This is one sample, not a general quality guarantee or a speedup claim.

The reference uses Diffusers commit `0377f0c1b34e3ff313d41edad1bd79c2ed8bb5ec` in a separate environment. Tests do not claim coverage of TPxSP combinations, multi-node execution, non-NVIDIA hardware, or third-party LoRAs. No H100 performance baseline or consistency GT is fabricated from the H200 measurements.

Desktop validation also passed on RTX 5090 (32 GB VRAM, x86_64) and DGX Spark (GB10, 128 GB unified memory, ARM64), using the same package versions above and source `7f3f903f039`. Both used one GPU, `--performance-mode speed --attention-backend torch_sdpa`, with no CPU offload. Each completed two 1024px/30-step/single-output HTTP requests and two 512px/4-step/two-output requests; corresponding same-device repeats were pixel-exact, and output images were visually inspected. These are functional checks, not throughput benchmarks or cross-hardware bitwise-equivalence claims. The cookbook now defaults to RTX 5090 and marks only the tested recipes verified; Anima-specific compatibility details live in the cookbook rather than the shared compatibility matrix.

## Measured Deployment Recipes

The cookbook now selects measured recipes rather than functional-only baselines. At 1024x1024, 30 steps, CFG 4, n=1, CPU generator and PNG/base64 output, five warm sequential HTTP requests gave:

| Hardware | Original eager | Recommended | Configuration |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| RTX 5090 32 GB | 6.99 s | 6.10 s | cuDNN SDPA + compile, tiled VAE |
| DGX Spark 128 GB unified | 26.03 s | 17.41 s | Torch SDPA + compile, tiled VAE |
| H200 141 GB | 3.22 s | 2.22 s | FA + compile, untiled VAE |

Two NVLink H200s with CFG parallelism + compile + untiled VAE measured 1.28 s. Untiled H200 recipes use about 4-5 GiB more allocated memory and are verified only at 1024/n1. Tiled paths also passed 512/n1, 1024/n2, and 1536/n1. At 512, CFG eager beat compiled; TP2/SP2 compilation was not the winner.

This search included 418 timed HTTP requests across 96 completed workload/configuration combinations. Startup/compilation time is excluded. The final recipes use default CPU-thread settings; no approximate caching or quantized attention is enabled. The three single-GPU recipes measured PSNR 21.95-35.44 dB / SSIM 0.851-0.969 against same-device eager across three prompt/seed pairs, not pixel equivalence or a perceptual quality guarantee.

Eager remains selectable. The picker only changes Anima recipes, not global runtime defaults. Pre-commit, cookbook config checks, Mintlify validation and browser interaction checks passed.

## Reproduce HTTP Tests

```bash
SGLANG_ANIMA_TEST_MODEL=circlestone-labs/Anima-Base-v1.0-Diffusers \
  python -m pytest python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/server/test_server_anima.py -q
```

issues.title: [Refactor] kernels/diffusion/tests: Prune dead code and fix tests that never ran
issues.body:
## Motivation

Six months of fast kernel and diffusion work left a lot behind in `python/sglang/kernels`, `python/sglang/multimodal_gen` and the kernel/diffusion test trees: kernels nothing calls, registry metadata nothing reads, per-model copies of the same fused-op glue, env knobs that do nothing, and tests that pass without testing anything. This PR removes that, and fixes the real bugs the audit turned up along the way (several were silently shipping).

**408 files, +3,629 / -26,346.** About 1.3K of the additions are test oracles and helpers moved out of production modules into `python/sglang/test/kernels/`.

## Bugs fixed (please review these first)

| Area | Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| SANA (diffusion) | Since #37816 the VAE loader calls `vae.state_dict()` before `load_state_dict`; `AutoencoderDC` builds its inner diffusers model lazily, so that call built it with random init and the later load returned early. **All 375 VAE tensors were random; every SANA T2I image on main is noise.** | `load_state_dict` loads into an already-built inner model. Regression test in `test_vae_loader.py` (fails on main). |
| GLM-Image (diffusion) | #33555 added an unconditional `query[:, t:] = q_img` write-back after an in-place RoPE; torch 2.14 rejects the self-copy, so **every GLM-Image request fails** in the first DiT block. | Copy back only when the rotation returned new memory. Regression test `test_glm_image_attention.py`; `test_ar_models` re-enabled (fails on main, passes here in 175 s on 2xH200). |
| MiniMax-H3 VAE | The default-on `h3_vae_qk_rmsnorm_rope` path ran in `quality=exact` but was not bit-exact (~25% of rotated channels differ). A second, faster, quality-gated fused path for the same op already existed. | Removed the non-bit-exact path. **Behavior change:** the exact tier now runs the native chain (bit-identical to native); lossless is unchanged. |
| Diffusion CI | `STANDALONE_FILES` moved to `server/gpu_cases.py` in #24630 but the CUDA partition planner kept reading the runner, so **no CUDA standalone file has run since June** (12 2-GPU files + the 1-GPU ones). | Planner reads the case config. All 15 newly scheduled files were run on H200 through the CI code path; one rotted test fixed. |
| Env vars | Code read the legacy `SGL_*` names while docs/`environ.py` define `SGLANG_*`, and the rewrite is one-directional, so the documented names did nothing: `SGLANG_USE_DEEPGEMM_BMM` (5 models), `SGLANG_DG_USE_NVRTC`, `SGLANG_CPU_QUANTIZATION`, `SGLANG_DSA_TOPK_ROW_SPLIT`. | Read via `envs`; legacy names still work. |
| `BaseFusedOp` | `KernelBackend.FLYDSL` mapped to a missing `forward_flydsl`, so `SGLANG_FORCE_FUSED_OP_BACKEND=flydsl` raised `AttributeError`. | Stub added + test. |
| Tests that never ran | `test_fp8_kernel` returned early on every CUDA GPU with sm>=90; `test_swapab_attention` was registered on H100 but gated to sm_10x (production SM100 kernel had no CUDA coverage); sm_100 / sm_120 / 2-GPU / 4-GPU diffusion unit tests sat on a 1-GPU H100 lane; `test_qwen_image21` cache tests exercised a test-local re-implementation of the fix. | Each now runs on hardware that satisfies its gate (or was deleted with its dead kernel); the qwen_image21 tests drive the real block and fail when the fix is reverted. |
| SenseNova-U1 | `FlowMatchingHead` called `SimpleMLPAdaLN` with a signature the class doesn't have (crash for `fm_head_layers > 2`). | Restored the timestep-conditioned head; test fails on main. |

## Modifications

### Kernels (`python/sglang/kernels`, -13.8K)
- **Dead / test-only kernels removed** (each re-verified with whole-repo grep incl. string lookups): seg_la kernel, dsv4 `fused_ape_pool_norm_rope`, tilelang `fp8_index`, KDA prefill timing scaffolding, nvlink push/pull all-reduce wrappers, inkling two-shot all-reduce, `cutedsl_gdn_mtp_ring` T=1 entry, non-`f_b` FlyDSL KDA decode, dsa `GetK/GetS`, adler32 whole-tensor entry points, ReplaySSM circular commit, cvt helpers, mxfp8 v-cache update, fp8 ue8m0/hopper/transpose helpers, `w8a8_block_fp8_matmul`, `awq_gemm_triton`, rocm `tkw1`, `moe_fused_gate_jit`, inkling gate v1, `post_reorder_triton_kernel`, `fused_inplace_qknorm_across_heads`, elementwise `silu_and_mul_triton`/autotune path, `rms_normalize_triton`, stale `top_p_renorm_triton` copy, and others.
- **Legacy DSV4 compressor path removed** (`compress_old.py`, `fused_compress_triton.py`, srt `dsv4/compress_hip.py`, the old `CompressorBackendMixin`): every CUDA/HIP backend uses `compressor_v2`; `fused_norm_rope_inplace` (live) moved to `dsv4/elementwise.py`. AOT dsv4 q/k norm+RoPE ops (duplicates of the JIT ones) removed.
- **Registry (option A):** the KernelSpec inventory stays; write-only metadata goes (`FormatSignature`, `KernelSpec.format_signature/description/group/name`, `BaseFusedOp.format_signature/descriptions/dispatch_forward`, unused selector/platform helpers). `spec.CUDA_ONLY` replaces ~44 inline frozensets. Unused `BaseFusedOp`s (4 RMSNorm, Gelu/GeluTanh/ReLU2/QuickGELU) removed; facade wrappers nobody imports removed (this also fixes facade functions shadowed by same-named submodules). `Fp8ScaledMMOp` no longer declares an SM90 heuristic as a capability.
- **#42184 criteria applied** to the four remaining gate sites (route-quant, engram, vision_rope, minimax_m3): gates check eligibility, launchers enforce contracts.
- **Duplicates:** sparse-MLA decode reuses the shared kernels (bit-exact, 720 cases x 2 archs incl. fully masked rows); mxfp8 gfx95 reuses `mxfp8_quant`. Forks that are *not* bit-exact stay, each with a one-line comment (grok RMSNorm, gfx1250 qk-RMSNorm, int8 group quant on ROCm, marlin SiTU, minimax Gemma RMSNorm).
- **Test oracles shipped in op modules moved to `sglang.test.kernels`** (LPLB, dsa transform index, DCP LSE combine, dsv4 K-cache quant refs, extend attention, dspark window, multigpu launcher, mhc, per-token-group quant dispatch).

### Diffusion (`python/sglang/multimodal_gen`, -9.4K)
- **Dead code:** SenseNova-U1 unreachable chat/interleave/it2i paths (~2.6K; T2I output byte-identical), auto-residency estimators and the warmup stage-iteration calibration chain nothing read, SANA-WM parity debug harness (`SANAWM_*` env hooks incl. `torch.load` input injection), `MINIMAX_H3_USE_FUSED_NORM` path, unresolved MiniMax-H3 euler scheduler, registry subprocess-inspect path (pointed at a nonexistent module), delta-gzip realtime encoding (server + web UI), bundled-overlay lookup, `EncodingStage`, bitsandbytes 4-bit swap, `generate_with_lora` (could never run), `convert_hf_to_fp8.py`, unused platform hooks, unread `ServerArgs` fields, etc.
- **Env:** 12 `envs.py` entries nothing read removed (+ the docs rows presenting 5 of them as working knobs); raw reads of `SGLANG_ENABLE_FUSED_QKNORM_ROPE` / `MINIMAX_H3_VAE_*` declared in `envs.py` with identical parsing; unprefixed GDN dev knobs dropped.
- **Refactors (bit-exact):** `BitExactFusionGate.run()` replaces 24 hand-written verify-once/fallback blocks and the `mismatch_msg` boilerplate; one LayerNorm+modulate helper for FLUX.3/GLM/LongCat; `sites/` exports one `QualityGatedFusion` per family instead of four wrappers each (~50 facade entries, 28 imports gone). Sites that are hand-tuned for launch overhead, re-raise, verify inside the try, or differ in reference were left as they are (listed in the commit messages).

### Tests and CI
- Deleted always-skipped tests (env var set nowhere, `skipif(True)`, hard-coded dev paths), tautologies (default/literal echoes, `inspect.getsource` shape tests, log-format echoes, torch-behavior tests), duplicate cases and duplicate helpers; trimmed grids with no extra coverage (`fused_fp8_qkv_kv_cache` 1,344 -> 288 cases, AOT `moe_align` 4,368 -> 144, AOT per-token-group quant 3,632 -> 320). CI-tooling meta-tests are intentionally kept.
- New lane wiring: swapab on B200; Blackwell, SM120 and 4-GPU diffusion unit steps; 2-GPU diffusion unit files as 2-gpu standalone files; `quant-videogen` installed for its tests; comm benches no longer register no-op AMD runs; HPC-Ops tests (always skipped: the package isn't in the CI venv) disabled explicitly.
- **CI cost:** the standalone-file fix adds runners (1-GPU H100: 5 -> 6 partitions; 2-GPU: 3 -> 5 by current estimates). The estimates are 2-15x above the measured H200 times; I'll copy this PR's CI-measured values into `STANDALONE_FILE_EST_TIMES` before merge.

## Accuracy Tests

End-to-end, same GPU, fixed seed, base vs this branch (fused paths confirmed active by a gate tracer on both sides; no gate disabled):

| Model | Paths exercised | Result |
|---|---|---|
| ERNIE-Image, LongCat-Image, FLUX.2-klein-4B, Joy, MOSS-Image, Anima, Qwen-Image, Wan2.1-1.3B, Helios-Distilled | `BitExactFusionGate.run`, LN+modulate helper, QK-norm+RoPE, handler-table sites, gated residual | byte-identical |
| GLM-Image (1024², 30 steps) | LN+modulate helper, QK-LN | identical to main+fix; fused == native |
| SANA 600M (512², 20 steps) | VAE fix | identical to main+fix; reproducible across processes (main is noise) |
| SenseNova-U1.5-8B-MoT T2I | dead-path removal | PNG md5 identical |
| Z-Image-Turbo server warmup | residency/warmup cleanup | PNG identical, same peak memory |
| MiniMax-H3 VAE decoder | lossless in-place path / exact tier | lossless identical; exact == native |

Kernel dedups were checked bit-for-bit on H200 and GB300 (scripts in the commit messages' descriptions).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No perf-path changes intended. `BitExactFusionGate.run` was not applied to the launch-overhead-tuned sites (the closures add ~160-180 ns per call on the host).

## Validation

- **H200 (sm_90):** every file under `test/registered/kernels/ops`, `test/registered/unit` and `multimodal_gen/test/unit` (1,624 files). Failures were re-run on main: identical failing test ids (rust extensions not built in the source tree, NPU-only, multi-GPU tests on one GPU, pre-existing diffusion kernel failures); 2 port collisions from parallel runs pass alone. 
- **GB300 (sm_103):** every file under `test/registered/kernels/ops` (334 files): failing ids identical to main.
- **RTX PRO 6000 (sm_120):** FA4 sm120 + FA4 + dense FA4 + sm120 paged MQA logits + sm120 fp8 linear + mxfp4 sm120 + diffusion fp8 FA sm120 + kernel namespace: all pass, same as main.
- **Multi-GPU:** every CUDA diffusion standalone file run on 2xH200 through the CI runner path (incl. `test_ar_models` and `test_diffusion_bcg_tp2_zimage_turbo` at the final head); Kandinsky 6 4-GPU cases on 4xH200.
- `pytest --collect-only` over the test trees: no new collection errors; import walk over `sglang.kernels`, `sglang.multimodal_gen`, `sglang.srt.{layers,models,...}`: no new import failures.
- **Not validated:** ROCm, NPU, XPU, MUSA (HIP-only deletions are traced through backend selection and import-checked on CUDA), a full AOT wheel link (affected TUs compiled for sm90/sm100), 4-GPU cases on Blackwell.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

issues.title: [Fix] attention: Make FlashInfer prefill bit-exact on radix-cache hits
issues.body:
## Motivation

With `--enable-deterministic-inference`, the FlashInfer backend produced bit-identical logprobs only while a prompt was uncached. As soon as the radix cache served a prefix hit, the same prompt at `temperature=0` could return different logprobs and even a different first token. This makes deterministic inference unusable with the radix cache, which is on by default.

The deterministic-inference docs listed radix cache as unsupported for FlashInfer and the server disabled it automatically. This PR removes that limitation.

## Root cause

For a paged prefill, FlashInfer sizes its CTA tile from

```
avg_packed_qo_len = sum(q_len_i * gqa_group) / batch_size
```

through `FA2DetermineCtaTileQ`. A cached request only sends the uncached tail to attention (`q_len = seq_len - prefix_len`), so `avg_packed_qo_len` shrinks and the kernel can pick a different `cta_tile_q` bucket than the full prefill of the same prompt. Different tile sizes split the softmax reduction differently, and the results stop being bit-exact.

The reduction order is otherwise batch invariant; only the tile choice differs.

## Fix

Under deterministic inference, pad the front of each paged-prefill q block with zero rows up to

```
min_q = deterministic_prefill_min_q(num_qo_heads, num_kv_heads, head_dim)
```

which keeps `avg_packed_qo_len` above the bucket threshold for every batch shape (GQA groups and head dim included). FlashInfer aligns a q block to the tail of its KV segment, so the real rows keep their original causal positions; the padded rows produce garbage that is discarded by gathering the output back to the real rows. The padded q rows are built inside the attention layer, so the rest of the model still sees the real token count.

Padding is skipped for ragged prefill, sliding-window KV pools, custom KV indices/masks, multi-item scoring, piecewise CUDA graph capture and cuda-graph prefill wrappers, where the assumption above does not hold or the extra copy is not worth it. The full prefill CUDA graph plans against a q buffer sized at capture, and flashinfer's `enable_cuda_graph` plan derives the tile from the bucket's static token count rather than the per-batch average, so padding there is neither needed nor possible and raising `qo_indptr` only broke the `q.shape[0] == qo_indptr[-1]` invariant (reported by Woody-Hu on A100). A radix hit and the full recompute of the same prompt usually land in different buckets, so this PR makes no bit-exactness claim for `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill full`; it only stops the crash there. The bit-exactness claims below are for eagerly planned attention, which is what the new CI case runs.

Enabling radix cache for FlashInfer also required splitting the deterministic backend whitelist: the absorbed-MLA check reused `RADIX_SUPPORTED_DETERMINISTIC_ATTENTION_BACKEND`, so adding `flashinfer` there would have silently allowed an unsupported MLA combination. The MLA check now uses its own `MLA_SUPPORTED_DETERMINISTIC_ATTENTION_BACKEND`.

## Validation

- FlashInfer kernel probe (`BatchPrefillWithPagedKVCacheWrapper`, cold vs radix hit, Qwen3-8B shapes 32/8/128, `head_dim=128`, `min_q=17`): with padding `max|diff| = 0.0` (bit-exact); without padding `max|diff| = 0.001953125`.
- Same probe on short queries q=2/4/6/37: padded runs are bit-exact against the full prefill; unpadded runs differ.
- End-to-end tiny dense model with radix cache enabled: padded prefill gives identical logprobs for cached and uncached requests; disabling the padding reproduces the divergence (`1.335e-5`).
- Interactive `sglang.test.test_deterministic --test-mode radix_cache` passes, and the mode now fails if `cached_tokens == 0`, so it cannot silently pass on a cache miss.
- Prefill overhead, `qwen3.5-9b` on one GPU with FlashInfer + deterministic inference, 16 concurrent requests, median of 3 bursts: the worst case where every request is a 1-4 token extend behind a 1024-token shared prefix goes from 65.7 ms to 70.7 ms per burst (~7.5%), while a cold full prefill of 16 x 1028 tokens is unchanged (1382.7 ms -> 1383.2 ms, within noise). The padding row copy only happens when a request is shorter than `min_q`; regular prefill never enters that path.
- Independent reproduction on A100 (SM80) by Woody-Hu (see the PR thread): Qwen3-4B, 3.7k-token prompts, recompute vs radix hit. Whitelist-only (no padding) flips 5/8 greedy outputs with step-0 top-k drift up to 0.107; with the padding 0/8 flips and `max|delta| = 0.0`.

## Tests

- New `test/registered/unit/layers/attention/test_flashinfer_deterministic.py`: 7/7.
- Existing `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_flashinfer_host_plan.py`: 5/5.
- Existing `test/registered/unit/test_model_overrides.py`: 115/115, including a new regression test that FlashInfer + deterministic inference keeps the radix cache.
- New CI case `TestFlashinferDeterministicRadixCache` runs the radix_cache mode on CUDA with `--disable-prefill-cuda-graph`.
- New kernel-level test `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_flashinfer_deterministic_prefill.py` (base-b-kernel-unit): padded 1-token and 3-token extends, and a mixed batch that keeps a long request next to a padded one, all bit-exact against their full prefill, plus a cuda-graph regression: driving `call_begin_forward` with a real `use_cuda_graph=True` wrapper keeps the real `qo_indptr` and attaches no gather indices, while the eager wrapper pads to `min_q`; 6/6 locally.

## Caveat

Hybrid GDN models (Qwen3.5 family) still show a cached/uncached difference when the uncached chunk is very short (`q_len <= 32`), with both FlashInfer and Triton, so it is a separate pre-existing property of the hybrid linear-attention path rather than of this padding. For `q_len >= 33` both backends are bit-exact on those models as well. The tests use the regular Qwen3 model, where the fix is exact.

The prefill CUDA graph is another independent source of non-determinism: with the default `cuda_graph_config.prefill.backend = "breakable"` the same request differs between graph replay and eager execution, so the new CI case disables it. That is orthogonal to this PR and is worth a separate look. On A100, Woody-Hu measured `disabled` / `breakable` / `full` as bit-exact with each other on both fa3 and padded FlashInfer, so the drift above is so far an SM120 observation.

## Related work

#43612 aligns chunked-prefill chunk starts to FlashInfer's 128-row q-tile grid from the scheduler, and explicitly leaves radix-cache hits, tiny last chunks and batches of 1-token extends unaddressed. This PR covers the radix-cache-hit case from the attention side, enabled only under deterministic inference. The two are complementary: chunk alignment avoids off-grid starts when the scheduler is free to move them, while padding makes short extends match the full-prefill tile when the start is fixed by the prefix length.

issues.body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

<!-- PR title: [Type] scope: title, or [Type] [Hardware] scope: title.
Type: Feat, Fix, Refactor, Perf, Doc, Test, CI, or Chore.
Scope: any module or model name (no fixed list or letter-case restriction), e.g. attention, qwen3, or flash-attn.
Hardware: optional single tag without spaces. Use uppercase hardware tags (AMD, NVIDIA, NPU, MI300X), except for exactly these four spellings: Intel, Apple, Huawei, Ascend.
Title: no letter-case restriction.
Reverts: use GitHub's default title, Revert "original title".
Examples: [Fix] attention: Fix KV cache indexing; [Perf] [AMD] flash-attn: Optimize decode performance. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

`FlashAttentionBackend.__init__` selects a FlashAttention build (FA3, generic FA4, or the SM12x FA4 entry points added in #32991) and binds it to `self.flash_attn_varlen_func` / `self.flash_attn_with_kvcache`. Only one call site uses that binding: the `fa_skip_kv_cache` varlen call (#33007). The other 14 call sites go through the module-level wrapper `sglang.kernels.ops.attention.flash_attention`, passing `ver=self.fa_impl_ver`. That wrapper has no SM12x branch, which causes two problems:

- On SM12x with FA4, the entry points `__init__` selects run on one path, and the generic FA4 entry points run everywhere else. One consequence: the static `max_seqlen_k` that the SM12x runtime policy sets for CUDA-graph decode is dropped before it reaches the paged-decode fast path.
- A subclass that needs a different FA build, such as a vendor backend, has to replace both the `__init__` binding and every module-level call. There is no single seam.

What a single dispatch buys:

- **What `__init__` selects is what runs.** The kernel choice lives in one assignment, so a build-specific feature (the SM12x entry points, their runtime policy, any future build) reaches every call site, not only the one that happens to read `self.*`.
- **One override point for other FA builds.** #45946 (SAIL FA3 / FlashMLA) is a live example. To swap the FA build today, it extracts the binding into `_init_flash_attention_functions` and overrides it, and it also adds `_call_flash_attn_with_kvcache` / `_call_flash_attn_varlen_func` methods and rewrites every call site to go through them, because those call sites ignore the binding. On top of this PR, overriding the binding is enough: the `_call_*` methods and the call-site rewrites can go, along with the function-local import they run on every CUDA call. The FA part of that PR's base-class diff shrinks to the method extraction.
- **No `ver=` to thread through each call**, and the new guard test keeps the backend from drifting back to two paths, which is how it got here (see below).

### History

The backend used to have a single dispatch. #22028 bound `self.flash_attn_*` in `__init__` and aliased them at the top of each forward. Four days later, #20796 replaced those aliases with the module-level wrapper plus `ver=`, so it could route FA3 through the kernels-community loader. That left the `__init__` binding unused. #32991 added the SM12x choice to that binding, and #33007 reconnected one call site. #33426 unified the dispatch again, but it was reverted in #39405 for process reasons (merged before review and CI completed) and never resubmitted.

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->

- Every FA call in `flashattention_backend.py` goes through `self.flash_attn_*`. The per-call `ver=` and the module-level wrapper import are removed.
- For FA3, `__init__` now binds `sglang.kernels.ops.attention.flash_attention_v3`, which is the build the wrapper already dispatched to for `ver=3`. `fa_skip_kv_cache` on FA3 used to call `sgl_kernel.flash_attn` directly; it now follows `SGLANG_USE_SGL_FA3_KERNEL` like every other path. The default (`1`) still loads the `sgl_kernel` build. `get_scheduler_metadata` still comes from `sgl_kernel`.
- `flash_attention_v4_sm120.flash_attn_varlen_func` / `flash_attn_with_kvcache` accept and forward `mask_mod`. Previously their `**_` swallowed it, which would drop FA4 image masks on SM12x now that those paths route there. A call with `mask_mod` skips the cached paged-decode fast path.
- New `test_flashattention_kernel_dispatch.py`, a CPU test: it fails if any FA call in the backend uses a name other than `self.flash_attn_*`. Verified to fail on `main` and pass here.

Behavior by configuration:

| Configuration | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| FA3 | wrapper(`ver=3`) -> `flash_attention_v3`; `fa_skip` -> `sgl_kernel.flash_attn` | `flash_attention_v3` everywhere (same kernel by default) |
| FA4, not SM12x | wrapper(`ver=4`) -> `flash_attention_v4`; `fa_skip` -> `flash_attention_v4` | `flash_attention_v4` everywhere; kwargs the wrapper filtered out land in its `**_` |
| FA4, SM12x | 14 sites -> generic `flash_attention_v4`; `fa_skip` -> `flash_attention_v4_sm120` | `flash_attention_v4_sm120` everywhere, with `max_seqlen_k` and `mask_mod` reaching it |

Out of scope: `dots_hybrid_backend.py` and `minicpm/attention_adapter.py` still call the module-level wrapper with their FA backend's `fa_impl_ver`.

## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->

A/B tests ran this branch and its merge base (`d4939cc267`) side by side on two GPUs of the same host, with identical server flags. GSM8K used sgl-eval 0.1.3, 200 examples, temperature 0, max_tokens 1024. For Qwen2.5 the prompt was Qwen's own math prompt ("Please reason step by step, and put your final answer within \boxed{}"), because the default GSM8K prompt makes it answer with a bare `\boxed{}`. DeepSeek-V2-Lite used the default prompt.

**H200 (SM90)**

| Model / path | Flags | branch | main |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, GSM8K | `--attention-backend fa3` | 91.5 | 92.0 |
| Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, GSM8K | `--attention-backend fa4` | 90.5 | 91.0 |
| DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat (MLA), GSM8K | `--attention-backend fa3 --trust-remote-code` | 60.5 | 58.0 |
| gte-Qwen2-1.5B-instruct, `fa_skip_kv_cache` | `--is-embedding --attention-backend fa3 --disable-radix-cache --chunked-prefill-size -1` | cosine(branch, main) min 0.9999998 | |
| gte-Qwen2-1.5B-instruct, `fa_skip_kv_cache` | same, `--attention-backend fa4` | cosine(branch, main) min 1.0000000 | |

Unit tests:
dense `test_fa3.py` and `test_fa4.py`, `test_flashattention_return_lse.py`, `test_flashattention_paged_mha.py`, `test_flashattention_graph_metadata.py`, `test_flashattention_pa_swa_prefill_lens_size.py`, `test_verify_widening_is_wired.py`, dense `test_tbo.py`. Result: 38 passed, 0 skipped.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

<!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. -->

No kernel changes.

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
