issues.title: [Fix] attention: Dispatch hybrid-model full-attn layers by call form in FA backend
issues.body:
## Description

Fixes #42012.

Glm5Next-style hybrid models interleave linear-attention (KDA) layers with full-attention layers whose `RadixAttention` calls arrive in **plain-MHA form**: `q/k/v` share the head count (verified live: `q=k=v=(T, 8, 256)`) and `q_rope` is absent, backed by a per-token **single-latent-head** KV pool (`(N, 1, 512)`).

The FlashAttention backend routes every call through the backend-level `use_mla` flag when the model family is MLA-enabled, so those MHA-form calls entered the absorbed-MLA path and carved a zero-width rope slice out of the latent cache:

```
RuntimeError: shape '[-1, 64, 8, 0]' is invalid for input of size ...
              page_size × tp_k_head_num × (head_dim − v_head_dim = 0 for NoPE)
```

crashing at the first decode CUDA-graph capture. The fix routes **by call form**: when `q_rope` is absent and `k` carries the same head count as `q`, take the standard MHA path regardless of `use_mla`. Absorbed-MLA calls keep `k` as a single latent head (or pass `q_rope`) and never match the predicate, so DeepSeek-style MLA behavior is unchanged. Applied at the three routing sites (forward_extend, its save path, forward_decode).

## Validation (end-to-end, same setup as the issue)

8x RTX PRO 6000 (SM120), GLM-5.3-Flash FP8 TP8, `--attention-backend fa4`, docker image built 2026-09-18 (v0.5.20-equivalent) with the identical change bind-mounted:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| engine init | crash at first decode-graph capture (`shape '[-1, 64, 8, 0]'`) | healthy, capture passes |
| correctness | — | `17×19=323` + reasoning chain correct; generation clean |
| single-stream decode | — | 84.6 tok/s (3 runs stable) |
| ~3K-token prefill | — | ≈88 tok/s |

Triton on the same config measures 82.4 tok/s decode / ≈88 tok/s prefill, so the patched fa4 path is on par with the previously-only-working backend on this model; neither is the limiting factor for the hybrid model's overall throughput on SM120.

Two operational notes discovered along the way:
- FA4 CuTe rejects FP8 inputs below SM100 (`AssertionError: FP8 is only supported on SM100`), so on SM120 this checkpoint needs `--kv-cache-dtype bf16` to serve through fa4 — a separate kernel-support constraint, unchanged by this PR.
- With bf16 KV, `fa_k_descale`/`fa_v_descale` still get threaded and the CuTe interface rejects descale args for non-FP8 inputs (`q_descale/... only supported for FP8 inputs`). The v0.5.20 validation tree additionally guards the descale kwargs by cache dtype; I kept this PR minimal (routing fix only) but can fold that guard in if maintainers prefer it handled here.

## Test Plan

- Serve any Glm5Next checkpoint on SM120 with `--attention-backend fa4 --kv-cache-dtype bf16`: init/capture succeeds, output correct (validated above).
- DeepSeek-family MLA regressions: absorbed calls are structurally excluded from the new predicate (single-latent-head `k` or explicit `q_rope`); happy to run any standard MLA smoke the team uses.

issues.title: [sgl-kernel] Diagnose libtorch ABI mismatch on import instead of a cryptic undefined symbol
issues.body:
## Motivation

On a standalone `sglang-kernel` install next to a different PyTorch than it was built against, `import sgl_kernel` fails with `undefined symbol: c10::MessageLogger...`. That looks like a GPU-arch problem, so #29317 was filed as a "missing SM121 wheel" — but the wheel does contain `sm_121a`. The real cause is a PyTorch C++ ABI mismatch.

Docker and `pip install sglang` pin PyTorch to 2.11, so they aren't affected; this only hits the standalone-wheel + mismatched-torch case. #26598 is the long-term fix. Until then, this makes the error say the torch version is mismatched, so it stops getting misread as a missing arch.

## Modifications

- `load_utils.py`: on an `undefined symbol` failure, name the installed torch and the missing symbol instead of a generic reinstall/arch message.
- `load_utils.py` / `__init__.py`: add `load_common_ops()`; with `SGLANG_KERNEL_ALLOW_MISSING_OPS` set it warns and returns `None` instead of raising (debug only — kernels still raise if called).
- `tests/test_load_utils.py`: cover the ABI message, the non-ABI case, and the flag.
- `faq.mdx`: document the mismatch and the working install paths.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A — import-path only.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit
- [x] Add unit tests — `tests/test_load_utils.py`
- [x] Update documentation — `faq.mdx`
- [x] Accuracy and speed benchmarks — N/A
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance

## Notes

- `SGLANG_KERNEL_ALLOW_MISSING_OPS` uses `os.environ` since `sgl_kernel` can't import `sglang.srt.environ`; matches the existing `SGLANG_KERNEL_API_LOGLEVEL`.
- The flag is debug-only; it doesn't make a model serve on a mismatched install.

Refs #29317. Complements #26598.

issues.title: [Fix] qsa: Fail early on SM89 without classic FA2
issues.body:
## Base and scope

Retargeted to `main` after the model integration landed in #37500 (replacing #36497). Rebased onto `fd5c52588ff2` on October 26; current head `0570f5e17dbf` includes the required `6a39ddf1f2e0` CI baseline. The main-branch resolver still accepts an importable FA4 fallback on SM89 when classic FA2 is missing; this PR keeps its SM89 preflight fix independent of the model-support stack.

## Motivation

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next currently fails late on NVIDIA L20 / SM89 when the image does not contain classic FlashAttention / FA2:

```text
FlashInfer TRTLLM resolver -> unavailable on SM89
classic flash_attn / FA2    -> not importable
flash_attn.cute / FA4       -> importable, so the resolver selects it
first sparse decode         -> CuTe MLIR operation creation failure
```

On four L20s with the released FP8 checkpoint, the server loaded the approximately 173 GB checkpoint and became HTTP-ready before the first generation request failed in the FA4/CuTe path. Importability is therefore not a sufficient compatibility check, and the failure happens after the most expensive part of startup.

## Modifications

- Represent the resolved QSA sparse-decode backend explicitly as `TRTLLM`, `TRITON_ROCM`, `KDA_SM121`, classic `FA2`, or `FA4_CUTE` and use the same result for preflight and runtime dispatch.
- Reject the FA4/CuTe fallback only on exact SM89 when classic FA2 is unavailable, with an actionable error.
- Run the QSA check before `ModelRunner.load_model()` and log the selected backend once on TP rank zero.
- Keep the QSA implementation lazily imported for non-QSA models.
- Preserve the existing TRTLLM route on SM100/SM120, dedicated KDA route on SM121, and import-based policy on SM90. Preserve the current ROCm Triton packed-decode path without requiring FA2/FA4/aiter, and retain the existing aiter varlen helper. The behavioral change is intentionally limited to the hardware reproduced here.

## Independence / related work

- #36806 changes the exact SM120 FlashInfer route; it does not add an SM89 path or preflight.
- Draft #36787 adds SM120 kernels and leaves the existing flash-attn fallback on other architectures, including SM89.
- #36531 and #36558 track SM12x failures, not L20 / SM89.

The October 13 main snapshot still permits the import-based FA4 fallback on SM89. A targeted October 13 search of PR titles/bodies for QSA and SM89 found this PR and the separate L20 MoE-config PR, but no equivalent preflight implementation. This does not exclude other ongoing or unindexed work.

## Tests

### October 26: current head `0570f5e17dbf`

Rebase-only update; the patch is unchanged apart from surrounding main-branch context. On one L20, the registered policy tests and upstream ROCm resolver cases pass (**19 tests; actual ROCm kernel test deselected**), and the selected classic FA2 kernel passes all **16 FP16/BF16 parity cases**. Maximum absolute error: FP16 `0.000548`, BF16 `0.00416`. Local isolated CPU policy checks, Ruff, isort, formatting, and whitespace checks also pass.

Uses torch `2.14.1+cu130`, Triton `3.8.0`, classic FA2 `2.8.3.post1`, and the existing experiment environment with isolated updates to FlashInfer `0.7.2` and sglang-kernel `0.4.10`. The two full negative-startup runs below remain October 13 evidence; they were not repeated during this rebase. No 176B model was loaded for this update.

### October 13: historical head `99755df6008d`, real NVIDIA L20 / SM89

Fresh Python 3.12 environment with dependencies resolved from this head's `python/pyproject.toml`, without inheriting the old image's Python packages. Core versions: torch `2.14.1+cu130`, FlashInfer `0.7.1`, flash-attn-4 `4.0.0b34`, Triton `3.8.0`, transformers `5.19.0`, sglang-kernel `0.4.9`. Imported source files match this head. No dependency-version checks were disabled.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Registered policy tests + upstream ROCm resolver cases | **19 passed, 2 subtests passed** in each of three runs; one actual ROCm kernel test deselected on NVIDIA |
| Real SM89 preflight, FA2 absent / FA4 importable | Expected actionable error; 0 MiB allocated tensor memory |
| Full `launch_server`, FA2 absent | **Two consistent expected failures: 50.08 s and 49.16 s**, before weight loading |
| Real SM89 preflight after installing classic FA2 | Selects and logs `classic FlashAttention / FA2` |
| Selected FA2 kernel vs FP32 reference | **16/16 passed**: FP16/BF16, two seeds, four KV-length patterns |
| Installed dependency consistency | `uv pip check`: all 211 installed packages compatible |

The full-startup tests use the real local Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 checkpoint configuration, TP1, and disabled CUDA graphs. Both stack traces reach `ModelRunner.initialize -> preflight_model_backends -> preflight_qsa_sparse_decode_backend` and raise:

```text
RuntimeError: QSA sparse decode on NVIDIA SM89 requires classic FlashAttention / FA2,
but it is not importable. FlashAttention-4 / CuTe is not a validated QSA fallback
on SM89/Ada. Install a compatible FA2 build before starting SGLang.
```

Neither log contains `Load weight begin`; the model-runner memory baseline is 0.00 GB. An earlier attempt in the old image stopped at its FlashInfer version gate and is not counted as a passing startup test.

FA2 parity mirrors the QSA varlen call: 24 Q heads, 2 KV heads, head dimension 256, one query per row, `causal=True`, and KV lengths `[1]`, `[64]`, `[0,1,17]`, `[31,0,129,257]`. Maximum absolute error against the FP32 reference was **5.49e-4 for FP16** and **4.17e-3 for BF16**. Empty rows and extra packed-buffer capacity are included. Tolerances: FP16 `atol=0.002, rtol=0.005`; BF16 `atol=0.01, rtol=0.01`.

Build disclosure: classic FA2 `2.8.3.post1` was compiled locally with only its two CUDA/C++ build-standard flags changed to C++20, following upstream [#2879](https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/pull/2879) / [#2899](https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/pull/2899) for newer Torch headers. FA2 kernel sources were unchanged; this experiment-only build adaptation is not part of this SGLang PR.

### Check that newer FA4 has not already removed the failure

FA4 `4.0.0b34` does contain an SM8x forward path, so this is **not a claim that FA4 is universally unsupported on Ada**. Directly exercising the same varlen interface on L20 with the actual QSA head dimension 256 still fails all eight FP16/BF16 × KV-length cases with CUDA launch/configuration errors. Changing only the head dimension to 128 passes all eight numerical-control cases.

Minimal reproduction of the failing QSA shape, in that environment:

```python
import torch
from flash_attn.cute.interface import flash_attn_varlen_func

q = torch.randn(1, 24, 256, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
k = torch.randn(71, 2, 256, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
v = torch.randn_like(k)
cu_q = torch.tensor([0, 1], device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
cu_k = torch.tensor([0, 64], device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
flash_attn_varlen_func(q=q, k=k, v=v, cu_seqlens_q=cu_q,
                      cu_seqlens_k=cu_k, max_seqlen_q=1, max_seqlen_k=64,
                      softmax_scale=256**-0.5, causal=True)
```

The registered suite covers SM89, SM90, SM100, SM120, SM121, ROCm's no-varlen-dependency path, non-QSA lazy no-op, rank-zero logging, and exception propagation. Other architectures are policy/unit coverage, not hardware validation. Ruff, isort, registered-test taxonomy, and whitespace checks passed.

The [independent RTX 4090 report](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36968#issuecomment-6142214847) supports the original failure and workaround; it is not counted as testing this head. These results validate fail-fast and the selected kernel, **not successful full-model 176B serving, CUDA-graph capture, throughput, or complete upstream CI**.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable. This changes startup validation and backend observability, not a kernel or successful inference path.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code according to the contribution guide.
- [x] Add registered regression tests.
- [x] Validate the original failure boundary on real SM89 hardware.
- [x] Preserve non-SM89 behavior.
- [x] No documentation update is needed because no user-facing flag or API is added.

issues.title: [Fix] [Intel] attention: Fall back to intel_xpu for deterministic inference
issues.body:
## Motivation

Deterministic inference picks a CUDA-only attention backend on Intel XPU. With no `--attention-backend`, `_deterministic_attention_backend` falls through the SM100/SM120 check to `fa3`, whose factory asserts `SM>=80 and SM<=90`. `get_device_capability()` returns `(None, None)` on XPU, so the assert fires and the server dies during startup:

```
Attention backend not specified. Falling back to 'fa3' for deterministic inference.
...
AssertionError: FlashAttention v3 Backend requires SM>=80 and SM<=90.
```

Every deterministic run on XPU that does not name a backend is affected, including a plain `--enable-deterministic-inference` launch. `intel_xpu` is already in `DETERMINISTIC_ATTENTION_BACKEND_CHOICES`; nothing selected it.

## Modifications

- `arg_groups/overrides.py`: resolve the deterministic fallback to `intel_xpu` on XPU. The branch only runs when `attention_backend is None`, so an explicitly requested backend is untouched.
- `test/registered/unit/test_model_overrides.py`: cover both directions - the XPU fallback resolves to an XPU-capable backend, and an explicit backend is left alone. The first case fails on pre-fix code (verified), the second passes before and after.

## Accuracy Tests

Intel Arc Pro B60, `sgl-kernel-xpu` built from source.

`test/registered/cuda_graph/breakable/test_bcg_with_lora.py` - unmodified by this PR, and the test that surfaced the bug, since it enables deterministic inference without naming a backend. Before: every case errored at server launch on the fa3 assert. After: **12/12 pass** (`TestBCGLoRACsgmv` 6/6, `TestBCGLoRATriton` 6/6, ~2.5 min per class on one card).

Logs confirm the fix took effect and the test is not passing vacuously: each of the four servers logs `Falling back to 'intel_xpu' for deterministic inference`, and each class records 10 prefill batches served by the breakable CUDA graph (`cuda graph: True`), so the graph-vs-eager prompt-logprob comparison really ran through the graph path.

New unit cases: 2 passed; 1 of the 2 fails when the fix is reverted.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable - startup-path config resolution only, no effect on steady-state inference.

issues.title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] attention: Native FP8 KV cache for SM120 FA4 kernels
issues.body:
## Motivation

On SM120 (RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell), `--attention-backend fa4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` fails at startup:

```
AssertionError: FP8 is only supported on SM100 (compute capability 10.x) for FA4 CuTe.
```

The SM120 FA4 kernels only accept FP16/BF16 (see also #42333). FP8 KV halves both KV-cache memory and KV bandwidth. On a bandwidth-bound decode, that means more concurrent requests and lower per-step attention time. This PR runs E4M3 Q/K/V natively through the SM120 prefill and decode kernels.

## Modifications

- `fa4_sm120/flash_fwd.py`
  - QK^T and PV both run on the E4M3 `m16n8k32` warp MMA.
  - V stays in shared memory as E4M3, so there is no BF16 copy and V smem is halved. It is loaded as the N-major B operand through `LdMatrix16x16x8bOp(transpose=True)` with an explicit TV layout and retile, ported from `quack` `GemmSm120`. The auto-generated trait reads the wrong K for this atom.
  - Before the cast, P is pre-scaled by 256. This keeps small probabilities out of the E4M3 subnormal range, which matters with attention-sink-heavy distributions. The scale is undone in the output rescale, so `row_sum`/LSE are unchanged and split-KV partials stay linear.
  - Per-(batch, kv_head) q/k/v descales: `q·k` is folded into the softmax scale, and `v / 256` into the final O rescale. When no descales are passed, they are compile-time `1.0`, so the BF16 IR is unchanged.
  - Output dtype is decoupled from the input dtype (`o_dtype = BFloat16` under FP8). `sO` aliases `sQ` with a size that covers BF16 O.
  - Shared-memory accounting uses per-buffer element sizes. New tile candidates for head dims > 256 fit the 101376 B SM120 budget, for FP8 and also BF16. BF16 HD512 previously raised `exceeds SM120 shared-memory capacity`.
- `fa4_sm120/flash_fwd_decode.py`: the transposed HD256 paged-decode kernel gets the same FP8 path. V is the M-major A operand, and P is the K-major B operand in E4M3.
- `fa4_sm120/runtime.py`: FP8 paged decode with head dim > 256 selects `num_splits` to keep about 2k CTAs in flight, capped at 16. The cached host-plan fast paths stay BF16-only.
- `flash_attn/cute/interface.py`
  - Allows E4M3 on SM120 when q/k/v share the dtype.
  - Missing descales are filled with ones, and all three are made contiguous. This is needed because `DescaleTensors` rebuilds its fields by position from the non-`None` values, and the backend passes stride-0 `expand()` views.
- `flash_attn/cute/flash_fwd.py`: adds `o_dtype` in the shared base, defaulting to `dtype`, so SM80/SM90 are unaffected.
- `flashattention_backend.py`: on SM120 FA4, q is cast to FP8 and descales are passed for prefill and for head dims > 256 as well. Other architectures keep the existing condition.

The SM90/SM100 kernels and the native `sgl-kernel` path are untouched.

## Accuracy Tests

Kernel level, against an fp32 reference on dequantized inputs. The new unit tests cover varlen and paged inputs, HD128/256/512, `pack_gqa`, sliding window, and learnable sink:

| case | cosine |
|---|---|
| paged decode HD256, window 1023 | 0.99972 |
| paged decode HD512 | 0.99974 |
| paged prefill HD256 (819 q / 8192 k), window 1023 | 0.99972 |
| paged prefill HD512 (819 q / 8192 k) | 0.99968 |
| attention-sink distribution, all four cases above | 0.999998 |

The remaining error comes from rounding P to E4M3 (3 mantissa bits). BF16 outputs are bitwise identical to `main` for HD256 prefill and decode.

End to end: `gemma-4-31B-it` (ModelOpt mixed FP8/NVFP4, 50 sliding HD256 layers + 10 full HD512 layers), 1× RTX PRO 6000, `few_shot_gsm8k` on the 1209-question GSM8K-Platinum test set:

| KV cache | accuracy | invalid |
|---|---|---|
| BF16 | 0.730 | 0.012 |
| FP8 E4M3 (this PR) | 0.742 | 0.008 |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Kernel microbenchmark (CUDA graph, 100 replays, 9216 KV tokens, Hq=32; decode uses B=20):

| case | BF16 µs | FP8 µs | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| decode HD256, Hkv=16, window 1023 | 213.6 | 105.0 | 2.03× |
| decode HD512, Hkv=4 | 1018.3 | 549.6 | 1.85× |
| prefill HD256, 1024 q | 175.5 | 98.5 | 1.78× |
| prefill HD512, 1024 q | 12871.6 | 5880.1 | 2.19× |

Serving: same model and GPU, ISL 8k / OSL 1k with 90% prefix cache. The run sweeps concurrency under ITL p90 < 50 ms and TTFT avg < 8 s:

| KV cache | max concurrency | output tok/s | ITL p90 |
|---|---|---|---|
| BF16 | 20 | 383.36 | 49.12 ms |
| FP8 E4M3 (this PR) | 46 | 863.56 | 48.43 ms |

That is 2.25× output throughput at the same latency budget. With FP8, the KV pool holds 644569 full-attention and 96685 SWA tokens.

Server flags: `--attention-backend fa4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --page-size 1 --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.15 --mem-fraction-static 0.92`.

Note: Gemma 4 with FA4 and MTP speculative decoding additionally needs #43542. That fix is independent of this PR and not required for the results above.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_flash_attention_4_sm120.py`: 62 passed (9 new) on SM120. The new tests fail on `main`.
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

issues.title: [QSA] Tune sm120 sparse prefill geometry
issues.body:
**Depends on #36787 and stays a draft until it merges.** #36497 merged into `main` through #37500 on 2026-09-08, so this branch is now #36787 rebased onto `main` plus one commit; that commit is what this PR adds (its GPU test sits in `test/registered/kernels/ops/qsa/` after the test layout consolidation).

#36787 gave sm120 its QSA sparse decode, split-K and MQA scoring paths but left the two sparse prefill kernels (`_sparse_gqa_prefill` and `_sparse_gqa_chunk_prefill`) launching with the L20 fallback selection: the table's large-prefill entry supplies `BLOCK_N=16` with one warp and two stages, and the head tile comes from `max(16, next_power_of_2(group_size))`. This PR selects an sm120 launch family by measurement.

## Motivation

Prefill for this model routes every full-attention layer through the sparse kernels: the indexer selects `token_topk + compress_ratio - 1 = 2051` token slots per query row and the attention kernel streams up to that budget (rows whose visible context is shorter stream less). That makes the cost per call nearly independent of context length once the budget saturates; in the measurements below the chunk kernel moves only from 2.98 ms to 3.05 ms between 32k and 128k context on the previous geometry. The cost sits in launch configuration rather than data volume, so tuning the geometry improves it without touching the arithmetic.

The tuned family, held in `_SM120_PREFILL_CONFIGS` and selected by measurement:

- Group size 6 (the FP8 TP4/EP4 rank shape, 6 local query heads over 1 KV head): `BLOCK_M=8`, `BLOCK_N=16`, 4 warps, 3 stages.
- Group size 12 (the NVFP4 TP2 rank shape, 12 local query heads over 1 KV head): `BLOCK_M=16`, `BLOCK_N=16`, 2 warps, 3 stages.
- The tuned tuples apply only inside the measured workload envelope; everything else keeps the existing H20/L20 tables. The selector receives the kernel kind, the top-k, the local KV-head count, and the longest request from both launch sites, and the tuned family requires all of: the 188-SM SM120 configuration the numbers come from (an exact device set, not a threshold; unmeasured SM120 parts stay on the table), top-k 2051 (the only measured index width), head dimension 256, group size 6 with one local KV head or group size 12 with one or two (the measured TP rank shapes), 8,192 or more total query rows for ordinary prefill (its lowest measured point), and for chunk prefill 512 or more rows per request on average plus a grid-utilization bound (`max_q * num_requests <= 2 * total_q`) so a batch of one long request padded by short ones cannot take a geometry measured on uniform batches. Triton older than 3.7 is a policy floor: the family was measured on 3.7.1, and a 3.6.0 spot check compiled and ran the 8-row dot. sm121 (GB10) is excluded the same way as in #36787. `SGLANG_QSA_PREFILL_GEOMETRY` offers `table` (force the device table) and `tuned` (skip the device set and row gates while keeping the workload, architecture, and version gates, for measuring an unlisted SM120 part with the included benchmark), in the style of the #36787 backend overrides. The registered kernel test forces the tuned path on any SM120 card, so a 5090 run covers correctness there (its performance was not measured, which is why it is not in the device set); on the H100 kernel-unit runner the architecture gate makes that part skip.

On the mechanism: in both kernels one Triton program handles one query row, and `BLOCK_M` tiles the query heads of one KV group, so the fp32 accumulator is `[BLOCK_M, 256]` per program and a `BLOCK_M` below the group size is invalid rather than untried (Triton lowers the 8-row dot onto the 16-row MMA instruction shape). The ablations and the register table below carry the evidence: for group 6 either change alone measured slower, so the gain needs the smaller head tile and the schedule together, and the register data rules out the single-factor stories. For group 12, which cannot shrink `BLOCK_M` below its 12 heads, the 2-warp 3-stage schedule accounts for the full gain.


## Modifications

One commit over the stacked history:

- `_get_prefill_config` in `sparse_attn.py` with the named `_SM120_PREFILL_CONFIGS` table, the workload-envelope conditions (kernel kind, top-k, local KV-head count, row thresholds, and the grid-utilization bound), the exact device set, the Triton 3.7 version floor, the `SGLANG_QSA_PREFILL_GEOMETRY` override, and a bounded cache on the device-table choice.
- Two registered test files (GPU kernel tests and a CPU selector test) and a manual benchmark alongside the existing decode and MQA ones, with providers for the shipped selector, the previous geometry derived from the shipped table logic, forced geometry tuples from the command line, a torch reference, and a gather plus FlashAttention synthetic reference, over both prefill kernels and a configurable query count. The benchmark exits nonzero when a provider exceeds its error bound against the requested torch reference.

## Kernel measurements

Produced by the included benchmark on one GPU of the host below: batch 1, chunk 8192, 2,051 selected token slots per query row, head dimension 256, one KV head, BF16, CUDA events, 10 warmups, median of 100 iterations. Timed providers alternate inside one shared window because sequential per-provider runs measured up to 6.8% higher on the first provider from clock state. A provider's absolute time still depends on which providers share its window, so milliseconds are comparable within one table and the ratios are the result; repeats of one cell within a fixed window agree to about 0.1%. The torch reference is computed on every timing run, every provider is checked against it, and the benchmark exits nonzero past a 0.02 max-abs bound. The torch and synthetic columns are timed in their own windows at three iterations, so they are context rather than part of the interleaved comparison. The selected indices come from a deterministic affine walk over the visible range; adjacent rows therefore share fewer selected tokens than a real top-k output would, and the tables below measure the streaming cost, at most a pessimistic view of inter-row cache reuse. Iterations reuse the same K/V tensors, so at 8k and 32k the working set stays L2-resident across iterations; the 128k rows exceed it. A cold-cache or streaming variant (rotating K/V and index buffers between iterations) was not measured, so the cutoffs are established in the regime described here. The `previous` provider derives the pre-tuning geometry from the shipped table logic, so the delta reproduces on a single checkout, and every cell of every table can be regenerated with a forced-geometry provider from the benchmark's command line.

The chunk kernel, which serves prefill with a cached prefix and every chunk after the first (a prefix-free single-chunk prompt takes the non-chunked kernel):

| Rank shape | KV length | Previous | Tuned | Ratio | Torch reference | Gather+FlashAttention (synthetic) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 6 Q / 1 KV | 8,192 | 2.556 ms | 2.146 ms | 0.840x | 81.8 ms | 27.4 ms |
| 6 Q / 1 KV | 32,768 | 2.978 ms | 2.334 ms | 0.784x | 81.7 ms | 31.2 ms |
| 6 Q / 1 KV | 131,072 | 3.058 ms | 2.343 ms | 0.766x | 81.1 ms | 31.2 ms |
| 12 Q / 1 KV | 8,192 | 2.621 ms | 2.436 ms | 0.929x | 81.2 ms | 27.4 ms |
| 12 Q / 1 KV | 32,768 | 2.984 ms | 2.757 ms | 0.924x | 81.3 ms | 29.7 ms |
| 12 Q / 1 KV | 131,072 | 3.079 ms | 2.837 ms | 0.921x | 82.1 ms | 29.7 ms |

The synthetic column materializes packed K/V and calls FlashAttention on the result; the backend has no such prefill route, so it shows what a packed implementation would cost, and past 32k its gather materializes about 17 GB per iteration and dominates it.

The non-chunked kernel, retuned by the same selector, measured with query rows equal to the KV length (torch-checked run):

| Rank shape | KV length | Previous | Tuned | Ratio |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 6 Q / 1 KV | 8,192 | 2.386 ms | 2.200 ms | 0.922x |
| 6 Q / 1 KV | 32,768 | 11.142 ms | 10.035 ms | 0.901x |
| 6 Q / 1 KV | 131,072 | 45.407 ms | 40.873 ms | 0.900x |
| 12 Q / 1 KV | 8,192 | 2.574 ms | 2.486 ms | 0.966x |
| 12 Q / 1 KV | 32,768 | 11.067 ms | 10.687 ms | 0.966x |
| 12 Q / 1 KV | 131,072 | 45.156 ms | 43.430 ms | 0.962x |

The TP1 rank shape (24 query heads over 2 KV heads, group size 12) was measured separately and the tuned tuple wins there as well: 4.2 to 5.0% on the chunk kernel across the three KV lengths and 1.1% on the non-chunked kernel at 8k, at 8,192 query rows. The per-program tile is KV-head independent (the KV-head count only scales the grid), which the measurement confirms.

### Query-count sweep and the 512 cutoff

The benchmark takes a query count and a forced geometry, so the same harness measured the fixed sm120 tuples against the geometry the previous selector picks at each `total_q` (KV 8,192):

| total Q | Rank shape | Table geometry | Table ms | sm120 family ms | Ratio |
|---:|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 32 | 6 Q / 1 KV | (16,32,8,2) | 0.1081 | 0.1198 | 1.108x |
| 64 | 6 Q / 1 KV | (16,64,8,2) | 0.0830 | 0.1199 | 1.444x |
| 128 | 6 Q / 1 KV | (16,64,4,2) | 0.0814 | 0.1199 | 1.474x |
| 256 | 6 Q / 1 KV | (16,32,4,2) | 0.1485 | 0.1512 | 1.018x |
| 512 | 6 Q / 1 KV | (16,32,4,2) | 0.2924 | 0.1798 | 0.615x |
| 1,024 | 6 Q / 1 KV | (16,16,1,2) | 0.3797 | 0.3764 | 0.991x |
| 8,192 | 6 Q / 1 KV | (16,16,1,2) | 2.4172 | 2.0153 | 0.834x |
| 32 | 12 Q / 1 KV | (16,32,8,2) | 0.1080 | 0.1349 | 1.249x |
| 64 | 12 Q / 1 KV | (16,64,8,2) | 0.0830 | 0.1360 | 1.638x |
| 128 | 12 Q / 1 KV | (16,64,4,2) | 0.0806 | 0.1448 | 1.796x |
| 256 | 12 Q / 1 KV | (16,32,4,2) | 0.1467 | 0.1670 | 1.138x |
| 512 | 12 Q / 1 KV | (16,32,4,2) | 0.2944 | 0.1860 | 0.632x |
| 1,024 | 12 Q / 1 KV | (16,16,1,2) | 0.3886 | 0.3619 | 0.931x |
| 8,192 | 12 Q / 1 KV | (16,16,1,2) | 2.6221 | 2.4357 | 0.929x |

The table wins short prefills and the tuned family wins at 512 and above. The 512 cutoff is the lowest measured row count at which the family wins for both shapes; the observed crossover sits in (256, 512]. The sweep points below 8,192 hold KV at 8,192 with a prefix, so every row streams the full selected budget; the 8,192 point is prefix-free with ramping visibility, and it is the only measured ordinary-prefill point, which is why the ordinary path requires 8,192 rows while the sweep-backed cutoff applies to the chunk path. Production `total_q` is a batch sum. A measured batch of 16 requests of 64 rows (1,024 rows total) ran 4.2% slower on the group-6 tuple and 6.3% faster on the group-12 tuple than the table; in that benchmark shape the per-request context also drops to about 512 tokens, so the batching effect and the shorter-context effect are not separated by this one point. The gate requires 512 rows per request on average, which keeps every measured win and sends that mixed regime to the table, and the added grid-utilization bound keeps batches whose shape the sweep did not cover off the tuned path as well; the benchmark now takes per-request KV lengths so the two effects can be measured separately later. The gap is not monotonic above the cutoff: at 1,024 rows the win shrinks to 0.9% (group 6) and 6.9% (group 12) where the previous selector switches to its large-`total_q` entry, then widens again at 8,192. The family never regresses at or above 512 in these measurements, and the CPU selector test pins both tuples at every measured query count plus the 511/512 boundary.

### Geometry ablations

Group 6 (chunk kernel, 8,192 query rows, same tensors and indices across tuples):

| KV length | (16,16,1,2) previous | (8,16,1,2) | (16,16,4,3) | (8,16,4,3) tuned |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 8,192 | 2.4177 ms | 2.6044 ms | 2.5406 ms | 2.0138 ms |
| 32,768 | 2.9819 ms | 3.4373 ms | 3.1568 ms | 2.3370 ms |
| 131,072 | 3.0229 ms | 3.4725 ms | 3.1616 ms | 2.3496 ms |

Group 12 (`BLOCK_M` cannot go below the 12 heads, so the schedule is the only axis):

| KV length | 1 warp / 2 stages previous | 2 warps / 3 stages tuned | 4 warps / 3 stages |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 8,192 | 2.6210 ms | 2.4352 ms | 2.6461 ms |
| 32,768 | 2.9812 ms | 2.7546 ms | 3.0025 ms |
| 131,072 | 3.0645 ms | 2.8119 ms | 3.0349 ms |

Compiled-kernel attributes for the ablation tuples:

| Group | Tuple | Registers/thread | Spilled values |
|---:|:---|---:|---:|
| 6 | (16,16,1,2) previous | 254 | 0 |
| 6 | (8,16,4,3) tuned | 128 | 2 |
| 6 | (8,16,1,2) | 255 | 12 |
| 6 | (16,16,4,3) | 96 | 0 |
| 12 | (16,16,1,2) previous | 254 | 0 |
| 12 | (16,16,2,3) tuned | 164 | 0 |
| 12 | (16,16,4,3) | 96 | 0 |

### End-to-end serving

NVFP4 TP2 on two GPUs of the host below, PLE host offload, CUDA graphs, chunked prefill 8,192, MTP off; random inputs at ISL 8,192 / OSL 128, 64 prompts, this branch against its exact base commit. Concurrency 1 was run three times per side with the radix cache flushed before every run:

| ISL | Revision | Median TTFT, three runs | Spread |
|---:|---|---|---:|
| 8,192 | branch | 505.6 / 505.1 / 505.2 ms | 0.5 ms |
| 8,192 | base | 511.3 / 501.6 / 504.2 ms | 9.7 ms |
| 131,072 | branch | 8,293.4 / 8,321.9 / 8,321.2 ms | 28.5 ms |
| 131,072 | base | 8,340.8 / 8,356.7 / 8,338.1 ms | 18.6 ms |

At ISL 8,192 the within-side spread reaches 9.7 ms (about 2%), larger than the expected effect, which is about 1.0 ms by construction: a prefix-free single-chunk prompt takes the non-chunked kernel, where the group-12 saving is about 0.09 ms per layer across the twelve full-attention layers. So at that shape the serving-level effect is below what the measurement resolves, in either direction. At ISL 131,072 the prompt spans sixteen chunks and every chunk after the first takes the chunk kernel, where the win is largest; every branch run is faster than every base run and the medians differ by 19.6 ms (0.24%). That is smaller than the sum of the kernel-table savings, which is expected where prefill attention overlaps other per-chunk work, and it is the regime where the change shows at serving level. The kernel tables above are the measurement of the change itself. A single concurrency-16 pair at ISL 8,192 measured TTFT 3,529.8 ms (branch) against 3,564.8 ms (base).

## Accuracy Tests

The tuned tuples change the online-softmax tile boundaries (`BLOCK_N` 32 to 16 at `total_q` 512, and the schedule elsewhere), so prefill outputs are not bitwise identical to the previous geometry. The registered tests bound the kernel against an FP32 torch reference at `atol=rtol=2e-2`, and end to end the `sglang.test.run_eval` GSM8K protocol (5-shot; the five prefix examples are held out of the 1,319-item test split, scoring 1,314; chat API, greedy decoding at temperature 0, thinking enabled) ran on an NVFP4 TP2 server built from this branch and from the exact base commit on the same two GPUs:

| Server | GSM8K |
|---|---:|
| This branch | 98.10% |
| Base commit | 97.72% |

Greedy decoding removes sampling variance; residual differences can still come from request arrival order under 16 client threads, dynamic batching, and kernel reduction order. The 0.38-point difference is in the branch's favor and sits below an approximate standard error for a difference of two runs at this sample count (about 0.55 points, treating the runs as independent; the shared prompt set makes the true uncertainty of the difference smaller than that bound, and one pair of runs cannot settle it), so the right reading is no measured regression. An earlier temperature-1.0 pair of the same protocol moved by the same margin in the other direction, which is consistent with that reading.

## Tests

`test/registered/kernels/ops/qsa/test_qsa_sparse_prefill_triton.py`, registered on the `base-b-kernel-unit` H100 suite (the test taxonomy check keeps kernel tests off the 5090 `1-gpu-small` runner), so CI covers the fallback path and the tuned branch runs whenever the file is executed on an SM120 card:

- Ordinary and chunk prefill against an FP32 torch sparse-attention reference at `atol=2e-2, rtol=2e-2`: both rank geometries, one and two KV heads, ragged batch 1/2/8, non-multiple-of-four prefixes, negative and out-of-range selected indices, deterministic replay, and side streams.
- A case per tuned group size through the real interface with 2,560 query rows at prefix 0: past the 512-row gate with no selector mock, so on an SM120 card the real selector picks the tuned tuple, the non-chunked kernel compiles and runs `BLOCK_M=8`, and rows past index 2,050 stream the full 2,051-slot budget. The case also asserts the selector's returned tuple under the production predicate.
- Chunk-path steady-state cases at prefix 2,050 covering the full 129-tile inner loop with every slot visible and valid.
- A hardware case asserting the geometry the selector returns on the running device, deriving the fallback expectation from `_get_table_prefill_config`.
- A launch-recorder case intercepting both kernels' launch objects at 513 rows through the real selector and asserting the constexpr geometry they received, so reverting either call site fails the suite on the SM120 runner (the H100 run derives its expectation from the table).

`test/registered/unit/layers/attention/test_qsa_sparse_prefill_config.py` (CPU): imports `_SM120_PREFILL_CONFIGS` and pins both tuples at every measured query count plus the 511/512 boundary, covers the `SGLANG_QSA_PREFILL_GEOMETRY` values, the Triton version gate, and the fallback path with the architecture predicates mocked, and drives the real `is_sm120_supported` and `is_sm121` predicates through mocked CUDA facts.

The existing QSA suites (`test_qsa.py`, `test_qsa_mqa_triton.py`, `test_qsa_sparse_index_bounds.py`, `test_qsa_mtp_shared_indexer.py`, compressed addressing) pass unchanged.

Compute Sanitizer memcheck, initcheck, racecheck and synccheck are clean on the benchmark's sanitizer driver: batch 1, tuned geometry, both kernels at both 8k and 128k for both rank shapes (eight cases per tool), guard-banded allocations.

## Environment

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| CPU | 2x AMD EPYC 9355 |
| GPU | 8x NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition 96 GB, sm_120a |
| Driver / CUDA | 595.71.05 / 13.2 |
| torch / Triton / FlashInfer | 2.13.0+cu130 / 3.7.1 / 0.6.17 |
| OS | Ubuntu 24.04.4, kernel 6.8 |

## Not covered

The indexer scoring and selection chain is unchanged. The chunk wrapper still derives its launch bound with a device read; removing the host reads on that path is a separate change that needs its own measurement.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). The new environment variable is documented in the environment variables reference.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

issues.title: Add DDTree speculative decoding
issues.body:
## Summary

This PR adds DDTree (Diffusion Draft Tree) speculative decoding support.

DDTree extends DFLASH-style draft execution with tree-based verification. Instead of verifying only a linear draft chain, DDTree can use a larger tree budget to verify multiple candidate branches and improve acceptance length. The worker uses `DFlashWorkerV2` for draft-worker initialization, memory pool setup, and CUDA graph handling, while keeping a DDTree-specific non-overlap decode loop for tree construction and verification.

## Changes

- Add `DDTreeWorker`, `DDTreeDraftInput`, and `DDTreeVerifyInput`.
- Add DDTree tree construction and EAGLE-format tree topology conversion utilities.
- Register `DDTREE` as a speculative decoding algorithm.
- Add `--speculative-ddtree-budget`.
- Add DDTree-specific environment knobs:
  - `SGLANG_DDTREE_MAX_TOPK`
  - `SGLANG_DDTREE_DEPTH_BONUS`
  - `SGLANG_DDTREE_RANK_PROBE`
- Support DDTree target-verify CUDA graph shapes where `draft_token_num = ddtree_budget + 1`.
- Support DDTree draft-worker CUDA graph replay with `input_embeds`.
- Make hybrid/Mamba target-verify metadata use per-request `spec_info.topk` and support DDTree tree topology tensors.
- Disable Mamba conv-window dedup for DDTree full-tree verify, where per-token tree ancestors are required.
- Route DDTree decode preparation through its own draft input state instead of the EAGLE prepare path.

## Validation

### Correctness

Tested on a hybrid GDN model with:

- Target model:  an SFT-tuned MoE model with NVFP4 quantization
- Draft model: a DFLASH draft checkpoint
- TP: 1
- Attention backend: Triton
- `max_new_tokens=512`
- `max_running_requests=1`
- strict memory check enabled

Single prompt generation succeeds:

- Output is correct
- `spec_accept_length = 1.8235`

The 40-prompt benchmark completes without scheduler exceptions or memory leak reports.

### Performance

Benchmark setup:

- Dataset: 40 prompts
- Warmup: 3 requests
- Max new tokens: 512
- Same target model, draft model, hardware, and runtime config across runs

| Method | Budget / Block | AL mean | AL median | AR mean | TPS mean |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| DFLASH | block=16 | 2.576 | 1.607 | 0.102 | 146.2 |
| DDTree | budget=8 | 2.329 | 1.605 | 0.086 | 126.2 |
| DDTree | budget=16 | 2.621 | 1.807 | 0.105 | 128.6 |
| DDTree | budget=32 | 2.750 | 1.903 | 0.114 | 119.8 |

DDTree shows clear budget scaling:

- budget 8 -> 16: AL mean improves from `2.329` to `2.621` (+12.5%)
- budget 16 -> 32: AL mean improves from `2.621` to `2.750` (+4.9%)
- budget 8 -> 32: AL mean improves from `2.329` to `2.750` (+18.1%)

Compared with DFLASH block=16:

- DDTree budget=16 improves AL mean by +1.7% and AL median by +12.4%
- DDTree budget=32 improves AL mean by +6.8% and AL median by +18.4%

As expected, larger DDTree budgets trade additional verification work for higher acceptance length.


## Contributors

Engine Architecture Group 5, Engine Infrastructure Department, Xiaohongshu (RedNote): Fei Ziyu, Luo Zhaokai, Su Zhan, Chenchen Hong, Jin Huayi.

issues.title: [Fix] Avoid FP8 descales for FA4 BF16 KV decode
issues.body:
## Motivation

With a ModelOpt FP8 checkpoint and an explicit BF16 KV cache, FA4 prefill succeeds but decode passes the checkpoint's KV scales to attention. Current FA4 rejects these arguments with `q_descale/k_descale/v_descale are only supported for FP8 inputs`.

Addresses the explicit BF16 KV configuration reported in #31640. The current FA4 interface supports FP8 descales, so the old proposal to suppress all FA4 decode descales would discard required scaling for FP8 inputs.

## Modifications

Only pass checkpoint descales to FA4 when the resolved KV dtype is FP8. Preserve query conversion and existing FA3, FP8 and MXFP8 policies.

Extend the CPU paged-MHA tests with BF16 aliases, auto, prefill/decode, and FP8 scaling checks. Reuse the dense attention fixture for a GPU regression with non-unit checkpoint scales and a BF16 KV cache, comparing both extend and decode with the reference output.

## Accuracy Tests

Tested on one NVIDIA RTX PRO 5000 72GB Blackwell (SM120), Python 3.12.3, PyTorch 2.11.0+cu129, and the repository-pinned CUTLASS DSL 4.6.2.

- Before the fix: the new GPU regression fails in decode with the FA4 descale assertion; extend passes. CPU regressions fail for both `bf16` and `bfloat16` decode.
- After the fix: `test/registered/unit/layers/test_flashattention_paged_mha.py`: **3 passed, 12 subtests passed**, with CUDA unavailable.
- Entire `test/registered/attention/unittests/dense/test_fa4.py`: **11 passed, 38 subtests passed**, including the new BF16 regression, existing layout cases, CUDA graphs and speculative decoding cases. GPU checks use the fixture's reference implementation and existing `atol=rtol=0.03`.
- All applicable pre-commit hooks pass for the three changed files.

The original B200/Nemotron-120B full-model scenario was not run. This change does not add support for any new FP8 KV configuration.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not benchmarked; this is a decode correctness fix with no kernel changes.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add regression tests using existing CPU and GPU test files.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.
- Documentation: no public API or configuration change.
- Accuracy: attention reference comparisons passed; full-model accuracy and speed benchmarks were not run.

issues.title: fix(attention): auto-split SM120 FA4 target verification
issues.body:
## Summary

- Route eligible SM120 FA4 BF16 target-verification calls through the existing
  architecture-owned decode SplitKV policy instead of the ordinary prefill
  policy.
- Forward the live maximum KV length when target verification delegates
  automatic split selection.
- Preserve ordinary prefill, deterministic inference, explicit split requests,
  non-SM120 backends, and unsupported attention variants.

## Motivation

SGLang represents target verification through `forward_extend`, so it currently
inherits the SM120 FA4 prefill policy (`num_splits=1`).  Target verification is
instead a short-query workload and can use the existing decode-side automatic
SplitKV heuristic without changing the public FlashAttention API.

## Scope

The new default applies only to SM120 FA4 with BF16 Q/K/V, causal global paged
attention, and no cascade, context parallelism, local/sliding attention, sinks,
score modification, relative bias, cross attention, softcap, or KV-cache bypass.
All other calls retain their previous policy.

This change does not add a calibration model, tuning cache, per-shape
refinement, FP8 KV support, startup hook, or configuration variable.

## Performance

Measured on three otherwise idle NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition
GPUs with paired CUDA Graph replay timing.  Each p50 contains seven alternating
batches of 256 replays.

The matrix covers BF16, head dimension 128, page size 64, one KV head, GQA
groups 6/8/16, target-verification lengths 2 through 8, and KV lengths
128/256/512/768/1024 (105 shapes total).

- 105/105 correctness comparisons passed against explicit unsplit execution.
- 61 shapes selected the exact unsplit launch plan.
- 44 shapes selected SplitKV; every one was faster than unsplit.
- Worst SplitKV/unsplit p50 ratio: 0.6662 (at least 1.50x faster).
- Selected split counts: 6, 8, 12, and 16.

By KV length, the heuristic selected SplitKV for 0/21, 0/21, 2/21, 21/21,
and 21/21 shapes respectively.

## Test plan

- `test_flashattention_paged_mha.py`: 3 passed.
- `test_flash_attention_4_sm120.py`: 55 passed.
- Registered-test metadata checker passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.

issues.title: [Fix] Run attention on a padded extend batch's real rows
issues.body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #42936
* #42898
* #42897
* __->__ #42896
* #42895
* #42894
* #42893
* #42892
* #42891

## Motivation

MLP sync pads each rank's extend batch to a multiple of attention TP (`input_ids`, `positions`, `out_cache_loc`), while the attention metadata still covers only the real tokens. The prefill CUDA graph path already runs attention on the real rows. In eager mode, though, the backends got the padded queries:

- flashinfer's paged and ragged prefill and flashinfer MLA's ragged path reject them. Qwen3-30B-A3B with DeepEP at TP 2 fails as soon as prefill runs eager, as it does by default under pipeline parallelism:
  ```
  q.shape[0] (6) does not match qo_indptr[-1] (5)
  ```
- The other backends compute only the rows their metadata covers and leave the rest of the output uninitialized.

## Modifications

- `RadixAttention` does in eager what the prefill graph path does:
  - it runs the backend on the real rows, with the cache locations and positions narrowed for the call;
  - it allocates the padded output up front, with the graph branch's allocation (`_new_attention_output`, now shared). A backend that writes into `forward_batch._attn_output` (flashattention, triton, aiter, trtllm_mha's NVFP4 output) fills the real rows in place; another backend's output is copied in. Only the padded tail is zeroed. A backend that returns more than its output (its LSE, or a sparse indexer's output beside it) returns a tuple, which is padded as it comes, so no output is allocated for that call.
- K and V go with the queries unless the caller gives them an extent of their own, the layer is a cross-attention (K and V are the encoder's), or they have a different row count. K and V that hold a cached prefix declare their extent: the chunked-prefix chunks did, and DeepSeek's one-shot MHA, whose K and V cover every token of the sequences, now does too, so they are never taken for padded rows when their row count happens to equal the padded query count.
- The other per-row inputs are narrowed with the rows they belong to:
  - `rel_bias`, `aux_tensors`, the q/k/v descales and the mxfp8 deferred norm/RoPE inputs, from the list the graph path's extra-kwargs route already narrows (`_PER_ROW_EXTRA_KWARGS`, now shared);
  - `k_rope` and the k/v descales follow K and V; a sparse indexer's `idx_q` follows the queries and its `idx_k` / `idx_v` the keys, as the prefill graph's sparse attention already narrows them (MiniMax's backend trimmed them itself only while it received the padded queries).
- The FA4 wrappers (`flash_attn_varlen_func` and `flash_attn_with_kvcache` in `flash_attention_v4.py`) pass `out=` on to the kernel. They dropped it, so FA4 allocated a second output that was then copied in; the output the prefill graph path preallocates now reaches FA4 too. Where the wrapper pads MLA query heads, or the kernel is a released flash-attn-4 build without `out=`, the result is still a new tensor.
- trtllm_mha's FMHA-v2 prefill (SM90 and SM120) also writes into the output it is given, as its other prefill kernel already did, so the padded call and the prefill graph path no longer copy a second output in.
- DeepSeek's born-FP8 query for DSA's `flashmla_sparse_q8` prefill (`SGLANG_ENABLE_DSA_Q8KV8_BORN_FP8_Q`) is prepared for every row but handed to the backend for the rows its attention call takes: the stash records the real rows of a padded extend (`padded_extend_real_tokens`, the same test the narrowing uses), which the backend reads as a prefix of the rows written.
- Target verify, which plans its padded rows itself, is left as it is.
- The real count comes from `global_num_token_non_padded_cpu`, which every batch carries.
- Kimi K3 trimmed its own attention to the real rows for the same reason, counting them from `extend_seq_lens_cpu`, which GPU-only batches leave unset. That trim is removed, together with:
  - the padded o_proj output it kept for the SP collectives;
  - the trimmed `out_cache_loc` it left on the batch.
- `test_radix_attention_padded_extend.py` covers:
  - only padded extend batches are narrowed;
  - the backend sees the real rows and the tail is zero;
  - keys with their own extent or row count, or a cross-attention's, are left whole, also when they are as long as the padded queries (a cached prefix, or encoder rows);
  - the per-row inputs follow the rows they belong to, a sparse indexer's too (each index output shaped by the query rows);
  - the output is written in place or copied, with `_attn_output` restored afterwards.

## Accuracy Tests

- Qwen3-30B-A3B, DeepEP, TP 2, deterministic inference (flashinfer), eager prefill, on B200: crashes on `main`, both with and without PP 2; runs with this change.
- `trtllm_mha` in eager prefill, which ran on the padded batch before: identical before and after.
- The output buffer handling and the per-row narrowing change no value. Qwen3-30B-A3B, DeepEP, TP 2, deterministic inference, eager prefill, 24 prompts of uneven length (every process takes the padded path 51–351 times): with the backend's own output copied in (flashinfer) or written in place (triton and fa4 on B200, fa3 on H200), input and output logprobs are bit-identical to narrowing Q, K and V alone.
- FA4 output reuse, counted at the FA4 kernel call (Qwen3-30B-A3B, DeepEP, TP 2, deterministic inference, B200), two launches per tree:
  - eager prefill: all 381 padded attention calls per process now hand the preallocated output to FA4 and get it back (none before). A padded attention call's peak memory drops from 609 KiB to 309 KiB, one real-row output (75 rows × 2048 × 2 bytes);
  - prefill CUDA graph: the 6,465 FA4 calls that have a preallocated output now write into it (none before);
  - input and output logprobs are bit-identical to before in both modes.
  - the same on an HGX B300 (SM103): the same counts and peak memory, and bit-identical logprobs in both modes.
- DeepSeek one-shot MHA over a cached prefix on a padded extend (a 4-layer DeepSeek-V3 config with dummy weights, DeepEP TP 4, flashinfer, eager prefill, `SGLANG_CHUNKED_PREFIX_CACHE_THRESHOLD=1`, B300): a 3-token cached prefix and 9 new tokens padded to 12, so K and V have as many rows as the padded queries. Without the declared extent, K and V were cut to 9 rows on every MLA layer and the greedy tokens changed; with it, the output is bit-identical to the same request without the prefix cache, in two launches.
- MiniMax-M3's sparse attention (its released config cut to 6 layers, index values on in two of the five sparse layers, dummy weights), TP 4 × DP 2 attention, eager prefill, on B300. Narrowing q, K and V without the indexer's inputs fails in `store_kv_index`, whose `idx_k` keeps the padded rows. With them narrowed, every padded call hands the backend the real rows for q, `idx_q` and `idx_v`, and the index output comes back on those rows. Sending the 24 prompts one at a time, so that each launch runs the same batches (9 of the 24 prefills padded), the greedy tokens match `main` on all 24 prompts. The logprobs differ from `main`'s by at most 0.0073; `main` differs from its own second launch by 0.0068.
- trtllm_mha's FMHA-v2 on H200 (Qwen3-30B-A3B, DeepEP TP 2, eager prefill, requests one at a time): all 192 padded attention calls per process now hand FMHA-v2 the preallocated output and get it back (none before), saving one real-row output per call; input and output logprobs are bit-identical to before.
- DSA's born-FP8 query (`SGLANG_ENABLE_DSA_Q8KV8_BORN_FP8_Q=1`, `flashmla_sparse_q8` prefill, FP8 KV cache) on H200: a DeepSeek-V3.2 config cut to 4 layers with bf16 dummy weights, TP 4 × DP 2 attention, eager prefill, 12 long prompts sent one at a time. On the padded prefill, every layer's stash records the real rows the attention call reads; stashing every written row instead fails the backend's check (`q8kv8 born-fp8 q stash mismatch: stashed (num_tokens=2082, layer_id=0) but consuming (num_tokens=2081, layer_id=0)`). Input and output logprobs are bit-identical to `main`, to the same run with the born-FP8 query off, and across two launches.
- Inkling-Small-NVFP4 with FA4's sheared relative bias, TP 4 × DP 2 attention, eager prefill on B200: narrowing Q, K and V alone fails FA4's `assert rel_bias.shape == (total_q, num_head, rel_extent)` on all four ranks; with the per-row inputs narrowed too it serves. (Inkling's output under DP attention is wrong on `main` as well, GSM8K 0.03, so that configuration has no accuracy to compare; at TP 4 this PR and `main` both score 0.74 with identical answers on the first questions.)
- Kimi K3 (synthetic, DeepEP TP 2, eager prefill, 5-token prompt padded to 6 rows), its own trim against this narrowing, per layer and per rank:
  - with the attention-residual bank: real and padded rows identical;
  - standard residual path: identical, except one launch of the trimmed tree that also differs from the trimmed tree's own second launch.
- H200 (fa3, deterministic inference), Qwen3-30B-A3B GSM8K at the top of this stack, against `main`: TP 4, TP 4 × DP 2 attention, TP 2 × PP 2, TP 4 × EP 4 DeepEP, and TP 4 × DP 4 attention × EP 4 DeepEP all give the same accuracy (0.915–0.930) and 200/200 identical answers.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: unpadded batches are unchanged; a padded eager batch now runs the backend on its real rows only, and FA4 writes into the output buffer it is given instead of allocating another.

Memory, on B300 (Qwen3-30B-A3B's config with dummy weights, DeepEP TP 2, eager prefill, deterministic inference):
- A padded attention call's own peak, 127 real of 128 rows × 2048: triton, which writes in place, 528,384 bytes, the padded output; flashinfer, whose output is copied in, 1,044,480 bytes, the padded output plus its real-row output, released at the end of the call. FA4 writes in place too (above).
- The whole run's peak allocated and reserved memory per rank is identical to `main`'s to the byte with triton and with FA4.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

issues.title: [cake_kernels] opt-in P1/P2 model routes: DeepSeek-V3 grouped routing, DeepSeek-V4 sparse MLA decode, Mamba2 SSD/SSU, SP all-gather matmul, MiniMax-H3 diffusion stages (SGLANG_CAKE_ROUTES)
issues.body:
## Motivation
Part 2 of the Cake-kernel forwarding work for sgl-project/sglang#42176: opt-in wiring of the forwarded P1/P2 Cake kernels
behind `SGLANG_CAKE_ROUTES` (introduced in #42406). Nothing changes when the switch is unset; every route admits on the
real tensors at the call site and falls back to the stock kernel with identical arguments otherwise.

> **Stacked on #42407 (`cake/09-kimi-k3-e2e`) → #42406 and on the Part 1 groups #42384, #42385, #42386 (merged into this branch).** Review only this PR's own commits (the P1/P2 route commits and the FlashInfer-main re-validation commits on top).

## Routes added (`python/sglang/kernels/cake_kernels/_routes.py`)
| route | model family | engine call site | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dsv3_grouped_routing` | DeepSeek-V3 / R1 / V3.2 | `srt/layers/moe/topk.py::biased_grouped_topk_gpu` | same positional contract as the stock FlashInfer branch; shared-expert append unchanged; FlashInfer host rejections cached per shape |
| `dsv4_sparse_mla_decode` | DeepSeek-V4 (trtllm backend, SM100/103), DeepSeek-V4.1 (SM120/121 default backend) | `deepseek_v4_trtllm_backend.py` decode / verify / varlen prefill; `deepseek_v4_backend.py` DSv4.1 mixed-cache decode | workspace-size admission, counter priming before CUDA-graph capture, grow-only split scratch (eager only); `dsv4/cake_routes.py` |
| `mamba_ssd_prefill`, `mamba_ssu` | Nemotron-H, granite hybrids (Mamba2) | `attention/mamba/mamba.py` SSD prefill and both `selective_state_update` sites via `mamba/cake_routes.py`; chunk-128 metadata built once per forward in `mamba2_metadata.py` | BF16/FP16 state, 128-multiple prefill; radix-cache track rows mapped onto the kernel's per-sequence checkpoints (`Mamba2Metadata.prepare_mixed`, chunk-aligned rows keep the engine's slot copy); calls in which every sequence is a single chunk-128 keep the stock kernel (see below); promoted SSU rows only |
| `sp_all_gather_matmul` | Llama-3.1-70B (`--enable-layernorm-sp`) | `srt/layers/layernorm_sp.py::column_parallel_g_matmul` | prepared / functional all-gather+matmul for unquantized BF16 participants; cached K-major weight copy; `LlamaForCausalLM` accepted as an SP architecture only while this route is selected. The FlashInfer kernel requires torch's **NVSHMEM** symmetric-memory backend: the route selects it in `distributed/bootstrap.init_parallel_runtime` (before the first symmetric allocation), the adapter admission checks it, a FlashInfer `ValueError` is a cached refusal, and torch's fused symm-mem SP ops are disabled for the process once NVSHMEM is selected (they cannot allocate under that backend). `SGLANG_CAKE_SP_CHECK=1` recomputes the stock all-gather + matmul per call and compares at BF16 tolerance (diagnostic) |
| `minimax_h3_diffusion` | MiniMax-H3 DiT (`multimodal_gen`) | `dits/minimax_h3.py` block stages via `minimax_h3_cake_routes.py` | per-stage admission (bf16 pre-attention pack, dense varlen attention, out-proj + gated residual, fc1 SwiGLU); GEMM stages only after an eager warm-up launch. Measured on MiniMax-H3 FL2VA t2va (1× GB200, 768p / 4 s / 8 steps): the attention stage is admitted on all 352 DiT calls, the GEMM stages on none (the engine's AdaLN tables have 6 or 3 rows, the FlashInfer stages require 9); e2e time unchanged (19.9 s vs 19.9 s), +0.9 GB peak; the Cake attention matches FlashAttention-4 within BF16 tolerance on the real shapes but is not faster, so the route stays opt-in |
| `dsa_indexer`, `msa_nvfp4_sparse_decode` | DeepSeek-V3.2 indexer, MiniMax-M3 | registered, **not wired** | engine contract mismatch (paged FP8 indexer logits / exact-shape dense-MQA plans; no NVFP4 KV pool for the MiniMax sparse path) — stock paths untouched |

Route logging: the first "taken" and the first fallback of every distinct reason are logged once per route
(`[cake-route] <route>: …`), so an e2e run can prove which kernel executed and why a batch did not take Cake.

## Tests
- New CPU unit tests (mocked adapters/forwarders; route off → stock with the exact kwargs; on + admitted → Cake with the
  contract arguments; rejected / inside capture / FlashInfer host rejection → stock, logged once):
  `test_cake_deepseek_routes.py` (21), `test_cake_mamba_sp_routes.py` (26), `test_cake_minimax_routes.py` (17).
- Gate on this branch head: ruff check/format, isort, codespell, whitespace clean; 68 new + 189 existing kernel-namespace
  tests pass.

## Model e2e (this round)
- **Nemotron-H-8B-Reasoning-128K BF16, TP1, 1× GB200**, `--mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16` in every arm.
  - Default server configuration: baseline vs `mamba_ssu,mamba_ssd_prefill` vs `mamba_ssd_prefill` → GSM8K-200
    0.890 / 0.895 / 0.895, decode 335.6 / 2454 / 7540 tok/s (bs 1/8/32) in every arm, bitwise-identical logprobs.
    **The Cake kernels did not run**: plain-decode SSU (T=1, headdim 64) has no promoted Cake row, and the SSD prefill
    route is rejected because the engine requests Mamba radix-cache track states on every prefill (not mapped onto the
    Cake checkpoint contract).
  - `--disable-radix-cache` in both arms (the SSD route admits 128-multiple prefills): GSM8K-200 0.890 → 0.885 / 0.900;
    single 1024-token request prefill **24.0k → 27.7k input tok/s, TTFT 42.6 → 37.0 ms**; bs 8/32 prefill within
    1.4 %; decode identical (SSU stock); serving (200 × 1024/128, conc 32) 36.4k → 37.0k tok/s with TTFT medians
    404 → 354 ms (serving TTFT is noise-dominated at this size: identical-kernel arms spread 277–408 ms). Greedy texts
    identical; a 1024-token input-logprob probe shows the kernel difference (mean |Δ| 0.035). Route log:
    `[cake-route] mamba_ssd_prefill: Cake kernel selected (x=(1, 1024, 128, 64)/bfloat16 …)`.
  - Kernel-level A/B at the model shape (stock Triton SSD vs the Cake route helper, random inputs, BF16 state): Cake is
    1.5–2.0× faster (0.25 vs 0.50 ms at 1024 tokens) and not bitwise: max |Δ| one bf16 ulp at |out| ≈ 90, mean |Δ| 0.0077;
    against an fp32 recurrent reference 1.5 % of outputs fall outside atol/rtol 1e-2 vs 0.6 % for the stock kernel (tracked
    internally; the route stays opt-in).
  - **Radix cache ON (follow-up commits in this PR)**: the engine's Mamba track-state requests are now mapped onto the Cake
    checkpoint contract, so the SSD route admits tracked 128-multiple prefills with the default server configuration
    (route log `Cake kernel selected (x=(1, 1024, 128, 64)…)`; GSM8K 200/50/50 q baseline 0.875/0.880/0.840 vs route
    0.895/0.900/0.860; fixed-prompt logprobs identical). A prefix-hit probe (1024 cached tokens + a 128-token extend) then
    returned all-NaN logits on the route arm; isolated at the kernel level to any call in which every sequence is exactly
    one chunk-128 (random *and* zero initial states, NaN count varies per call; batches with a ≥ 2-chunk sequence are
    clean). The route keeps the stock kernel for that geometry (host extend lengths; logged once) and the probe is clean
    again (same greedy ids as the cold run, max |Δlp| 0.0009 on the outputs); the kernel defect is tracked separately.
- **DeepSeek-V4-Flash FP8, TP4, 4× GB200** (`--dsv4-attn-backend trtllm --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`, FlashInfer mHC kernels in both arms):
  baseline GSM8K 0.970 vs `dsv4_sparse_mla_decode` **0.020** — an e2e correctness regression. The route was taken on the
  SWA-only, c4 and c128 layers and on the varlen-prefill site; the eager (`--disable-cuda-graph`) arm scores the same, so
  it is not a capture/replay issue. An env-gated in-engine A/B (`SGLANG_CAKE_DEBUG_DSV4_AB`, this PR) re-runs the stock
  kernel on the identical tensors: returning the stock output restores GSM8K 0.980 with logprobs identical to the
  baseline, while the Cake output differs by up to 12–17 (abs) with 12–79 % of elements outside the FP8 tolerance. A
  standalone repro shows the upstream Cake SM100 kernel attends every column up to `sparse_topk` regardless of
  `sparse_topk_lens` (a poisoned tail beyond `lens` leaves the stock output bit-identical and destroys the Cake output)
  and does not apply the `seq_lens` sliding-window validity; FlashInfer's own hardening suite passes at the pin. Tracked
  upstream; **the route stays opt-in and must not be enabled until the FlashInfer fix lands.** Graph-batch rows also fall
  back on the compressed layers (workspace 1.1 GB > the 128 MiB engine buffer).
- **DeepSeek-V3.2-NVFP4, TP4, 4× GB200**: `dsv3_grouped_routing` is unreachable on this checkpoint — the
  `flashinfer_trtllm` MoE runner fuses the router (`BypassedTopKOutput`), so both arms ran identical kernels (GSM8K 0.970,
  bitwise-identical logprobs).
- **DeepSeek-V3-0324 FP8, TP4, 4× GB300** (real weights): under the engine default (`--moe-runner-backend auto` resolves
  to `flashinfer_trtllm` for DeepSeek-V3 fp8 on sm100) the route is likewise unreachable (0 route lines, arms bitwise
  identical, GSM8K-400 0.940 vs 0.938). With `--moe-runner-backend triton` in both arms the route is taken on every rank:
  GSM8K-400 0.935 → 0.945, every e2e metric within ±1 % (the router is microseconds per layer), memory equal. The arms are
  not bitwise identical (1024-token input logprobs: mean |Δ| 0.15 nat); a per-call stock-vs-Cake check inside the route
  (`SGLANG_CAKE_DSV3_ROUTING_CHECK=1`, eager) over 1.0 M routed rows per rank shows identical expert ids and order in
  every row and weights within one FP32 ulp of the stock FlashInfer router, while two identical stock servers are bitwise
  equal — the drift is the chaotic amplification of that rounding through 61 MoE layers, not a kernel defect. Perf-neutral,
  no production path uses it on sm100/sm103 while the default runner fuses routing; the route stays opt-in.
- MiniMax-H3: one e2e A/B on 1× GB200 (above); no video-quality eval in this round — frames differ from the stock run by
  ≈26 dB PSNR against a 36.8 dB stock run-to-run baseline, consistent with trajectory divergence from bf16 rounding-order
  differences (kernel outputs within tolerance), not certified quality-neutral.
- Llama-3.1-70B SP: GPU run on the real architecture with seeded dummy weights (1 node × 4 GB300, TP4, `--load-format dummy`,
  stock no-SP baseline vs the route): the prepared packed-QKV launcher is admitted for qkv (inp 2048×8192 bf16, weight 2560×8192,
  world 4), the per-call Cake-vs-stock check is bit-identical (1151 calls per rank, 19.7 G elements, max abs diff 0), and the
  arms' greedy tokens / logprobs are identical (256/256 tokens, 1023 input logprobs, max diff 0). e2e perf is **not** positive
  in this configuration: selecting the route forces the NVSHMEM symmetric-memory backend, under which sglang's custom
  all-reduce cannot allocate and falls back to NCCL (steady decode throughput ×0.77–0.80 at bs 1/8/32), and the prepared
  launcher is refused inside prefill CUDA-graph capture, so captured prefills run the stock SP path (TTFT ×0.99–1.02). Model
  quality on the real BF16 weights is not measured (checkpoint not reachable from the cluster). Keep the route opt-in.
- MiniMax-M2/M3: wiring + CPU tests only; MiniMax-M2 needs an NVFP4 checkpoint (none public: the warp-decode runner is
  NVFP4-only) and MiniMax-M3's MSA route needs an NVFP4 KV pool the engine does not have.

## FlashInfer main re-validation (`58171ea83f32185a7990cfc15c969ecf79bb406c`)
The Mamba2 SSD / SSU, SP all-gather+matmul and MiniMax-H3 contracts changed on FlashInfer main (any-seqlen exact-scan SSD
with token-major output and FP32 state, promoted headdim-64 SSU row, all-gather+matmul on the engine's `[N, K]` weight view
with any row count, MiniMax-H3 stages on the engine's native operands). The top commits move the three routes to those
contracts; the stock paths are untouched and the adapters keep every admission check the new kernels require. Re-measured
with FlashInfer main in the same container:

- **Nemotron-H-8B BF16 TP1, 1× GB200, radix cache ON, GSM8K-200 0.885 in all arms.** The SSD route now runs on every
  prefill of ≥ 128 tokens (log `Cake kernel selected (x=(1, 795, 128, 64) …)`); packed batches shorter than 128 tokens stay
  on the stock kernel (the FlashInfer host builds a fixed 128-row TMA token box and rejects shorter inputs — logged fallback,
  tracked upstream). `mamba_ssd_prefill`: bs1 prefill 22.5k → **28.9k input tok/s (TTFT 45.5 → 35.5 ms)**, bs32 prefill
  80.7k → 88.3k, decode unchanged, serving 36.3k → 38.1k tok/s. `mamba_ssu,mamba_ssd_prefill`: bs32 decode 7589 → **8380
  tok/s**, serving **40.1k tok/s**, TPOT 4.27 → 4.21 ms. Prefix-hit probes (1024+128, 1536+256): same greedy ids, no NaN.
  Kernel-level A/B at the model shape (random inputs, 128…1152 tokens, with/without initial states): Cake 0.12–0.15 ms vs
  stock Triton 0.42–0.55 ms (3.3–3.8×); against an fp32 recurrent reference 0.58–0.75 % of outputs fall outside atol/rtol
  1e-2 vs 0.55–0.70 % for the stock kernel (same accuracy class); the FP32-state Cake path gives bit-identical outputs to the
  BF16-state path, so the engine-default `--mamba-ssm-dtype float32` no longer silently receives BF16 states.
- **Llama-3.1-70B architecture (seeded dummy weights) TP4 `--enable-layernorm-sp`, 1× 4 GB300.** The route now covers both SP
  projections (packed QKV `N = 2560` and gate_up `N = 14336`) with the weight read in place; per-call Cake-vs-stock check
  (eager arm): 9101 calls per rank, 0 outside BF16 1e-2 over 4.2e11 elements, max |Δ| 1.2e-7; cross-arm logprobs identical.
  End to end unchanged by the re-pin: decode ×0.78–0.81, serving ×0.86, TTFT ×0.88, TPOT ×1.17 — the kernel still requires the
  NVSHMEM symmetric-memory backend, which moves the custom all-reduce onto NCCL (tracked upstream). Keep the route opt-in.
- **MiniMax-H3 FL2VA t2va, 1× GB200, 3 alternating stock/Cake pairs + stock A/A.** All four stages now run on Cake at the real
  shapes (350/350 pre-attention, 352/352 attention, 350/350 out_proj, 350/350 fc1 per run; 3- and 6-row AdaLN tables, int64
  indices, strided q/k/v); generate time 19.4–19.7 s vs 19.8–20.0 s stock; peak memory +484 MB; frame PSNR vs the paired
  stock run 26.2 / 21.6 / 27.6 dB against a 27.8 dB stock run-to-run band (two of three pairs inside it).

## Not changed
No FlashInfer kernel numerics, no default-path changes, no tolerance changes. Kernel-side shape/API gaps found while wiring
are tracked internally.
