issues.title: fix(inkling): translate unified-memory checkpoint destinations to physical slots
issues.body:
## Motivation

On the unified memory pool the scheduler hands out virtual Mamba slot ids, while the Inkling short-conv kernels write checkpoints to physical slots. #41144 fixed the main path by rewriting `forward_batch.mamba_track_indices` in place to a physical buffer. Two gaps remain:

- `commit_conv_state_after_mtp_verify` passes the scheduler's virtual `mamba_track_indices` to the verify scatter untranslated. DSPARK on the unified pool reaches it.
- The EAGLE draft-extend CUDA-graph runners do not pass checkpoint destinations. As a result, the captured graph writes the draft model's conv checkpoint into reserved slot 0 instead of the intended checkpoint slot, while eager draft extend writes to the correct slot. This PR makes the captured graph write to the intended checkpoint slot as well. This issue is not specific to unified memory.

The in-place rewrite also assumes one backend prepares each batch. When several do, as multi-layer EAGLE does with one draft backend per step, every backend after the first translates the already-physical ids again (`v2p[v2p[v]]`). Main currently rejects `--enable-unified-memory` with speculative algorithms other than DSPARK, so serving does not reach this today; keeping the batch virtual removes the hazard instead of relying on that restriction.

## Modifications

- `ForwardBatch.mamba_track_indices` stays virtual. `InklingShortConvAttnBackend` translates it into a fixed-address int64 buffer it owns and stores the physical ids in `InklingShortConvMetadata.track_cache_indices`. All Inkling checkpoint consumers (fused and unfused, decode, extend and draft extend) read that field. The static pool keeps the identity path. #41144's in-place rebind and its buffer are removed.
- `commit_conv_state_after_mtp_verify` translates the checkpoint destinations, as the GDN backend already does.
- Both EAGLE draft-extend runners allocate a checkpoint-destination buffer when `enable_mamba_extra_buffer` is set, pass it at capture, staging and replay, refresh live ids on replay and zero only the padded rows. The ordinary runner folds the refresh into its grouped copy. Helpers live in `speculative/draft_checkpoint.py`.
- Draft extend no longer runs the prefill-style track scatter. It writes its accepted-window checkpoint in its own cache update, and the inert prefill scatter would overwrite that destination during capture.
- GPU regression tests cover real allocator compaction, physical checkpoint writes, graph replay, repeated metadata preparation across backends, strided ids, padding, disabled tracking, buffer bounds and the verify commit.

## Accuracy Tests

Validated on an NVIDIA B200 against main `048b2a07f3`, with this PR rebased onto it; the end-to-end runs also include #39982 and #42072.

- `test_inkling_checkpoint_indices.py`: 17 tests and 29 subtests pass. The 33 related existing test files give the same results as main.
- The draft-extend checkpoint path is specifically covered by `test_draft_runners_capture_and_replay_checkpoint_destinations`, which checks checkpoint destinations during CUDA graph capture and replay.
- Inkling (`thinkingmachines/Inkling`, revision `test`), `--enable-deterministic-inference`, 32 LongBench prompts: logprob match, prefill cache hit and decode cache hit are at `avg_kl_div=0.0` on the static, lazy and unified pools, and multi-layer EAGLE MTP (two heads) on the static pool is at 0.0 as well. `test_inkling.py` passes 5/5 and `test_inkling_unified.py` 9/9.
- Inkling-Small NVFP4 + DSPARK, TP4, static pool: all three KL checks at 0.0.
- Unified pool + DSPARK: main allows only the triton attention backend for this pairing, and its prefill and decode are not bit-identical here (`avg_kl_div=0.116` with no cache hit, the same on main and with this PR), so the end-to-end KL check cannot isolate the verify-commit translation. The unit test above covers it.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Speculative accept length over the same workloads, read from the decode log (main / this PR):

| Setup | main | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| Inkling MTP, multi-layer EAGLE, static pool | 2.736 | 2.736 |
| Inkling-Small NVFP4 + DSPARK, TP4, static pool | 2.118 | 2.118 |

Per step, the unified pool adds one translate and an int64 copy of at most `bs` entries; the ordinary draft-extend runner folds its refresh into the existing grouped copy, and the multi-layer runner adds one copy.

### Follow-up: shared-prefix checkpoint restoration

Compared the merge parent (`1e490772e5`) with the merged fix
(`1d02a36bb7`) on 12 varied inputs. Eight baseline cases had draft
acceptance below 100%.

| Shared-prefix result | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Aggregate draft acceptance | 72.67% (452/622) | 73.06% (453/620) |
| Aggregate completion tokens / verify calls | 768/311 (2.4695) | 768/310 (2.4774) |
| Proof case: verify calls for 64 output tokens | 30 | 29 |
| Proof case: draft acceptance | 55.00% | 58.62% |

The proof-case change reproduced in five additional cache-flush/reseed
repetitions per revision. Its cold control required 29 verify calls on
both revisions. All paired output token IDs matched between revisions.

<details>
<summary>Setup and limitations</summary>

RTX 5090 / WSL, reduced 8-layer Inkling test checkpoint, FA4, static
pools, extra_buffer, page/track interval 128, and two-head multi-layer
EAGLE with draft-extend CUDA graphs. Both revisions used the same
SM120 MoE compatibility override and diagnostic instrumentation.

Each seed generated 640 tokens. Follow-up requests reused a generated
768- or 896-token checkpoint with exactly one uncached input token.
Logs confirmed draft graph replay and checkpoint restore calls for
both draft pools.

The five proof-case repetitions were selected after the initial
comparison and were not independent server replicates.

Results were not uniformly positive: a separate 8-token continuation
experiment used 49 verify calls on both revisions, with accepted drafts
changing from 48/98 to 47/98. Two inputs had warm/cold output differences
identically on both revisions; their causes remain unestablished.

These results demonstrate a small, workload-specific acceptance
improvement, not a general throughput gain.

</details>

issues.title: [Qwen 3.8 Flash Next] Add sm120 (RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell) support
issues.body:
#36497 merged into `main` through #37500 on 2026-09-08, so this branch now sits on `main` (rebased at `9c8d4641f`) with no external dependency. The commits listed below are the whole diff.

On sm120 the model from #36497 does not serve as written. The QSA sparse decode path is gated on `is_sm100_supported()` and falls back to a packed gather plus a FlashAttention varlen call; the QSA MQA indexer scoring runs TileLang with a silent torch fallback; and the JIT modules are built during graph capture. The PLE host-load path also performs a wasted row-zero read on non-owner ranks (correct output, unnecessary PCIe traffic). This PR adds the sm120 paths: a direct-paged Triton sparse decode with a fused split-K merge, Triton MQA scoring, a fused small-row NVFP4 MoE kernel in the in-tree CUDA JIT, sm120 launch geometry for the hyperconnection mix, tuned FP8 fused-MoE configs for this GPU, NUMA-interleaved pinning for the offloaded PLE table, and correctness fixes for the items above. With this branch both checkpoints serve with CUDA graphs and NEXTN speculative decoding: FP8 at TP4/EP4 and NVFP4 at TP2/EP1.

## Motivation

sm120 is the workstation and consumer Blackwell architecture (RTX PRO 6000, RTX 5090, GB10 at sm_121). The QSA decode kernels this model depends on exist only for sm100: trtllm-gen has no sm120 cubins, so the gate is closed and the fallback gathers the selected tokens into a packed buffer before every attention call. Two day-0 reports describe the same gap: #36531 (the QSA fallback selects the pip FA4 path on sm120 and fails at the MLIR build) and the GB10 comment on #36497 asking to widen the sm100 gate. #36532 (FlashInfer GDN wanted fp32 state on sm120 while flag validation accepted bf16) is covered on `main` itself now, which converts the prefill state to fp32 on sm12x and ships the pooled bf16 decode kernel with FlashInfer 0.6.18, so the GDN commit this PR carried before the rebase is dropped.

Widening the gate was measured and is not the right fix: `trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache` with `backend="auto"` routes compute capability below 10 to XQA, and forcing `backend="trtllm-gen"` fails at `fmhaRunner.cuh:37: Unsupported architecture`. XQA cannot address the paged pool directly, so it pays a page-aligned gather that costs more than the attention itself at large batch (measured below). The contribution here is a direct-paged kernel that skips the gather at large batch and splits along the top-k axis to reach XQA-class latency at small batch.

The irregular sparse-attention and gather paths are Triton: sparse decode, MQA scoring and the PLE gather have shape-dynamic index expansion where the compile keys are the fixed head and page tiles, not the sequence lengths. The quantized MoE GEMM is an in-tree sgl-kernel CUDA JIT kernel because it is a fixed-layout `mma.sync.kind::mxf4nvf4` grouped GEMM with the architecture and model shape as compile keys. FlashInfer stays in place everywhere it owns the full production contract on sm100, including the NVFP4 MoE above 16 tokens, which remains the fallback.

## Modifications

Eleven commits, oldest first (hashes omitted; see `git log`).

| Subject | What it does |
|---|---|
| [QSA] Add direct-paged Triton sparse decode on sm120 | Reads the selected tokens straight from the paged KV pool through the request table. `SGLANG_QSA_DECODE_BACKEND` selects `auto`/`triton`/`flash_attn`/`trtllm`; `auto` picks Triton on sm120 (excluding sm121) and trtllm-gen where it exists. The MQA counterpart `SGLANG_QSA_MQA_BACKEND` accepts `auto`/`tilelang`/`triton`/`torch`. |
| [sm120] Fix serving fallbacks and graph capture | Masks the PLE host load for non-owner ranks, makes the MQA path recoverable through `SGLANG_QSA_MQA_BACKEND` instead of dropping to torch silently, prewarms the Qwen4Exp JIT kernels before graph capture. |
| [MoE] Add tuned fused MoE configs for RTX PRO 6000 | Triton 3.7.1 FP8 blockwise configs for E=64/128/256 at N=640, the EP8/EP4/EP2 layouts of this model. |
| [QSA] Add split-K sparse decode for small batches | Two-stage split along the KV axis with the 12 grouped query heads packed into M; the split count is a static function of query rows so graph capture stays valid. |
| [QSA] Add Triton MQA scoring on sm120 | Packed-prefill and direct-paged decode/verify scoring for the indexer; default on sm120, sm100 keeps TileLang. |
| [QSA] Fuse split-K merge into sparse decode | The last program per row merges the partial softmax states with a graph-safe counter reset, removing the separate reduction launch. |
| [PLE] Interleave the pinned table across NUMA nodes | Allocates the offloaded PLE table with `mmap` + `numa_interleave_memory` + `cudaHostRegister` instead of `pin_memory=True` so it does not exhaust the NUMA node local to the GPU. Goes through the `allocate_ple_host_table` backend switch that `main` gained with the file-backed table (pinned branch only; the mapping is read back with `ple_pinned_mapping`). Opt-out env provided. |
| [HC] Tune sm120 Triton geometry by row bucket | Picks grid and tile from the static row count (1, 2-16, 17-64) on sm120; other architectures keep the previous choice. |
| [MoE] Add fused small-row NVFP4 kernel for sm120 | One cooperative JIT launch per layer for 1-16 routed tokens: W4A4 quantize, FC1, SiLU-mul with group-16 requantization, grouped FC2, routing-weight finalize, all in checkpoint layout. Falls back to FlashInfer CUTLASS when cooperative launch or occupancy is not provable; above 16 tokens CUTLASS is unchanged. |
| [QSA] Bound sparse indices and use 64-bit KV addresses | Prefill kernels bound the selected index by the request's own extent; decode, compaction and decode MQA compute slot-times-stride products in 64 bit. |
| [PLE] Select the prefetch buffer from capture state | Asks the driver for the capture state instead of trusting a runner flag that some graph runners never set; keeps the mmap reachable until device work finishes. The prewarm reads the resolved graph config and draft width from the runtime context bags, since the worker's record only carries the raw flag value (found by @detain while running the stack on `main`). |

New environment variables, all declared in `environ.py` with defaults that preserve non-sm120 behavior: `SGLANG_QSA_DECODE_BACKEND`, `SGLANG_QSA_MQA_BACKEND`, `SGLANG_PLE_OFFLOAD_NUMA_INTERLEAVE`, and `SGLANG_NVFP4_MOE_SM120` (a kill switch for the small-row kernel, default on; turning it off restores the FlashInfer CUTLASS path everywhere).

New registered tests: `kernels/ops/qsa/test_qsa_sparse_decode_triton.py`, `kernels/ops/qsa/test_qsa_mqa_triton.py`, `kernels/ops/qsa/test_qsa_sparse_index_bounds.py`, `kernels/ops/moe/test_nvfp4_moe_sm120.py`, `unit/models/test_qwen4_ple_prefetch_buffers.py`, `unit/utils/test_interleaved_pinned_table.py`, `unit/layers/moe/test_nvfp4_smallm_dispatch.py` (CPU), an extension of `unit/layers/moe/test_fused_moe_triton_config.py` (CPU), plus additions to the existing QSA, PLE offload, PLE table, hc_mix and cuda graph tests. The three kernel benchmarks live under `test/manual/kernels/benchmark/` (they need an sm120 GPU and, for the MoE one, local checkpoint tensors, so they are not registered CI jobs).

## Environment

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| CPU | 2x AMD EPYC 9355 |
| GPU | 8x NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition 96 GB, sm_120a |
| Driver / CUDA | 595.71.05 / 13.2 |
| torch / Triton / FlashInfer | 2.13.0+cu130 / 3.7.1 / 0.6.17 |
| OS | Ubuntu 24.04.4, kernel 6.8 |

PCIe workstation host, no NVLink; measured GDDR7 bandwidth 1.459 TB/s; two unequal NUMA nodes (257.6 GB and 128.9 GB), which is why the NUMA commit exists.

## Accuracy Tests

Every serving and accuracy number below was measured at the branch tip. Sampling for `sglang.test.run_eval`: T=1.0, top-p 0.95, top-k 20, max tokens 32768, thinking on. Server: CUDA graphs, NEXTN 3 steps / 4 draft tokens, PLE offloaded to host.

| Task | n | Checkpoint and layout | Score |
|---|---:|---|---:|
| GSM8K | 1314 | FP8, TP4/EP4 | 98.10% |
| GSM8K | 1314 | NVFP4, TP2/EP1 | 97.87% |
| AIME26, reference protocol (8 passes, 131k max tokens) | 30 | FP8, TP4/EP4 | 96.25% |
| GPQA | 198 | FP8, TP4/EP4 | 80.81% |
| GPQA | 198 | NVFP4, TP2/EP1 | 78.28% |
| IFEval | 541 | FP8, TP4/EP4 | prompt strict 0.9316, inst strict 0.9508 |
| IFEval | 541 | NVFP4, TP2/EP1 | prompt strict 0.9057, inst strict 0.9365 |

The NVFP4 model card publishes 98.75% for AIME26 under the 8-pass protocol; the 96.25% above is the FP8 checkpoint under the same protocol (per-pass spread 93.3 to 100; repeated 8-pass runs during development landed between 96.3 and 98.3). Multimodal observations exist but their protocols are not all matched to published ones, so they are not claimed as comparisons.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

### QSA sparse decode

Isolated kernel benchmark at the model's full-attention shape: 24 query heads, 2 KV heads, head dim 256, bf16, 2051 selected-token slots per row, page size 64 for the gathered paths, ragged valid counts. CUDA events around the complete call, 10 warmups.

| Query rows | flash_attn packed fallback (ms) | XQA end to end (ms) | XQA kernel alone (ms) | Triton direct paged (ms) | + split-K (ms) | + fused merge, head (ms) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 0.0633 | 0.0377 | 0.0181 | 0.0901 | 0.0363 | 0.0318 |
| 4 | 0.0772 | 0.0374 | 0.0183 | 0.0912 | 0.0363 | 0.0314 |
| 16 | 0.0767 | 0.0417 | 0.0184 | 0.0917 | 0.0367 | 0.0361 |
| 64 | 0.5489 | 0.5476 | 0.1848 | 0.1985 | 0.1991 | 0.1992 |

The final column carries a 3-4 us cost at small rows over the pre-review revision of this kernel; it combines a defensive reinitialization of the split-K reduction generation with a retuned split schedule, and still beats every fallback at every row count. At 64 rows the split count is 1, so the last two columns both run the non-split kernel and their near-identical times are expected. The XQA column is what widening the sm100 gate would select: at 64 rows it spends 0.363 ms of 0.548 in the gather, and its 1-16 row numbers are optimistic because the gathered working set stays L2-resident across benchmark iterations. Numerics against an fp32 reference stay at the bf16 output-rounding floor (max abs 0.000477 to 0.007577 across 1-64 rows); eager calls are bitwise reproducible and captured graphs replay with zero drift. The split-K path is clean under Compute Sanitizer memcheck, initcheck, racecheck and synccheck with guard bands, across capture and replay.

### QSA MQA indexer scoring

Decode scores a 32k source sequence (8192 compressed keys); prefill is one causal packed sequence. CUDA events, 2 warmups.

| Point | Query rows | torch (us) | TileLang (us) | Triton (us) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| decode batch 1 | 1 | 95.7 | 16.6 | 17.7 |
| decode batch 16 | 16 | 130.3 | 15.5 | 16.6 |
| decode batch 64 | 64 | 727.1 | 37.9 | 29.4 |
| prefill 8k | 8192 | 1297.3 | 132.7 | 73.5 |
| prefill 32k | 32768 | 21841.9 | 3221.6 | 1083.4 |

TileLang keeps a 2-4 us edge at decode batch 1-16; Triton wins at batch 64 and both prefill points and removes both the third DSL and the silent torch fallback from the sm120 path. Max abs logit error against torch is 2.4e-6 and all selected top-k sets matched exactly, including rows below the 512-block budget.

### NVFP4 small-row routed MoE

Layer 0 real checkpoint tensors, TP2 rank 0, 512 local experts, hidden 2560, rank-local intermediate 320, top-k 10. One MoE call per captured graph, 30 repeats, 256 MiB L2 flush per sample.

| Tokens | FlashInfer CUTLASS median (us) | This PR median (us) | Median change |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 72.1 | 45.1 | 37.4% faster |
| 4 | 111.6 | 84.5 | 24.3% faster |
| 16 | 216.1 | 195.1 | 9.7% faster |

Both GEMMs stay W4A4 group 16; relative L2 error against fp32-dequantized weights matches FlashInfer to the third decimal (0.1375 vs 0.1377 at 16 tokens). Graph capture replays all three shapes with stable workspace addresses.

### Hyperconnection mix and FP8 MoE configs

hc_mix: a captured graph of 97 mix calls with distinct weights runs 5.0/5.4/20.8% faster at 1/16/64 rows (13.93 us per call at one row); max abs error is unchanged and 10,000 replays show no drift. The tuned FP8 fused-MoE configs reduce the isolated TP4/EP4 chain from 37.05 to 24.04 us at one token and 0.5-3.3% at 16-2048 tokens; the same chain measures 22.94 us against 49.90 us on FlashInfer CUTLASS per-tensor FP8 and 57.39 us on the CuTe-DSL sm12x grouped MoE from flashinfer PR 4720. E=512/N=160 (TP4 without EP) is rejected by the FP8 quantization layer before any config selection: the per-partition gate-up output size 160 is not divisible by the weight quantization block size 128, so no config exists for it.

### End to end serving

`sglang.bench_serving`, random dataset, ISL 1024 / OSL 512, CUDA graphs on, PLE offloaded to pinned host memory. Each row issues more prompts than its concurrency window, so median TTFT includes scheduler queueing for the requests beyond the window: NEXTN drains the window roughly twice as fast at concurrency 16, which is why its TTFT drops there, while at concurrency 64 the draft-extend prefill overhead dominates and TTFT rises.

FP8, TP4/EP4:

| Concurrency | Spec | Output tok/s | TPOT med (ms) | TTFT med (ms) | Accept len |
|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | none | 115.8 | 8.41 | 101.1 | |
| 16 | none | 873.8 | 16.27 | 1066.7 | |
| 64 | none | 1682.2 | 32.42 | 2719.9 | |
| 1 | NEXTN 3/4 | 220.6 | 4.40 | 109.9 | 2.92 |
| 16 | NEXTN 3/4 | 1111.4 | 12.47 | 216.9 | 2.98 |
| 64 | NEXTN 3/4 | 1754.2 | 25.01 | 3836.6 | 3.05 |

NVFP4, TP2/EP1 (two GPUs matching the four-GPU FP8 numbers is expected here: decode is weight-bandwidth-bound, NVFP4 halves the streamed weight bytes, and tensor-parallel traffic over PCIe scales poorly, so fewer ranks lose little):

| Concurrency | Spec | Output tok/s | TPOT med (ms) | TTFT med (ms) | Accept len |
|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | none | 124.7 | 7.83 | 95.2 | |
| 16 | none | 855.7 | 16.84 | 974.8 | |
| 64 | none | 1666.7 | 33.18 | 2552.4 | |
| 1 | NEXTN 3/4 | 216.0 | 4.56 | 101.8 | 2.94 |
| 16 | NEXTN 3/4 | 1069.2 | 13.20 | 194.5 | 3.00 |
| 64 | NEXTN 3/4 | 1703.1 | 25.22 | 3711.8 | 3.02 |

Reference point at the #36497 head `73a255206` on the same host: FP8 TP4/EP4, eager, no MTP, concurrency 1, 17.4 output tok/s at 57.21 ms median TPOT; a baseline for "it serves at all", not a like-for-like graph comparison.

The NUMA commit is what lets the NVFP4 NEXTN configuration start with the PLE table offloaded: `pin_memory=True` put both TP2 ranks' 47.7 GiB on the 128.9 GB node local to GPUs 4-7, the node went into reclaim and the driver failed with Xid 31 MMU faults at a host address during the draft load. Interleaved, each rank spreads 23.8 GiB evenly across both nodes and startup completes; single-stream throughput is about 2 percent below a GPU-resident table, the expected cost of PCIe reads.

## Rebase notes (2026-09-16)

Rebased from the #36497 head onto `main` at `9c8d4641f`. Besides the GDN commit drop and the PLE allocation change described above, the QSA tests sit in `test/registered/kernels/ops/qsa/` following the test layout consolidation (#39966), and the tree is formatted with ruff-format as the pre-commit config now asks. CPU verification on the rebased tree: the touched CPU suites pass (61 tests, 51 subtests). GPU check of the rebased tree on a DGX Spark (GB10, sm_121) on 2026-09-17: file-backed PLE boots and serves with defaults, with the Triton QSA kernels forced on, and with NEXTN (table in the comments). The exact-sm120 numbers above are from before the rebase; @detain reports the pre-rebase stack running on 4x RTX PRO 6000 Workstation Edition together with #37275, #38144, #38209 and #36644 (see the #37275 thread). An sm120 re-run of the rebased tree follows when a card frees up.

## Not covered

- **FP8 KV cache.** `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` still asserts in the QSA path (#36545); neither checkpoint requests it. Separate PR.
- **QSA prefill.** Decode is direct-paged; prefix and chunked prefill still gather more than they need. Separate PR.
- **RealWorldQA.** Under the official Qwen3-VL protocol (exact prompt, 602K-4M pixel smart resize, thinking recipe, rule-plus-judge extraction, all 765 items) scores 86.4-87.2 against the published 88.5; runs with NEXTN off and with rejection sampling land in the same band, so speculative decoding is excluded as the cause and the residual gap is still being investigated as an evaluation-protocol or serving-numerics question, not claimed as a kernel result.
- **CI coverage.** The registered kernel and GPU unit tests use the `base-b-kernel-unit` suites, as the test taxonomy check asks, and those run on H100/B200/H200 runners, so the sm120-gated tests skip there; the architecture-independent parts do run. The `1-gpu-small` runner is a 5090 (SM120), but no kernel-unit suite is defined on it. If maintainers want the sm120 paths exercised in CI, a `base-b-kernel-unit-test-1-gpu-small` suite would do it and I can wire the registrations to it.
- **Other sm120 parts.** Only RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition was measured. RTX 5090 (sm_120) should take the same paths but is untested here. GB10 (sm_121) keeps upstream defaults everywhere: the backend auto-selection does not route it onto the new Triton QSA paths (the env vars allow an explicit opt-in), and the small-row NVFP4 kernel refuses it and falls back to CUTLASS.
- **Adoption instead of duplication.** sglang #28125, #36043, #34827 and flashinfer #4720/#4718 overlap with the FP8 MoE and NVFP4 GEMM area. The tuned Triton FP8 configs here are an interim path; when one of those lands with the checkpoint's scale format and wins on the full routed chain, it should replace them.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).

issues.title: [diffusion] attention: add fp8_fa_sm120 FP8 backend for SM120 GPUs
issues.body:
## Motivation

SM120 GPUs (GeForce RTX 50, RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell) have FP8 tensor cores, but the diffusion
runtime has no FP8 attention path for them. On SM120 the default is Torch SDPA, and BF16
attention there is already near the hardware ceiling: cuDNN SDPA reaches 95% of the measured
BF16 mma.sync peak on an RTX 5080. The only way to go faster on these cards is lower precision.

On MiniMax-H3 (56 heads, head_dim 128, S=30272) attention is about 47% of the GPU time of a
denoise step, so this is where an FP8 kernel pays off.

This PR adds `fp8_fa_sm120`: an opt-in attention backend around an FP8 (E4M3) flash-attention
forward written in CuTe-DSL for SM120.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/fp8_fa_sm120/`
  - `kernel.py`: the CuTe-DSL kernel. E4M3 QK and PV with FP32 accumulation, online softmax in
    registers, two-stage K/V prefetch so the copy overlaps the math, probabilities packed to
    E4M3 inside registers (no shared-memory round trip), 128 x 32 CTA tile.
  - `fused_prep.py`: two Triton passes that quantize strided BF16 Q/K/V views per head straight
    into the kernel buffers (amax, then pack). No FP32 intermediates, no layout copy.
  - `plan.py`: one compiled kernel plus its buffers per (S, H, strides, scale, device).
    `bind_inputs()` rebinds storage, so all DiT layers share one compilation.
- `multimodal_gen/runtime/layers/attention/backends/fp8_fa_sm120_attn.py`: the backend. Handles
  `forward` and `forward_varlen` (including the MiniMax-H3 trailing-padding packing). Falls back
  to cuDNN SDPA for causal, batch > 1, head_dim != 128, non-BF16 and non-SM120 calls, and logs
  each fallback reason once.
- `AttentionBackendEnum.FP8_FA_SM120` and a resolver in `platforms/cuda.py`. Nothing selects the
  backend automatically.
- Docs: two rows in `sglang-diffusion/attention_backends.mdx`.
- Tests: `multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_fp8_fa_sm120_attn.py` (skipped unless an SM120 GPU is
  present).

No new dependency: `nvidia-cutlass-dsl` and Triton are already required.

Limits: dense, non-causal, batch 1, head_dim 128, BF16 inputs. The device gate is SM120 only.
SM121 can get the same kernel later, but I have no SM121 hardware to test on, so it is not part
of this PR. Each new sequence length compiles once (about 10 s). The plan keeps E4M3 copies
of Q/K/V plus the output buffer (about 1.1 GB at S=30272, H=56), shared by all layers.

The kernel structure (tiled mma.sync, online softmax, register accumulators) follows the NVIDIA
CuTe FlashAttention-2 example. The TMA layout, swizzle and K/V scheduling choices were informed by Blake Ledden's CuTe-DSL FlashAttention-2 port for SM120 (NVIDIA/cutlass#3030), which was also the public FP8 reference on this hardware before the FlashInfer kernel landed; thanks to Blake for walking me through its design. 

The closest existing FP8 kernel for these GPUs is `fmha_v2_prefill_sm120` in FlashInfer. The diffusion runtime does not call it. It is the FP8 reference in the tables below.

## Accuracy Tests

Per call, against cuDNN SDPA BF16 on the same inputs (H=56, D=128, normally distributed
synthetic Q/K/V): relative RMS 0.0535 to 0.0539 at S=20440 and S=30272. The FlashInfer FP8 kernel
lands in the same band on the same inputs, so the error is the price of E4M3 Q/K/V, not
something specific to this kernel.

End to end, MiniMax-H3 Ref2VA, 768x768, 107 frames, 50 steps, seed 42, RTX PRO 6000:

| clip pair | PSNR (dB) | SSIM |
|---|---:|---:|
| stock Torch SDPA vs stock cuDNN SDPA (noise floor between two BF16 backends) | 22.9 | 0.82 |
| `fp8_fa_sm120` vs stock cuDNN SDPA | 19.75 | 0.707 |

So the FP8 clip sits about 3 dB below the spread between two stock BF16 backends. Subject,
composition and motion are the same and the clip is sharp. I did not find a visible artifact,
but this is a lossy backend and that is why it is opt-in only. Clips are deterministic across
pods (the cuDNN clip from two different pods is bit-identical).

Unit tests (7) cover: output against cuDNN at two sequence lengths including a masked tail,
plan reuse across calls and across impl instances, H3 trailing-padding varlen, multi-segment
varlen, causal fallback, and resolution by name.

Frames 0, 53 and 106 of the two clips, cuDNN SDPA on top and `fp8_fa_sm120` below. The full clips
are attached under the image.

<!-- drag pr/artifacts/h3-frames-cudnn-vs-fp8_fa_sm120.png, h3-cudnn-sdpa.mp4 and h3-fp8_fa_sm120.mp4 here -->

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Kernel only, H=56, D=128, non-causal, CUDA events, 20 warmup, 5 x 10 iterations, times in ms.
cuDNN SDPA, Torch SDPA and FA4 have no FP8 path on SM120, so their BF16 kernels are the production
baseline this backend replaces. FlashInfer `fmha_v2_prefill_sm120` is the only other FP8 attention
kernel for these GPUs, so it is the FP8 reference.

RTX 5080:

| S | `fp8_fa_sm120` (FP8) | FlashInfer `fmha_v2_prefill_sm120` (FP8) | cuDNN SDPA (BF16) | Torch FlashAttention-2 SDPA (BF16) | SGLang FA4 SM120 (BF16) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 30272 | 123.6 | 131.8 | 226.2 | 245.4 | 251.8 |
| 20440 | 57.0 | 60.4 | 106.5 | 112.4 | 115.5 |

RTX PRO 6000:

| S | `fp8_fa_sm120` (FP8) | FlashInfer `fmha_v2_prefill_sm120` (FP8) | cuDNN SDPA (BF16) | Torch FlashAttention-2 SDPA (BF16) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 30272 | 43.7 | 53.7 | 73.7 | 74.4 |
| 20440 | 19.9 | 25.0 | 32.3 | 34.2 |

End to end on MiniMax-H3 Ref2VA (768x768, 107 frames, 50 steps, RTX PRO 6000, same pod, v0.5.19
tag with stock pins): 6.87 s/it with `torch_cudnn_sdpa`, 5.61 s/it with `fp8_fa_sm120` (-18.3%).

issues.title: [docs] Qwen-Image-2.1 cookbook: ComfyUI sections, trimmed examples, and the RTX 5090 DiT-resident recipe (1.42x)
issues.body:
Consolidates three open cookbook PRs into one, because two of them edit the same
line of the Qwen-Image-2.1 picker and would have conflicted whichever merged
second.

Supersedes #35468, #40457 and #40525.

## 1. A ComfyUI section on every diffusion cookbook page (was #35468)

Adds `docs/src/snippets/diffusion/comfyui-support.jsx` and a four-line
`<ComfyUISupport model="…" />` include to each page, so the per-model facts
(server node, `integratedKey`, workflow file) live in one place and stay in sync
with the plugin instead of being restated per page.

**Coverage gap to settle before merge:** the branch was opened in August and
main has grown since. 15 of the 26 pages under `docs/cookbook/diffusion/` now
carry the section; the 8 model pages added since (Qwen-Image-2.1, LTX-2.5,
LongCat-Image, SANA-Video, SenseNova-U1.5, LingBot-Video-MoE, LTX2 & LTX2.3)
do not. Adding them is not mechanical — each needs an `integratedKey` that
matches `executor_class_dict` in the plugin plus a real workflow filename — so
this PR either grows those entries or the title narrows.

## 2. Trimmed Qwen-Image-2.1 example commands (was #40457)

Drops defaults from the emitted curl and shortens the RTX 4090 residency recipe
to `--component-residency text_encoder=layerwise-offload`.

**The shortening was verified, not assumed.** `--component-residency`'s help
says components without an assignment "keep their automatic placement", which
reads as though dropping `dit=resident vae=resident` could let the DiT be
offloaded. It does not. Measured on one RTX 5090, 1024x1024 / 40 steps / seed 42,
five requests per arm:

| GPU | recipe | p50 | s/step | VRAM after load |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| RTX 5090 | `dit=resident text_encoder=layerwise-offload vae=resident --warmup-resolutions 1024x1024` | 14.136 s | 0.3173 | 24891 MiB |
| RTX 5090 | `text_encoder=layerwise-offload` | 14.115 s | 0.3173 | 24891 MiB |
| RTX 4090 | `dit=resident text_encoder=layerwise-offload vae=resident --warmup-resolutions 1024x1024` | 18.668 s | 0.4208 | 20598 MiB |
| RTX 4090 | `text_encoder=layerwise-offload` | 18.673 s | 0.4201 | 20598 MiB |

Identical per-step time and byte-identical memory footprint on both cards — the
automatic placement lands on the same arrangement. The 4090 matters here because
it is the card whose documented recipe this shortens, and it is the tighter of
the two at 24 GB.

## 3. The RTX 5090 gets the DiT-resident recipe (was #40525)

The picker gated that branch on `s.hw === "rtx4090"`, so an RTX 5090 fell through
to `--dit-layerwise-offload true` and streamed the 13.25 GiB DiT through every
one of the 40 steps. Streaming only the Qwen3-VL encoder — which runs once per
request — is much faster, and it fits: the 5090 has 8 GB more than the 4090 that
already used this recipe.

| RTX 5090 recipe | p50 | s/step | steady VRAM |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--dit-layerwise-offload true` (before) | 19.95 s | 0.4674 | 19.3 GB |
| the DiT-resident recipe (after) | **14.12 s** | **0.3166** | **17.0 GB** |

**1.42x faster on less steady memory.** Each arm repeats to 0.1% and the two do
not overlap; peak during load rises to 24.9 GB, still inside 32 GB. Both arms
return a PNG of identical byte length, consistent with placement leaving the
output alone.

The condition also becomes `effectiveAttention(s) === platformAttention(s)` so
each card keeps its own kernel: FlashAttention on the 4090, Torch SDPA on the
5090's sm120, where an `fa` request already falls back to SDPA.

## What actually changes

Resolving the patched config across every hardware x attention combination and
diffing against `main` gives five changed selections and nineteen untouched:

```
rtx5090 platform|fa|sdpa
  - --performance-mode manual --dit-layerwise-offload true
  + --performance-mode manual --component-residency text_encoder=layerwise-offload
rtx4090 platform|fa
  - --performance-mode manual --component-residency dit=resident text_encoder=layerwise-offload vae=resident --warmup-resolutions 1024x1024
  + --performance-mode manual --component-residency text_encoder=layerwise-offload
```

RTX 5090 with SageAttention keeps the DiT-layerwise path (unvalidated
combination), and every RTX PRO 6000, DGX Spark, H200 and B200 selection is
unchanged.

Docs-only; no runtime code is touched.

issues.title: [docs] Qwen-Image-2.1: give the RTX 5090 the DiT-resident offload recipe (1.42x)
issues.body:
## What

The Qwen-Image-2.1 picker gates its DiT-resident offload branch on
`s.hw === "rtx4090"`, so an RTX 5090 falls through to
`--dit-layerwise-offload true` and streams the DiT through every denoising step.
Keeping the DiT on the card and streaming only the Qwen3-VL encoder — which runs
once per request — is substantially faster there, and it fits: the 5090 has 8GB
more than the 4090 that already uses this recipe.

## Measurement

One RTX 5090, 1024x1024, 40 steps, seed 42, guidance 1, `output_format: png`,
one output. Same box, same checkpoint snapshot (`b3179ad3`), same Torch SDPA,
sglang `6ad78f2`. Only the component placement differs, and placement does not
change numerics.

| RTX 5090 recipe | p50 | s/step | steady VRAM | peak at load |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--dit-layerwise-offload true` (current) | 19.946 s | 0.4674 | 19.3 GB | 19.3 GB |
| `--component-residency dit=resident text_encoder=layerwise-offload vae=resident` | **14.082 s** | **0.3166** | **17.0 GB** | 24.9 GB |

**1.42x faster on less steady memory.** Each arm repeats to 0.1%
(`[19.97, 19.95, 19.95]` and `[14.14, 14.08, 14.08]`) and the two do not overlap.
Peak during load rises to 24.9 GB, still well inside 32 GB. Both arms return a
PNG of identical byte length (2,432,136), consistent with placement leaving the
output alone.

## Scope of the change

The condition becomes `effectiveAttention(s) === platformAttention(s)` so each
card keeps its own kernel: FlashAttention on the RTX 4090, Torch SDPA on the
5090's sm120 (where an `fa` request already falls back to SDPA).

I resolved the patched config across every hardware x attention combination and
diffed it against `main`. Exactly three selections change, all of them RTX 5090
on SDPA:

```
CHANGED rtx5090 att=platform|fa|sdpa
  - --performance-mode manual --dit-layerwise-offload true
  + --performance-mode manual --component-residency dit=resident text_encoder=layerwise-offload vae=resident --warmup-resolutions 1024x1024
21 other selections unchanged
```

RTX 5090 with SageAttention still takes the DiT-layerwise path (that combination
is unvalidated), and every RTX 4090, RTX PRO 6000, DGX Spark, H200 and B200
selection is byte-identical to before.

## Context

This came out of a cross-hardware benchmark of Qwen-Image-2.1 on B200 / H200 /
RTX 5090 / RTX 4090. The 24 GB RTX 4090 was landing within 1.4x of the 32 GB
RTX 5090, which is what pointed at the recipe rather than the silicon — the 4090
was already on the better one.

Docs-only change; no runtime code is touched.

issues.title: [diffusion] model: support qwen-image-2.1
issues.body:
## Motivation

Add native Qwen-Image 2.1 text-to-image generation and editing, including multiple reference images and RGBA input/output. SGLang owns the model components and preserves the checkpoint's Transformers 4.57.3 conditioning semantics.

## Modifications

- Add the DiT, RGBA VAE, Qwen3-VL conditioning, model registration, and CLI/server integration.
- Align conditioning and VAE normalization with [Diffusers #14804](https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers/pull/14804): training image markers, white alpha compositing for vision only, empty-prompt handling, pre-final-norm text features, and FP32 VAE normalization.
- Integrate request-scoped prefix caching, Cache-DiT, breakable CUDA graphs, TP/Ulysses/Ring/CFG parallelism, encoder sharding, VAE parallel decoding, component/layerwise offload, and adapter mapping.
- Add complex RoPE, Q/K normalization, and scale-only LayerNorm fusions with first-call equality checks and native fallbacks. Detect the running CUDA build's complex multiplication FMA order for Hopper and Blackwell.
- Scope vision RoPE recomputation after device transfers to Qwen-Image 2.1, preserving the existing MiniMax-H3 encoder behavior.
- Add `qwen_image21_t2i_tp2` for the two-GPU E2E suite (temporarily disabled until the checkpoint is accessible to fork PR CI): 1024×1024 PNG, 40 steps, CFG 1, seed 42, two consecutive requests, model API and pinned image-consistency checks. Reference image (merged): [ci-data-diffusion #7](https://github.com/sgl-project/ci-data-diffusion/pull/7).
- Add unit, CUDA, distributed, and supplemental full-checkpoint HTTP tests; update compatibility/quantization docs and the hardware-aware cookbook command picker.
- Add verified single-RTX PRO 6000 resident/offload recipes and retain non-default picker selections when a shared configuration link is refreshed.

## Speed tests

Incremental Q/K normalization on one B200 (resident, FlashAttention, eager, 1024×1024, 40 steps, seed 42, CFG 1; four fresh starts in new/base/base/new order, two warmups per start) reduced median generation latency from 3.114 to 2.828 s (9.17%; 10 samples per variant) and editing from 3.742 to 3.450 s (7.81%; six samples per variant).

The subsequent scale-only LayerNorm change reduced median generation latency from 2.831 to 2.748 s (2.92%) and editing from 3.436 to 3.358 s (2.26%), with identical corresponding output pixels. These measurements predate the latest conditioning correction and apply only to the tested commits/workload; they are not a new accuracy baseline.

On one RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (96GB, SM120), corrected implementation `1eab5de5990` passed 1024×1024/40-step HTTP generation, editing, transparent generation, and repeated transparent-input editing with Torch SDPA. Resident generation/edit medians were 8.23/9.85 s with 40.1 GiB peak device memory; DiT offload measured 10.28/10.66 s and 26.1 GiB. All 13 corresponding RGBA outputs matched exactly across placements; 156 kernel/model tests passed (21 skipped). Multi-GPU and NVFP4 recipes on this GPU remain unverified.

## Checklist

Regression validation on two H200 GPUs at `2d7c5365fb0`: all 41 focused vision/Qwen tests passed, including exact CPU/GPU RoPE checks and the real component-offload path. Two consecutive H3 ref2va requests produced six sampled frames identical pixel-for-pixel to main `9784d5f979c9`; the previous PR head differed on every sampled frame. Both main and the corrected branch remain below the H100 reference-image SSIM threshold on this H200 environment, so this comparison establishes parity with main rather than an upstream H100 consistency pass. Reference images and thresholds are unchanged.

- [x] Format code with pre-commit; validate documentation and links.
- [x] Add unit, distributed, and HTTP tests; retain the temporarily disabled TP2 E2E definition.
- [x] Verify strict RoPE equivalence on Hopper and Blackwell.
- [x] Correct VAE input layout and validate transparent editing against Transformers 4.57.3.
- [x] Complete the corrected-conditioning LayerNorm feature matrix.
- [x] Pass upstream lint with the consolidated kernel-test taxonomy.
- [ ] Complete upstream NVIDIA CI.

The TP2 E2E case is temporarily disabled in `6078c9049b3` after [upstream CI returned HTTP 401 during checkpoint loading](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35321287777/job/105600776865). The case configuration, scheduling estimate, and pinned reference image are retained for re-enabling it when the checkpoint is accessible to fork PR CI. Earlier isolated B200 TP2 consistency tests passed.

issues.title: [Qwen3.8] Fix FP8 KV cache support in QSA
issues.body:
## Summary

- support FP8 KV cache in QSA normal and chunked prefill by widening cached K/V to the query dtype and applying the per-layer KV descales
- dequantize compacted FP8 cache into query-dtype scratch buffers for the FlashAttention fallback, while preserving FP8 cache buffers for the TRT-LLM decode path and passing its BMM descales
- use per-layer scales when writing the KV cache without mutating the K/V tensors still consumed by initial prefill
- keep the existing BF16 paths compile-time separated, and add focused coverage for FP8, non-unit scales, fallback, decode, and cache writes

Addresses the remaining prefill/chunk-prefill FP8 path related to #36545.

## Context

With an FP8 KV cache, a long cached chunk-prefill request reaches the QSA Triton kernel with BF16 queries and FP8 cached keys/values. `tl.dot` then rejects the mixed input dtypes. PR #36806 fixes the exact-SM120 QSA sparse-decode routing and supersedes the broader SM12x routing proposed in #36556. That decode-path fix does not dequantize FP8 QSA cache entries consumed by normal or chunked prefill; this PR covers that orthogonal data path.

This PR is stacked on #36497 because the Qwen3.8/QSA implementation is not on `main` yet.

## Validation

- `pre-commit run --from-ref 73a255206f --to-ref d2c8b42cb1`: all hooks passed
- existing QSA GPU suite on RTX 5090 (SM120): `52 passed`
- new focused QSA FP8 KV GPU suite on RTX 5090: `7 passed`
  - normal prefill and cached chunk prefill against a dequantized reference
  - non-unit K/V descales
  - BF16 regression path
  - FlashAttention fallback compaction and native TRT-LLM decode scaling
  - scaled cache writes preserve the original prefill tensors
- real checkpoint smoke test: `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4`, TP=8 on 8x RTX 5090, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`
  - FP8 K/V cache allocated successfully
  - decode CUDA Graphs captured for batch sizes 1, 2, 4, and 8
  - WikiText-103 50k-token request after a 45k-token prewarm: 44,992 cached tokens (89.984%) and successful generation
  - 8 concurrent distinct-suffix requests and an 8-concurrent cached replay both completed; the server reported an 8-request decode batch with CUDA Graph enabled

- fresh current-base RED/GREEN revalidation ([full setup and results](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36644#issuecomment-5466422753)) on `qwen4-main-squashed` `99c9362` (including #36806), 4x RTX 5090, TP=4, and real WikiText-103 token IDs
  - RED: a 45,000-token prewarm failed in `_sparse_gqa_chunk_prefill` at `tl.dot(q_values, keys)` with `Unsupported rhs dtype fp8e4nv`
  - GREEN: the same prewarm passed; a follow-up 50,000-token request reused 44,992 cached prompt tokens (89.984%) and generated successfully

The original TP=8 end-to-end worktree additionally carried #36556. The fresh TP=4 RED/GREEN revalidation instead used the current base `99c9362`, including #36806. Both sides of each A/B carried the same unrelated ModelOpt NVFP4 MoE TP-padding loader fix required to load this particular exported checkpoint; none of those auxiliary changes are included in this PR. The checkpoint exposes unit/default KV scales, while non-unit scale behavior is covered by the focused kernel tests above.

## Accuracy

Full official GSM8K A/B (`python -m sglang.test.run_eval`, all 1,314 examples, Chat API, thinking disabled, temperature 0, max 512 output tokens, concurrency 8) on the same patched source, checkpoint, and TP=8 host; only `--kv-cache-dtype` changes:

| Metric | BF16 KV | FP8 KV | FP8 delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Correct / 1,314 | 1,265 | 1,261 | -4 |
| Accuracy | 96.2709% | 95.9665% | -0.3044 pp |
| Output throughput (tok/s) | 437.24 | 437.84 | +0.14% |

The paired result agrees on 1,298/1,314 examples (98.78%): 1,255 are correct under both KV dtypes, 43 are wrong under both, 10 are BF16-only correct, and 6 are FP8-only correct. A two-sided exact McNemar test on the 16 discordant examples gives p=0.45, so this run does not show a statistically significant task-accuracy difference. The focused GPU tests separately compare normal and cached chunk-prefill FP8 outputs against a dequantized reference with non-unit K/V scales.

## Serving performance

Controlled A/B on the same patched source, model, 8x RTX 5090 host, and exact WikiText-103 token-ID prompts; each setting contains 16 requests and only `--kv-cache-dtype` changes:

| Workload / metric | BF16 KV | FP8 KV | FP8 delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1k input / 1k output, c=8, output tok/s | 764.50 | 764.44 | -0.01% |
| 50k input / 400 output, 89.98% cache hit, c=1, output tok/s | 99.79 | 100.25 | +0.46% |
| same c=1, TTFT p50 / p90 (ms) | 928 / 1,001 | 925 / 961 | -0.28% / -3.95% |
| 50k input / 400 output, 89.98% cache hit, c=8, output tok/s | 255.21 | 257.25 | +0.80% |
| same c=8, TTFT p50 / p90 (ms) | 4,299 / 8,751 | 4,284 / 8,684 | -0.37% / -0.76% |

The same long-context BF16 workload before vs. after this patch was -0.44% at c=1 and +1.17% at c=8, showing no measurable BF16 regression. FP8 increased allocated KV capacity per GPU from 762,496 to 1,440,320 tokens (+88.9%). The unpatched 50k / 90%-hit FP8 case crashes in the QSA mixed-dtype dot before producing a comparable result, so these numbers are intended as a regression guardrail rather than a broad speedup claim.

## Integration note

Commit `d2c8b42cb1` applies cleanly to the current `qwen4-main-squashed` head `99c9362` (including #36806). The controlled RED/GREEN revalidation above reproduces the failure on the base and passes with this commit. The full changed-file pre-commit suite passes, and the four files changed here pass the same hooks.

issues.title: [multimodal] Add SM120 Triton attention backend
issues.body:
## Motivation
Diffusion currently falls back to Torch SDPA on SM120 consumer Blackwell GPUs because FlashAttention is unavailable in this build. This PR exposes an explicit `sm120_triton_attn` backend that reuses SRT's Triton extend-attention kernel path and its SM120 block-size tuning.

## Changes
- Add `AttentionBackendEnum.SM120_TRITON_ATTN` and wire it through CUDA backend selection with an SM12.x hardware guard.
- Allow DiT configs to opt into `sm120_triton_attn`.
- Add a diffusion attention backend wrapper using `extend_attention_fwd(skip_prefix=True)` for dense self-attention and Torch SDPA fallback for non-CUDA or cross-attention cases.
- Add unit coverage for CLI/backend selection and a 5090-only benchmark test that compares `sm120_triton_attn` with `torch_sdpa`.

## Validation

issues.title: [Config] Round 5.1: the published-side readers ask the bags, and a platform fact gets one address
issues.body:
## Motivation

Round 4 got `arg_groups` to the point where resolution never writes a field on
`ServerArgs`: handlers *declare* what they decide, and `publish()` projects the
result into read-only config bags. The reader side was still half-converted —
runtime code read raw `server_args` fields, two production names existed only so
tests could patch them, and a platform fact such as "this box is SM100" had one
copy per importing module, so it could only be stated to one reader at a time.

That last one had already cost a round-4 CI failure (the module choosing an
attention backend and the module validating the choice held different copies of
the same fact) and was blocking the per-model split in #37087.

This PR finishes the reader side. Part 2 is **#37087**, stacked on this branch;
merge this one first.

## Modifications

Ten commits, each standing on its own.

1. **The last two patch seams leave the module.** `attention_backends_of` (3
   patch sites) and `supports_mamba_cache_extra_buffer` (2). Both are stated as
   inputs now — the first reads three backend fields, and those fields are what
   the tests wanted to control anyway.

2. **86 function-local `runtime_context` imports across 48 files become eager.**
   Lifting all of them, then importing each affected module *first* in a fresh
   interpreter, found 16 that broke; the pass runs to a fixed point with a
   revert-on-failure step, ending at 86 → 4. The 4 that stay are real cycles
   (`eplb/expert_distribution` ×2, `musa/flashattention_backend`,
   `moe_runner/flashinfer_trtllm`).

3. **81 runtime reads across 27 files ask the bags**, and `_apply_fields` — the
   last channel through which anything wrote back onto the record — is closed.
   The criterion is not "can this field be mapped" but "has the reader's process
   published yet": the launcher's own pre-publish reads (172 across 9 files) stay
   on the record.

4. **A platform fact gets one address.** `from ... import is_cuda` binds a *copy*
   into each importing module; `get_platform().is_cuda` puts the value in one
   object, so one `override_platform(...)` reaches every reader. The probes in
   `utils/common.py` remain the only real implementation — this is their address,
   not a second copy.

5. **The sm-family probes follow**, plus `device_sm` / `device_capability`, which
   are not yes/no facts but want the same override.

6. **The KV-events descriptor leaves the record** — 117 lines of published-side
   description move to where the published config lives.

7. **`configure_logger` reads the record it was handed** — a defect introduced by
   commit 3 and fixed here (details under Accuracy Tests).

8. **83 remaining device-probe reads in `arg_groups` go through the address.**
   This is what makes #37087 possible: a family that moves to its own module
   takes its probe reads with it, and a module-scoped patch would have to move too.

9. **Parameters nobody reads leave the signatures** — functions that kept a
   `server_args` argument they no longer name, dropped with the argument at every
   call site.

10. **Per-worker placement goes back to being read per worker.** Two readers
    converted in commit 3 decide which GPU a worker draws on, which the standing
    rule routes through a constructor argument rather than the config tier.

New tests: `test_platform_context.py`, `test_pre_publish_readers.py`,
`test_platform_address_not_frozen.py`.

## Accuracy Tests

No kernel or model-forward code is touched; this changes where configuration
values are read from. The equivalent check is that the resolved configuration is
unchanged:

- **62-shape resolution probe: IDENTICAL.** Each shape runs `resolve_once()` +
  `check_server_args()` and the full resolved configuration is compared field by
  field, along with the exception type and message. Identical on the branch tip
  and on each of the ten commits individually.
- **Every registered unit test file run on its own**, branch and base, comparing
  the two failure sets: **0 regressions** — every failure on the branch is also
  on `main`.
- **A real server boots and serves**: Qwen3-0.6B to `/health`, then a `/generate`
  round trip.

Three defects were found this way rather than by the suite, and each has a guard:

- `configure_logger` (commit 7) runs before `publish`, and `multimodal_gen` calls
  it with a `ServerArgs` that never publishes these bags. Reading
  `get_observability()` took the server down on **every** launch while the whole
  CPU suite stayed green, because every unit test publishes first. Caught by
  booting a server; `test_pre_publish_readers.py` now derives the protected set
  from `_launch_subprocesses` and drives each callee against an unpublished
  context.
- Four module-scope bindings (`_is_sm120 = get_platform().is_sm120` and three in
  `fp8_utils`) read the fact once at import and kept it, so an override could not
  reach them and the answer depended on import order — the substitution *looked*
  converted without being converted. `test_platform_address_not_frozen.py` fails
  on any module-scope `x = get_platform().y`.
- `sparsity/factory.py` still read `hisparse_config` off the record after the
  write-back closed, which turned a registered `base-a-test-cpu` test red.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The probes behind `get_platform()` are `@lru_cache(maxsize=1)`; a call measures
**26.2 ns**. The reads this replaces were module-level constants, so the change
is one cached call per decision instead of an attribute load, off the per-request
path. Resolution time is unchanged — the 62-shape probe runs in the same time
before and after.

No change to the forward path, the scheduler loop, or any kernel.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

Commit 3 is where the risk is; commits 7 and 10 are its two escapes. Three
questions to ask of any reader it converted, in this order, because each one
caught a real defect: **when does this run**, **whose record is it holding**, and
— for the reads it did *not* convert — **did closing the write-back just break
this one**.

Merge this before #37087. The repo force-deletes heads on merge and auto-retargets
children to `main`, so #37087's base needs checking afterwards.

issues.title: [Kernel] Route large SM90 row/column-scaled FP8 GEMMs to Torch
issues.body:
## Summary

Follow-up to [#33275](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33275), which added MiniMax-H3 and its online FP8 transformer path.

The current `sgl_kernel.fp8_scaled_mm` is slower than Torch `_scaled_mm` on the larger H3 dense shapes on SM90. This PR adds both implementations to `BaseFusedOp` and routes shapes using:

`(K >= 5376 and N >= 3584) or (K >= 3584 and M >= 8192)`

The AOT kernel remains the fallback for smaller shapes. The Torch path requires FP8 E4M3FN inputs, BF16 output, FP32 row/column scales, compatible layouts, and no bias.

## Kernel results

H100 80 GB, median of 10 measurements after 5 warmups:

| Operation | M × K × N | SGLang AOT | Torch | Reduction | Torch TFLOP/s |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Attention QKV, TP1 | 8320 × 5376 × 21504 | 2036.7 µs | 1351.1 µs | 33.66% | 1424 |
| MLP gate/up, TP2 | 8320 × 5376 × 14336 | 1321.9 µs | 896.4 µs | 32.19% | 1431 |
| MLP gate/up, TP1 | 23216 × 5376 × 28672 | 7823.2 µs | 5295.9 µs | 32.30% | 1351 |
| MLP gate/up, TP1 | 15760 × 5376 × 28672 | 4892.1 µs | 3570.9 µs | 27.01% | 1361 |
| MLP down, TP1 | 8320 × 14336 × 5376 | 990.0 µs | 843.9 µs | 14.76% | 1520 |

The sweep covered all 64 H3 dense shapes across TP1/2/4/8 and four production sequence lengths. Torch won 49 shapes, AOT won 15, and the heuristic selected the measured winner for all 64.

## Full MiniMax-H3 result

H100 ×8, TP2/Ulysses4, FP8, FlashAttention, 768×1120 FL2VA request with 49 denoising steps. Medians from three matched runs after two warmups:

| Metric | AOT only | Routed | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Inference | 30.213 s | 27.955 s | -7.47% |
| Wall time | 31.076 s | 29.068 s | -6.46% |
| Peak memory | 35,254 MB | 35,254 MB | unchanged |

The matched outputs were byte-identical. All eight profiler traces confirmed the routed path while retaining AOT for smaller shapes.

## Newer GPUs

I only have access to SM90 hardware, so the capability gate is intentionally limited to SM90. Help benchmarking and tuning these shapes on SM100/SM120 would be appreciated. Torch `_scaled_mm` may also win there

Full prefill CUDA graphs currently cannot replay pipeline-parallel stages. The runner has no graph-stable storage for pipeline inputs, does not pass those inputs to non-first stages, and rejects pipeline proxy outputs.

## Modifications

- Add token-major pipeline proxy buffers for full-prefill graph capture and replay.
- Register pipeline inputs with the prefill graph buffer registry so live inputs are copied and padded safely.
- Preserve global attention-layer indexing on partitioned pipeline stages.
- Pass graph-stable pipeline inputs to non-first stages and trim pipeline outputs to the live token count.
- Add unit coverage for layer alignment, buffer allocation, registry filling, and output trimming.
- Add a dedicated two-GPU FullCG test under `test/registered/cuda_graph/full_prefill/` while retaining the existing generic PP canary test.
- Replay a 47-token PP prompt through the 64-token prefill bucket with the normal FullCG decode path enabled, and assert that the request actually uses the prefill graph.

## Accuracy Tests

No numerical kernels or model math are changed. The two-GPU end-to-end test passes with KV canary checks enabled and observes `cuda graph: True` for the 47-token prefill batch.

issues.body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

On NPU (Neural Processing Unit) devices, enabling torch.compile for diffusion models causes severe performance degradation, resulting in 6x+ latency increase compared to non-compiled execution. This is due to NPU's current suboptimal support for torch.compile optimization passes.

To address this issue, this PR:

1. Skips torch.compile by default on NPU for diffusion models to avoid the performance regression
2. Adds an escape hatch environment variable SGLANG_FORCE_TORCH_COMPILE_NPU for users who still want to experiment with torch.compile on NPU despite the performance warning
3. Provides clear warning messages to inform users about the performance impact when torch.compile is requested on NPU
## Modifications

### 1. Environment Variable Addition (python/sglang/multimodal_gen/envs.py)
- Added SGLANG_FORCE_TORCH_COMPILE_NPU environment variable
- Default value: False (torch.compile is skipped on NPU by default)
- When set to 1 or true , users can force-enable torch.compile on NPU at their own risk
### 2. Torch Compile Logic Update (python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/pipelines/diffusers_pipeline.py)
- Modified _apply_torch_compile() method to detect NPU devices using is_npu()
- On NPU:
  - Logs a warning about the 6x+ latency increase
  - Skips torch.compile by default
  - Only applies torch.compile if SGLANG_FORCE_TORCH_COMPILE_NPU is explicitly set
- On other devices (CUDA, ROCm): torch.compile behavior remains unchanged
### 3. Import Updates
- Added import for envs from sglang.multimodal_gen
- Utilizes existing is_npu() utility from sglang.srt.utils

## Motivation

On Blackwell GPUs (SM120), when using --fp8-gemm-backend auto , DeepGEMM produces incorrect results if the checkpoint's scale format is not ue8m0 , causing accuracy degradation and CUDA crashes at high concurrency. This PR automatically falls back to the Triton backend when the checkpoint's scale format is not ue8m0 on Blackwell GPUs.

issues.title: fix(diffusion): fall back to SDPA on SM120 GPUs
issues.body:
## Summary
- Fall back to Torch SDPA backend on SM120 (Blackwell workstation/consumer) GPUs for diffusion models
- SM120 GPUs like RTX PRO 6000 are not supported by sgl-kernel's flash_attn

## Issue
Fixes #15342

## Root Cause
The code at line 249 checks `has_device_capability(80)` which returns True for SM120 (12.0 >= 8.0). However, sgl-kernel's flash_attn only supports SM90 (Hopper) and SM100 (Blackwell Ultra), not SM120.

This causes the error:
```
NotImplementedError: flash_attn at sgl-kernel is only supported on sm90 and above
```

The error message is misleading - it says "sm90 and above" but actually only SM90 and SM100 are supported.

## Fix
Add an explicit check for `is_sm120()` to fall back to Torch SDPA backend, similar to how PR #15766 fixed the same issue for TRT AllReduce Fusion in server_args.py.

## Test Plan
- On SM120 GPUs (RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell), diffusion models should now use SDPA backend instead of failing
- On SM90/SM100 GPUs, FlashAttention will still be used
